docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12 (the versions CI tests).
  • Java 11. Hail runs on the JVM and is built for Java 11; it warns on other versions.
  • Poetry 2.x for a development install. A plain pip install works too.

Hail (0.2.137 or later) and its bundled Spark are installed as ordinary Python dependencies. You do not need a Spark installation: on a laptop or a single node, Hail starts a local Spark session the first time a command needs it.

docs.title: Install with Poetry (recommended)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/bigbio/hvantk
cd hvantk
poetry install
eval "$(poetry env activate)"

poetry install uses the committed poetry.lock, so you get the dependency set that CI and the container image were built from.

docs.title: Install with pip
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/bigbio/hvantk
cd hvantk
pip install -e .

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
hvantk utils check-install

It checks for a proxy setting that would break Hail, starts Hail, builds a small synthetic MatrixTable and prints its schema. python -m hvantk works wherever the hvantk script is not on your PATH.

docs.title: Optional features (extras)
docs.text:
The base install covers dataset builds and most analyses. Plotting, machine learning and a few provider-specific dependencies are extras. Install the ones you need, or all of them:

poetry install --extras "ancestry psroc"     # or: poetry install --all-extras
pip install -e ".[ancestry,psroc]"
Extra Pulls in Needed for ancestry scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn hvantk ancestry-inference psroc scikit-learn, matplotlib, plotly hvantk psroc ml scikit-learn hvantk rerank hgc matplotlib, seaborn hvantk hgc QC plots and the HTML report enrichex matplotlib, seaborn hvantk enrichex plots and --generate-report viz matplotlib, seaborn, plotly hvantk qtlcascade plots and report; hvantk ptm report and --save-plots constraint tspex, matplotlib, seaborn, statsmodels hvantk ptm constraint and hvantk ptm test ptm cptac, sorted-nearest hvantk download cptac-phospho and cptac-expression expression scanpy hvantk expression summarize and markers cohort nothing: scipy is a base dependency; kept so hvantk[cohort] still installs interactive plotly nothing: no command imports plotly today duckdb duckdb nothing: no command imports duckdb today

Without the extra, most of these commands stop with a message that names the extra to install.

A few details for the expression extra:

  • hvantk expression describe and summarize-ucsc work on a base install.
  • hvantk ptm constraint --expression-source anndata --expression-metric mean also needs it. The default metric, median, does not.
  • It does not install on Intel macOS. scanpy depends on numba and llvmlite, and llvmlite ships no x86_64 macOS wheel from 0.47 on. It installs normally on Linux and Apple Silicon. On an Intel Mac, run the expression commands on Linux or the cluster; the rest of the toolkit is unaffected.

docs.title: Container image for clusters
docs.text: For Slurm clusters, hvantk ships an Apptainer definition (containers/hvantk.def) built from poetry.lock with Java 11. Running on HPC covers building it and running Hail jobs with it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Hail hangs or fails with JSONDecodeError. An HTTP proxy is intercepting Hail's localhost traffic. Unset HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY, or set NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1. hvantk utils check-install warns about this.
  • Java version warnings or JVM start-up errors. Point JAVA_HOME at a Java 11 JDK.
  • Out of memory in local mode. Give the Spark driver more memory before starting Python: export PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS="--driver-memory 8g pyspark-shell".
  • Exported VCF or TSV files contain comma decimals (AF=0,25). Hail formats numbers with the JVM's locale. Set export JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US".
  • Spark log lines and warnings on stderr (loopback hostname, native-hadoop library, illegal reflective access) are harmless.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This walk-through takes about ten minutes on a laptop. It builds two small public datasets, turns one of them into gene sets, tests a gene list for enrichment, and checks a source for upstream changes. You need a working installation and internet access. Hail starts a local Spark session the first time a command needs it, so expect Spark log lines on stderr.

docs.title: 1. Check the installation
docs.text:
hvantk utils check-install

It starts Hail, builds a small synthetic MatrixTable and prints its schema. If it fails, see Installation → Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 2. See what you can build
docs.text:
hvantk plugins list

Every data source is a plugin, and every dataset has an id of the form <provider>:<dataset>, such as hgnc:lookup or clinvar:variants. Data sources says how each one is acquired.

docs.title: 3. Build two datasets
docs.text:
hvantk reprocess hgnc:lookup --raw-dir data/hgnc --output data/hgnc.ht
hvantk reprocess clingen:gene-disease --raw-dir data/clingen --output data/clingen.ht

A second run into the same --raw-dir stops with FileExistsError when the raw file is already there. Add --skip-download to rebuild from it, or use a fresh --raw-dir.

Each command downloads the raw file into --raw-dir, builds a Hail table at --output, and writes a provenance record next to it (data/hgnc.ht.provenance.json):

{
  "plugin": "hgnc",
  "dataset": "hgnc:lookup",
  "plugin_version": "0.2.0",
  "source_fingerprint": "sha256:6f8c05…",
  "schema_id": "hgnc-lookup-v1",
  "build_timestamp": "2026-10-19T22:30:58+00:00",
  "builder_commit": "3af91c0…",
  "parents": [],
  "build_parameters": {}
}

Each build ends by probing the upstream source. drift: clean means the source still matches the fingerprint shipped with your hvantk release. drift: drifted means it has changed since (a new release or a larger file); the build still used the current file and succeeded. See Check a source for drift.

docs.title: 4. Turn ClinGen into gene sets
docs.text:
hvantk genesets clingen --ht data/clingen.ht --min-classification Definitive \
  -o results/clingen_sets.json

This writes one gene set per ClinGen expert panel, keeping Definitive gene-disease pairs only (56 sets in October 2026). The JSON also stores a background universe, by default the union of all sets in the file (2,101 genes here). Gene sets covers the other sources and the file format.

docs.title: 5. Test a gene list for enrichment
docs.text:
printf "MYH7
MYBPC3
TNNT2
TNNI3
TPM1
ACTC1
MYL2
MYL3
LMNA
SCN5A
" > my_genes.txt
hvantk enrichex overlap -g my_genes.txt -s results/clingen_sets.json -o results/overlap.tsv

overlap runs a two-sided Fisher's exact test per gene set against the file's background and corrects for multiple testing with Benjamini-Hochberg. The ten sarcomere and cardiac genes come out where you would expect:

gene_set_name                      n_overlap  p_value   p_adjusted  overlap_genes
Hereditary Cardiovascular Disease  5          1.9e-08   1.1e-06     MYBPC3,MYH7,MYL2,SCN5A,TPM1
Dilated Cardiomyopathy             4          1.3e-07   3.5e-06     LMNA,MYH7,SCN5A,TNNT2
Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy        3          4.3e-06   8.0e-05     ACTC1,MYL3,TNNI3

The TSV also carries the odds ratio and its confidence interval. EnrichEx explains the test and the case-control burden mode.

docs.title: 6. Check a source for drift later
docs.text:
hvantk drift hgnc:lookup

It prints clean, or drifted with a diff of the fingerprint, and exits 1 when the source has drifted, so a scheduled job can act on it.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
This page covers all annotation and expression data sources supported by hvantk: what they are, where to get them, and how to build datasets from the raw data. Sources are split into two categories: those with built-in downloaders (automated) and those that require manual download (too large, license-gated, or fragile URLs).

Every build on this page goes through the unified hvantk reprocess <plugin>:<dataset> entry point — see Building datasets for the orchestration pattern, lifecycle flags, and --plugin-arg KEY=VALUE conventions used below.

docs.title: Dataset summary
docs.text: Every dataset hvantk can build, grouped by how you get the raw data. Backend is the builder's output format (hail writes a Hail Table, .ht; anndata writes an AnnData, .h5ad; pandas writes a Parquet file, .parquet). Licence/terms notes are what the plugin's own catalog entry, its SKILL.md or THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md states; the last quotes the source of each licence it lists. "Not stated in plugin docs" means the terms are not documented in this repository, not that the data is unrestricted. Check the source's own terms before you redistribute anything you build.

docs.title: Built-in downloaders (16 datasets)
docs.text: Dataset Type Backend Licence / terms clinvar:variants AnnotationTable hail Public domain clingen:gene-disease AnnotationTable hail CC BY 4.0 gencc:submissions AnnotationTable hail not stated in plugin docs hgnc:lookup AnnotationTable hail CC0 gnomad-metrics:metrics AnnotationTable hail CC0 ucsc-cellbrowser:default ExpressionMatrix anndata varies per collection; not centrally stated expression-atlas:dataset ExpressionMatrix anndata varies per accession (CC BY 4.0 for several; see hvantk catalog show <accession>) ensembl-gene:structure AnnotationTable hail No restrictions (Ensembl data; third-party constraints may apply) uniprot-ptm:sites AnnotationTable hail not stated in plugin docs cptac:expression ExpressionMatrix anndata not stated in plugin docs (via the cptac PyPI package) cptac:phospho ExpressionMatrix anndata not stated in plugin docs (via the cptac PyPI package) peptideatlas:phospho AnnotationTable pandas not stated in plugin docs insider:interfaces AnnotationTable hail Not stated (checked 2026-10-13; see SKILL.md) gwas-catalog:associations AnnotationTable hail EBI Services Terms of Use (CC0 covers only the separate summary statistics) gevir:metrics AnnotationTable hail Academic use onek-genomes:samples AnnotationTable hail No restriction; acknowledgement required (downloads only through reprocess; there is no hvantk download command for it)

docs.title: Downloader or documented acquisition
docs.text:
A dataset's manifest declares one of three acquisition states — per dataset, not per provider, since a multi-dataset plugin can mix them (onek-genomes ships one BYO dataset and one auto-downloaded one):

  • lifecycle.download is declared — a real downloader exists; hvantk download <source> or hvantk reprocess <plugin>:<dataset> fetches the raw file.
  • acquisition: {mode: byo, reason: ...} is declared — acquisition cannot be automated, so it is documented instead (reason is one of size, credentialed, license, publication-only, unstable-url). The user supplies --raw-dir themselves; byo and lifecycle.download are mutually exclusive — a manifest cannot claim both that fetching is impossible and ship a function that fetches. reprocess skips the download stage automatically for a BYO dataset — passing --skip-download yourself is legal but not required.
  • Neither block is declared — automatable in principle, but no downloader has been written yet; hvantk reprocess needs --skip-download until one lands.

(An explicit acquisition.mode: download with no lifecycle.download is a schema error: it asserts a downloader exists without shipping one.)

The decision between the first two states: build a downloader when the raw file is under 1 GB, publicly accessible (no licence gate), high-value, and served from a stable, predictable URL. Document acquisition instead when the file is over 1 GB, needs licence acceptance or manual steps, or the URL structure is complex or fragile (FTP directory listings, versioned mirrors). The third state means a downloader could be written in principle but has not been yet; nothing on this page is currently in that state.

docs.title: File format note
docs.text:
Downloaded .gz files may be standard gzip (single-threaded in Hail) rather than BGZF (parallel). Pre-convert before building:

hvantk utils convert-bgz input.gz

docs.title: Sources with built-in downloaders
docs.text: Source Command Approx. Size ClinVar hvantk download clinvar ~500 MB ClinGen hvantk download clingen ~5 MB GenCC hvantk download gencc ~10 MB HGNC hvantk download hgnc ~20 MB gnomAD constraint hvantk download gnomad-metrics ~4.6 MB (v2.1.1) / ~82 MB (v4.0) UCSC Cell Browser hvantk download ucsc varies Expression Atlas hvantk download expression-atlas varies Ensembl gene annotations hvantk download ensembl-structure ~64 MB UniProt PTM sites hvantk download uniprot-ptm varies (REST API query) CPTAC protein expression hvantk download cptac-expression varies by cancer type CPTAC phosphoproteomics hvantk download cptac-phospho varies by cancer type PeptideAtlas phospho hvantk download peptideatlas-phospho ~549 MB INSIDER interfaces hvantk download insider-interfaces ~49 MB GWAS Catalog hvantk download gwas-catalog ~70 MB zip (~601 MB unzipped TSV) GeVIR gene metrics hvantk download gevir ~10.3 MB xlsx (~0.6 MB derived TSV) 1000 Genomes sample panel (no standalone command; see 1000 Genomes) ~55 KB

docs.title: ClinVar
docs.text:
Clinically relevant variants and their annotations (e.g. Pathogenic, Benign, VUS). URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/vcf_GRCh38/

# Download latest ClinVar VCF (GRCh38) with tabix index
hvantk download clinvar --output-dir data/clinvar

# Download a specific archived version
hvantk download clinvar --version 20260101 --output-dir data/clinvar

# Download GRCh37 build, verify checksum
hvantk download clinvar --genome-build GRCh37 --verify-md5

Build:

# Download + build in one step
hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants \
  --raw-dir data/clinvar/ \
  --output clinvar.ht

# From a VCF already in --raw-dir
hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants \
  --raw-dir data/clinvar/ \
  --output clinvar.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg reference_genome=GRCh38

docs.title: ClinGen
docs.text:
# Download today's ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity snapshot
# Output: Clingen-Gene-Disease-Summary-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv
hvantk download clingen --output-dir data/clingen

# Check download availability
hvantk download clingen --list-versions

Build:

hvantk reprocess clingen:gene-disease \
  --raw-dir data/clingen/ \
  --output clingen.ht \
  --plugin-arg min_classification=Strong

docs.title: GenCC
docs.text:
GenCC (Gene Curation Coalition) aggregates gene-disease validity assertions from 12+ submitting organizations (ClinGen, PanelApp, G2P, Orphanet, etc.).

# Download today's GenCC submissions snapshot
hvantk download gencc --output-dir data/gencc

# Check download availability
hvantk download gencc --list-versions

Build:

hvantk reprocess gencc:submissions \
  --raw-dir data/gencc/ \
  --output gencc.ht \
  --plugin-arg min_classification=Strong

docs.title: HGNC
docs.text:
# Download HGNC complete gene nomenclature set
hvantk download hgnc --output data/hgnc/hgnc_complete_set.txt

Build Hail Table:

# Single command: download into data/hgnc/ then build the table
hvantk reprocess hgnc:lookup \
  --raw-dir data/hgnc/ \
  --output hgnc.ht

# Or, if you already downloaded the TSV into data/hgnc/:
hvantk reprocess hgnc:lookup \
  --raw-dir data/hgnc/ \
  --output hgnc.ht \
  --skip-download

docs.title: UCSC Cell Browser
docs.text:
The UCSC Cell Browser catalog lists 267 datasets. About half are collections (groups of related datasets with no expression matrix at the top level). Use --list-datasets and --search to discover downloadable datasets.

# Discover available datasets
hvantk download ucsc --list-datasets

# Search by name, organism, or tissue (expands collections to show children)
hvantk download ucsc --list-datasets --search heart
hvantk download ucsc --list-datasets --search pancreas

# Download a leaf dataset directly
hvantk download ucsc --dataset adultPancreas --output-dir data/ucsc

# Download a child dataset from a collection (use the full path)
hvantk download ucsc --dataset hoc/all-heart --output-dir data/ucsc

Note: Collection names (e.g., hoc) cannot be downloaded directly — they contain no expression matrix. Use --search to find child dataset paths like hoc/all-heart, then download those.

Build (ucsc-cellbrowser:default, one named collection per build):

# Download + build in one step (dataset forwards to the download stage)
hvantk reprocess ucsc-cellbrowser:default \
  --raw-dir data/ucsc/adultPancreas \
  --output adult_pancreas.h5ad \
  --plugin-arg dataset=adultPancreas

# From files already downloaded with `hvantk download ucsc` above
hvantk reprocess ucsc-cellbrowser:default \
  --raw-dir data/ucsc/adultPancreas \
  --output adult_pancreas.h5ad \
  --skip-download

adult-ctx and dev-ctx are per-class summaries of the adult-ctx-meta-atlas and dev-ctx-meta-atlas parent collections, not their own UCSC collections, so neither declares lifecycle.download (acquisition.mode: byo, reason size — the parent's raw per-cell matrix is multi-GB). Each needs an expression_matrix.tsv (a gene column plus one column per class) and a metadata.tsv (one row per class, with n_cells) in --raw-dir; hvantk expression summarize-ucsc builds that summary as an .h5ad from the parent collection, so exporting it back to this TSV pair takes a manual step:

hvantk reprocess ucsc-cellbrowser:adult-ctx \
  --raw-dir data/ucsc/adult_ctx/ \
  --output adult_ctx_summary.h5ad \
  --skip-download

hvantk reprocess ucsc-cellbrowser:dev-ctx \
  --raw-dir data/ucsc/dev_ctx/ \
  --output dev_ctx_summary.h5ad \
  --skip-download

docs.title: Expression Atlas
docs.text:
# Download one accession's bulk RNA-seq experiment
hvantk download expression-atlas --accession E-MTAB-6798 --download-path data/expression_atlas

# Download + build in one call (reprocess forwards --plugin-arg accession=... to the
# download stage; the build stage ignores it and locates the two input files within
# --raw-dir)
hvantk reprocess expression-atlas:dataset --raw-dir data/expression_atlas \
  --output E-MTAB-6798.h5ad --plugin-arg accession=E-MTAB-6798

reprocess scopes the expression matrix to the accession named by the raw dir's SDRF file and raises if no TPM file matches it (an older raw dir's leftover file, or two downloads merged by hand, must not silently combine mismatched expression + metadata). The unfiltered download above fetches every file in the experiment's FTP directory, so the gene-level and the transcript-level TPM file can both be present. reprocess builds from the one whose columns are the SDRF's runs, or from the gene-level one when both qualify. For E-MTAB-6798 that is the transcript-level file (var keyed by the transcript id): its gene-level file has one column per assay group (g1 … g94), not per run. It raises when no file has the runs as columns.

A transcript-level build needs --plugin-arg level=gene to sum its values per gene and key var by the gene id instead — before the result can be used with hvantk expression markers/summarize or the PTM constraint expression loader, which read var_names as the gene id and refuse a transcript-keyed matrix. A gene-level build already works there without it. hvantk annotate prepare's matrix source type refuses a transcript-keyed matrix too, but needs more than level=gene either way: it resolves var_names as HGNC gene symbols, not Ensembl gene ids, so an Expression Atlas build (gene- or transcript-level) needs a symbol-keyed summary before it is usable there.

docs.title: Manual download sources
docs.text: Most of these sources need manual acquisition — too large, license-gated, or a fragile URL — and for those, follow the instructions below, place the raw file(s) in a per-source directory, then build via hvantk reprocess <plugin>:<dataset> (a BYO dataset skips the download stage automatically; --skip-download is legal but not required). Some members of this section ship a downloader instead (GeVIR, gnomAD constraint, Ensembl gene annotations, UniProt PTM sites, CPTAC phospho and expression, PeptideAtlas phospho, INSIDER interfaces, the GWAS Catalog and the 1000 Genomes sample metadata); they are grouped here because they carry a license, size, versioning or build-path caveat worth reading before relying on them.

docs.title: dbNSFP (~50 GB)
docs.text:
A database of functional prediction scores for human missense variants. URL: https://www.dbnsfp.org/

Download: Academic access is a two-step form process: (1) register with an institutional email through a Google Form and receive an access code once the domain is verified; (2) request the download links with that same email and code through a second form. The academic release is distributed under the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence, as a ~50 GB ZIP of per-chromosome variant tables plus the gene table and the search_dbNSFP program; it is also searchable online through an "Academic Portal". Commercial licensing goes through the maintainers. Start at the releases page, https://www.dbnsfp.org/releases/, or the download page, https://www.dbnsfp.org/download/. (Verified 2026-09-28: the legacy landing page, https://sites.google.com/site/jpopgen/dbNSFP, is frozen at v4.9 (2024-08-08) and now tells readers to access the current dbNSFP at dbNSFP.org; its S3 and Box archive links are dead.)

Pre-processing: dbNSFP is distributed as per-chromosome .gz files (standard gzip, not BGZF). The builder expects a single combined file, so concatenate and BGZF-compress first:

# Concatenate per-chromosome files into a single BGZF file
# (header is taken from chr1; remaining files skip the header line)
head -1 <(zcat dbNSFP<version>_variant.chr1.gz) > /tmp/dbnsfp_header.txt
(cat /tmp/dbnsfp_header.txt && for f in dbNSFP<version>_variant.chr*.gz; do zcat "$f" | tail -n +2; done) \
  | bgzip -@ 4 > dbnsfp_variant.bgz

Build:

# Place the concatenated BGZF file in data/dbnsfp/ (so the builder sees it), then
# build. dbNSFP declares acquisition.mode=byo (no plugin downloader exists), so
# reprocess skips the download stage automatically.
hvantk reprocess dbnsfp:variants \
  --raw-dir data/dbnsfp/ \
  --output dbnsfp.ht

Note: dbNSFP's builder reads BGZF input. If you only have a single combined .gz, pre-convert with hvantk utils convert-bgz dbNSFP<version>_variant.gz before building.

docs.title: gnomAD constraint metrics
docs.text:
Per-gene constraint metrics (pLI, oe_lof / LOEUF, missense Z) from gnomAD. The tables are small and public, so hvantk ships a downloader (hvantk download gnomad-metrics; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above).

  • v2.1.1 (GRCh37, ~4.6 MB) — the default and the table hvantk standardises on (keyed by gene_id).
  • v4.0 (GRCh38, ~82 MB) — newer; per-transcript rows, dotted column names, and no gene_id column, so build with --plugin-arg key=transcript. gnomAD did not re-release constraint for v4.1.

Download + build (end-to-end, defaults to v2.1.1 by-gene):

hvantk reprocess gnomad-metrics:metrics \
  --raw-dir data/gnomad_metrics/ \
  --output gnomad_metrics.ht

# v4.0 (GRCh38) instead, in its own --raw-dir: the builder reads the one
# constraint file it finds there and stops if it finds two.
hvantk download gnomad-metrics --version v4.0 \
  --output data/gnomad_metrics_v4/gnomad.v4.0.constraint_metrics.tsv
hvantk reprocess gnomad-metrics:metrics --skip-download \
  --raw-dir data/gnomad_metrics_v4/ --output gnomad_metrics_v4.ht \
  --plugin-arg key=transcript

docs.title: INSIDER interactome (~1.2 GB genomic BED; ~49 MB pair table)
docs.text:
Protein-protein interaction interface residues from the INSIDER database. URL: http://interactomeinsider.yulab.org/downloads.html

INSIDER ships two products, and hvantk builds a dataset from each:

dataset file size direct URL insider:variants Whole_Human_Interactome_Interface_hg38.bed ~1.17 GB http://interactomeinsider.yulab.org/bed/all.bed insider:interfaces H_sapiens_interfacesALL.txt ~49 MB http://interactomeinsider.yulab.org/downloads/interfacesALL/H_sapiens_interfacesALL.txt

Download: the downloads page carries no links in its markup, so both the plugin catalog (hvantk catalog show INSIDER_v1.0) and the insider:interfaces downloader use the direct URLs above. Both files are served over plain HTTP; the site has no HTTPS listener. The BED is >1 GB, so insider:variants stays manual acquisition; the pair table is small enough that insider:interfaces ships a real downloader instead:

hvantk download insider-interfaces --output data/insider/H_sapiens_interfacesALL.txt

Build:

# Place Whole_Human_Interactome_Interface_hg38.bed in data/insider/ then:
hvantk reprocess insider:variants \
  --raw-dir data/insider/ \
  --output interactome.ht \
  --skip-download

INSIDER also ships a gene-level dataset, insider:interfaces, built from H_sapiens_interfacesALL.txt (~49 MB) rather than the BED file. Where insider:variants is locus-keyed (interaction sites as genomic intervals), insider:interfaces is keyed by uniprot_id and summarises each protein's interactome: n_partners, n_partners_experimental, n_partners_predicted and n_interface_residues. The two are complementary, not alternatives — use interfaces when the question is "how connected is this gene", and variants when it is "does this variant fall in an interaction site". Unlike insider:variants, this file is well under 1 GB, so it declares lifecycle.download and reprocess fetches it automatically — no --skip-download needed:

hvantk reprocess insider:interfaces \
  --raw-dir data/insider/ \
  --output insider_interfaces.ht

docs.title: Ensembl gene annotations (~64 MB GTF)
docs.text:
The canonical per-gene table (ensembl-gene:structure): gene ID, gene name, biotype, coordinates, CDS length, coding-exon count, transcript count, and MANE Select — parsed from the pinned-release Ensembl GTF. The release is pinned in hvantk/resources/ensembl_release.py; the same pin governs the PTM coordinate mapper. The file is small and public, so hvantk ships a downloader (hvantk download ensembl-structure; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above) that fetches exactly that pinned release rather than whatever the FTP's "current" alias points at.

Download + build (end-to-end, fetches the pinned release automatically):

hvantk reprocess ensembl-gene:structure \
  --raw-dir data/ensembl/ \
  --output ensembl_structure.ht

Manual download: the same release-pinned GTF from the Ensembl FTP (https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/), placed in data/ensembl/, then built with --skip-download:

hvantk reprocess ensembl-gene:structure \
  --raw-dir data/ensembl/ \
  --output ensembl_structure.ht \
  --skip-download

docs.title: GeVIR (~10 MB workbook)
docs.text:
Gene-level intolerance-to-variation ranks (GeVIR and VIRLoF percentiles) for 19,361 protein-coding genes, keyed by Ensembl gene_id. Not a variant-level pathogenicity score. Abramovs, Brass & Tassabehji, 2020, Nature Genetics 52(1):35-39 (PMID 31873297, DOI 10.1038/s41588-019-0560-2). URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-019-0560-2

Download: the metric table is Supplementary Table 2 of the Nature Genetics paper, served as the article's MOESM3 object:

https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-019-0560-2/MediaObjects/41588_2019_560_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx

That is a ~10.3 MB .xlsx workbook (only MOESM3 of the six supplementary slots is public; the rest return 403), not a thin URL fetch: the builder reads a bgzipped TSV, so the downloader (hvantk download gevir; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above) extracts sheet table_2 itself (stdlib zipfile + xml.etree, no openpyxl dependency) and BGZF-compresses it, including restoring the ~29 gene symbols Excel's autocorrect silently turned into dates (e.g. MARCH6, SEPT11; see hvantk/skills/gevir/cli.py's module docstring for the full, externally-verified restoration rule).

Note: the authors' repository at https://github.com/gevirank/gevir ships the analysis code only — its tables/ directory holds a placeholder file — so it is not a source for the metric table. Earlier revisions of this guide pointed there.

Download + build (end-to-end, fetches and derives the TSV automatically):

hvantk reprocess gevir:metrics \
  --raw-dir data/gevir/ \
  --output gevir.ht

Manual download: an already-derived gevir_metrics_pmid31873297.tsv.bgz placed in data/gevir/, then built with --skip-download:

hvantk reprocess gevir:metrics \
  --raw-dir data/gevir/ \
  --output gevir.ht \
  --skip-download

docs.title: GWAS Catalog (~69.5 MB zip, ~601 MB unzipped)
docs.text:
The NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog full-associations TSV — SNP-trait associations with study provenance, p-value, effect size, and risk-allele frequency, built into a Hail Table keyed by (locus, alleles) with a sentinel ALT. v1.0 schema (34 columns). URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/

A periodic full dump, zipped, from EBI's FTP, released every 1-3 weeks. The zip is small and public, so hvantk ships a downloader (hvantk download gwas-catalog; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above) that fetches the current release from the FTP releases/latest/ alias and extracts the associations TSV it contains.

Download + build (end-to-end, fetches the current release automatically):

hvantk reprocess gwas-catalog:associations \
  --raw-dir data/gwas_catalog/ \
  --output gwas_catalog.ht

Manual download:

https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/releases/latest/gwas-catalog-associations-full.zip

Unzip to get gwas-catalog-download-associations-v1.0-full.tsv (verified live 2026-09-30: zip 69,506,531 bytes, TSV 600,996,055 bytes), place it in data/gwas_catalog/, then build with --skip-download:

hvantk reprocess gwas-catalog:associations \
  --raw-dir data/gwas_catalog/ \
  --output gwas_catalog.ht \
  --skip-download

docs.title: COSMIC Cancer Gene Census
docs.text:
Gene-level cancer annotations from the COSMIC Cancer Gene Census. URL: https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/census

Download: Requires COSMIC account. Download the Cancer Gene Census TSV from the COSMIC website.

Build:

# Place the downloaded export (e.g. cancer_gene_census.tsv.gz) in data/cosmic_cgc/ then:
hvantk reprocess cosmic-cgc:submissions \
  --raw-dir data/cosmic_cgc/ \
  --skip-download \
  --output cosmic_cgc.ht

docs.title: AlphaGenome variant-effect scores
docs.text:
Per-variant scores from Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome model (alphagenome:predictions) for expression, splicing, chromatin and contact-map tracks. hvantk does not call AlphaGenome: it ingests scores you have already produced with the AlphaGenome SDK, through the API or local weights, and summarises them into one row per variant. SDK: https://pypi.org/project/alphagenome/ (documentation: https://www.alphagenomedocs.com).

Licence: AlphaGenome outputs fall under the AlphaGenome Output Terms of Use: non-commercial use only, not for training machine-learning models, and any copy keeps a conspicuous notice (see hvantk/skills/alphagenome/tests/testdata/raw/alphagenome/NOTICE.md).

Produce the input: score each variant with score_variant(...), convert the result with variant_scorers.tidy_scores(...), cast variant_id and scored_interval to strings, and write the DataFrame with to_parquet(). hvantk/skills/alphagenome/SKILL.md §2 has the snippet. Put only these parquet files in one directory; every *.parquet file in it is read.

Build:

# Place the tidy_scores parquet files in data/alphagenome/ then:
hvantk reprocess alphagenome:predictions \
  --raw-dir data/alphagenome/ \
  --output alphagenome.ht

Note: the table is keyed by (locus, alleles) and carries one struct per AlphaGenome scorer (the 19 of the SDK's recommended set): the track with the largest absolute quantile score, the largest absolute raw score and the number of rows. --plugin-arg output_types=... and --plugin-arg ontology_curies=... filter rows before they are summarised. A scorer the plugin does not know, or a parquet file without the tidy-scores columns, stops the build with an error. --skip-download is not needed: the dataset declares acquisition.mode: byo.

docs.title: MSigDB gene sets
docs.text:
Molecular Signatures Database gene sets (msigdb:genesets), built from a collection's GMT file (e.g. C2 canonical pathways). The format is the same across collections, so the builder works for any MSigDB GMT. URL: https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/human/collections.jsp

Download: requires a free account and a login + license click-through, so no downloader is shipped. Download and unzip the collection's GMT.

Build:

# Place the unzipped .gmt in data/msigdb/ then:
hvantk reprocess msigdb:genesets \
  --raw-dir data/msigdb/ \
  --output msigdb.ht \
  --skip-download

docs.title: UniProt PTM Sites
docs.text:
Curated post-translational modification sites for reviewed human proteins from UniProt/Swiss-Prot. The downloader queries only UniProt's ft_mod_res ("Modified residue") feature — phosphorylation, acetylation, methylation, hydroxylation and similar single-residue marks. It does not cover modifications UniProt annotates under a different feature type: no ubiquitination, SUMOylation or NEDDylation (CROSSLNK) and no glycosylation (CARBOHYD). URL: https://www.uniprot.org/

This is a live REST query rather than a large or license-gated file, so hvantk ships a downloader (hvantk download uniprot-ptm; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above). The uniprot-ptm:sites table is built from genome-mapped sites, not from the raw UniProt download, and hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites runs every step: it downloads the raw TSV, fetches the pinned Ensembl GTF into the same --raw-dir (kept there, so later runs reuse it), maps the sites against it, and builds the Hail Table. hvantk ptm build runs the same mapping and can add PeptideAtlas and CPTAC phosphosites to the table.

Build:

# Download, map and build (UniProt sites)
hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites \
  --raw-dir data/ptm/ \
  --output data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht

# From files already in --raw-dir (a UniProt TSV and, optionally, the GTF)
hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites \
  --skip-download \
  --raw-dir data/ptm/ \
  --output data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht

# Multi-source build, with pre-downloaded files
hvantk ptm build \
  --gtf-path data/ref/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz \
  --ptm-tsv data/ptm/uniprot-ptm-human-<YYYY-MM-DD>.tsv \
  --output-dir data/ptm/ \
  --output-ht data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht

With --skip-download, the newest uniprot-ptm-human-<YYYY-MM-DD>.tsv in --raw-dir is mapped (hvantk download uniprot-ptm --output-dir data/ptm/ writes one), and the GTF is downloaded only if Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz is not already there. The mapping uses GRCh38 coordinates, so --plugin-arg reference_genome accepts only GRCh38.

docs.title: Ensembl GTF (~64 MB compressed)
docs.text:
The same pinned-release GTF as ensembl-gene:structure above, used by the PTM mapper for residue-to-genomic coordinate mapping (exon coordinates and CDS phases). URL: https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/gtf/homo_sapiens/

Download: Auto-downloaded by hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites (into its --raw-dir) and by hvantk ptm build. For manual download:

wget https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/gtf/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz

docs.title: CPTAC proteomics
docs.text:
Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) tumor proteomics, accessed via the cptac Python package (not direct HTTP) rather than a single downloadable file. URL: https://proteomics.cancer.gov/programs/cptac

cptac:phospho (phosphoproteomics, one AnnData per cancer type) ships a downloader (hvantk download cptac-phospho; it is also in the built-in-downloader list above):

hvantk reprocess cptac:phospho \
  --raw-dir data/cptac/ \
  --output cptac_phospho_brca.h5ad \
  --plugin-arg cancer_type=brca

cptac:expression (whole-proteome protein expression, also one AnnData per cancer type) ships the same shape of downloader (hvantk download cptac-expression; also in the built-in-downloader list above):

hvantk reprocess cptac:expression \
  --raw-dir data/cptac/ \
  --output cptac_expression_brca.h5ad \
  --plugin-arg cancer_type=brca

The cancer_type plugin-arg flows to both the download (fetch only that cancer) and the build (select its matrix+metadata pair). --all on hvantk download cptac-expression fetches every cancer type but does not merge them -- unlike cptac:phospho's pan-cancer TSV merge, each cancer type's expression matrix keeps its own gene set and sample columns. A long-format TSV/CSV staged by hand still works too, via the {"expression","metadata"} mapping form of parsed_input -- see hvantk/skills/cptac/expression/SKILL.md §6-7 for the full workflow.

docs.title: PeptideAtlas phospho sites
docs.text:
Human phosphorylation sites from PeptideAtlas (peptideatlas:phospho), built from the PeptideAtlas relational TSV dump. URL: https://peptideatlas.org/

hvantk reprocess peptideatlas:phospho \
  --raw-dir data/peptideatlas/ \
  --output peptideatlas_phospho.parquet

The upstream zip (e.g. atlas_build_606.tsv.zip) is ~549 MB. hvantk download peptideatlas-phospho (also in the built-in-downloader list above) fetches it, and the plugin's own lifecycle.parse stage extracts the intermediate TSV automatically — no --skip-parse or --intermediate needed.

docs.title: 1000 Genomes (NYGC/CCDG high-coverage callset)
docs.text:
Per-chromosome high-coverage VCFs (NYGC/CCDG) plus IGSR sample metadata (population, super-population, sex).

onek-genomes:variants (the VCFs) is byo (reason: size — multi-GB per chromosome), so no downloader is shipped. Mirror: https://ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/ftp/data_collections/1000G_2504_high_coverage/working/20201028_3202_phased/

# Place per-chromosome *_chr<N>.filtered.shapeit2-duohmm-phased.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) in
# data/onek_genomes/. chrX is phased separately and ships as
# *_chrX.filtered.eagle2-phased.v2.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) -- place that too, then:
hvantk reprocess onek-genomes:variants \
  --raw-dir data/onek_genomes/ \
  --output onek_genomes_variants.mt \
  --skip-download

onek-genomes:samples (the IGSR sample panel, ~55 KB) declares a lifecycle.download, but the plugin has no cli.py and no cli: block, so no standalone hvantk download command exists for it — the download only runs as part of reprocess:

hvantk reprocess onek-genomes:samples \
  --raw-dir data/onek_genomes/ \
  --output onek_genomes_samples.ht

docs.title: QTL data
docs.text: These datasets are used to build eQTL and pQTL Hail Tables for the QTL cascade pipeline.

docs.title: GTEx eQTL data
docs.text:
Expression quantitative trait loci from the GTEx project. Available as significant pairs (genome-wide significant associations) and allpairs (full summary statistics for coloc).

GTEx v11 (recommended): URL: https://www.gtexportal.org/home/downloads/adult-gtex/qtl

# Download significant pairs (Parquet format, ~50 MB per tissue)
# Navigate to GTEx Portal → Downloads → Adult GTEx → QTL → eQTL → Significant pairs.
# Place per-tissue files under /data/gtex_v11/signif_pairs/ then:

# Build significant-pairs table
hvantk reprocess gtex-eqtl:eqtls \
  --raw-dir /data/gtex_v11/signif_pairs/ \
  --output eqtl_liver.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=gtex_v11 \
  --plugin-arg tissue=Liver

# Build allpairs table for coloc (set p-threshold to 0)
hvantk reprocess gtex-eqtl:eqtls \
  --raw-dir /data/gtex_v11/allpairs/Liver/ \
  --output eqtl_allpairs_liver.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=gtex_v11 \
  --plugin-arg tissue=Liver \
  --plugin-arg p_threshold=0

GTEx v8 (TSV format):

# Place Liver.v8.signif_variant_gene_pairs.txt.gz under /data/gtex_v8/ then:
hvantk reprocess gtex-eqtl:eqtls \
  --raw-dir /data/gtex_v8/ \
  --output eqtl_liver_v8.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=gtex_v8

eQTLGen (blood eQTLs): URL: https://www.eqtlgen.org/cis-eqtls.html

Caveat: eQTLGen distributes a Z-score, not a beta/SE, and no allele frequency — beta, se, af and maf all come back null, so this source cannot feed colocalisation and only supports p-value-based overlap. Its coordinates are GRCh37 (b37); pass --plugin-arg reference_genome=GRCh37 to match them, or the contig format and the build label in the constructed variant ID disagree.

# Place cis-eQTLs_full.txt.gz under /data/eqtlgen/ then:
hvantk reprocess gtex-eqtl:eqtls \
  --raw-dir /data/eqtlgen/ \
  --output eqtl_blood.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=eqtlgen \
  --plugin-arg reference_genome=GRCh37

docs.title: Fang et al. (2025) pQTL data
docs.text:
Protein quantitative trait loci from Fang et al. (2025), covering 5 tissues (Colon, Heart, Liver, Lung, Thyroid). Space-delimited allpairs format with columns: gene_name SNP CHR BP A1 NMISS BETA STAT P. SE is derived as |BETA/STAT| (rows with STAT = 0 are filtered out).

No direct data URL: the allpairs files are supplementary material to a preprint, not a published dataset. Source: Fang et al. (2025), "Regulation of protein abundance in normal human tissues", medRxiv, doi:10.1101/2025.01.10.25320181.

Note: Fang pQTL data uses gene symbols. For symbol → Ensembl ID mapping, pass the HGNC lookup table built by hvantk reprocess hgnc:lookup via --plugin-arg hgnc_ht=<path>. Symbols that are not approved HGNC symbols are resolved through previous symbols, then aliases, when exactly one gene lists them; the build fails if no symbol maps.

# Build pQTL table with gene mapping
# Place Liver.allpairs_nobsGE72.txt.gz under /data/fang_pqtl/ then (the tissue name
# is inferred from the filename prefix before the first dot, so this exact naming
# matters -- see hvantk/core/utils/qtl_helpers.py):
hvantk reprocess pqtl:metrics \
  --raw-dir /data/fang_pqtl/ \
  --output pqtl_liver.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=gtex_fang \
  --plugin-arg tissue=Liver \
  --plugin-arg hgnc_ht=hgnc.ht \
  --plugin-arg p_threshold=5e-8

# Allpairs for coloc (omit p_threshold to keep all variants)
hvantk reprocess pqtl:metrics \
  --raw-dir /data/fang_pqtl/ \
  --output pqtl_allpairs_liver.ht \
  --skip-download \
  --plugin-arg source=gtex_fang \
  --plugin-arg tissue=Liver \
  --plugin-arg hgnc_ht=hgnc.ht

docs.title: Expression data sources
docs.text: These datasets are used to build expression MatrixTables via the UCSC Cell Browser and Expression Atlas downloaders.

docs.title: Bulk RNA-seq
docs.text: • Human tissue expression E-MTAB-6814 — Human tissue gene expression (brain, heart, liver, kidney), multiple developmental time points. URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-6814

docs.title: Single-cell RNA-seq
docs.text:
• Human heart scRNA-seq (Asp 2019) — Embryonic human heart single-cell RNA-seq data 6.5 wpc (PMID:31835037). URL: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/mbvhhf8m62/2
  • Human heart scRNA-seq (Farah 2024) — Single-cell RNA-seq data of the developing human heart, 9-15 wpc. URL: https://cells.ucsc.edu/?bp=heart&ds=hoc
  • Human heart cell atlas (HCA) — Adult human heart cell atlas (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2797-4). URL: https://cells.ucsc.edu/?bp=heart&ds=heart-cell-atlas

docs.title: Running on HPC
docs.text:
This guide describes how to run the hvantk toolkit, its environment, and its data on a shared HPC cluster, so that dataset builds, pipelines, and experiments run at scale.

It is written for a cluster with:

  • a Slurm scheduler (with a supported Spark-on-Slurm launcher),
  • Apptainer/Singularity available for containers,
  • outbound internet on compute nodes (if your compute nodes are firewalled, see the staging notes in §6 below),
  • a standard three-tier filesystem (small backed-up home, large project/work, fast purged scratch).

Adjust the partition names, paths, and Spark-on-Slurm launcher to your site.

docs.title: 0. TL;DR — the recommended path
docs.text:
1. Code → git clone the repo on the cluster. The gitignored local/ data tree moves separately (step 4).
  2. Environment → ship one Apptainer image (hvantk.sif) built from the repo's poetry.lock, pinning Java 11 + Hail 0.2.137 + pyspark 3.5.8 + all native libraries. This is the most important decision: it eliminates the native-library portability class of failure (e.g. an RPATH/libz break in a compiled wheel like pysam/pyBigWig).
  3. Hail → default to Spark local mode on one exclusive fat node; escalate to the cluster's Spark-on-Slurm multi-node launcher (via HVANTK_SKIP_HAIL_INIT) only when the working set exceeds a fat node's RAM.
  4. Data → move the data that must be transferred via Globus (through a Data Transfer Node), re-fetch the public bulk downloads on the login node, regenerate the derived Hail .mts on-cluster, and skip redundant/raw files.
  5. Streaming experiments → where compute nodes have internet, code that streams from VEP / GCS / UCSC / eQTL sources runs as-is. Still stage the big/repeated pulls (gnomAD, the ~9 GB phyloP bigWig) to project storage for speed and to respect rate limits.
  6. Validate every new node with hvantk utils check-install before running pipelines.

If this cluster already has the hvantk agent skills set up, use them instead of the manual commands in this guide: hpc-container builds and promotes the image, hpc-hail-job sizes and submits a Hail-backed command as a job, and hpc-sync keeps a cluster clone in step with GitHub (see Workflow skills). They read a per-cluster site profile and record provenance automatically. This guide explains the mechanism underneath them, and is still the reference for a manual run, debugging a failure, or a cluster without the skills set up yet.

docs.title: 1. What lives where
docs.text:
Layer What Mechanism Notes Code hvantk/, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, tests/ git clone tracked; tiny Environment Python 3.10 + Hail/JVM + native libs Apptainer .sif built from poetry.lock; §3 Data gitignored local/ tree Globus / refetch / regenerate §5 split Secrets/access EGA gvcfs, UKB-PPP, other gated sources manual copy §5

Why a container and not conda or poetry install on the node. A conda env or a node-level poetry install still links against the host's system libraries (libz, libbz2, libcurl, libhdf5, glibc). A mismatch there is the canonical cause of dlopen/RPATH failures in compiled wheels. A .sif carries its own copies of those libraries, so the dynamic loader resolves against them regardless of the node. A container is also one file (vs. a conda env's ~100k files, which exhausts inode quotas and stresses the shared filesystem). hvantk's stack is unusually native-lib-heavy — Hail's JVM/Spark, pysam (htslib), pyarrow (Arrow C++), h5py (HDF5), scipy/scikit-learn (BLAS/LAPACK), duckdb — so the container payoff is large.

docs.title: 1.1 Keeping the cluster's clone current
docs.text:
The cluster has its own bare repo, and the working repo pushes to it via a second remote called hpc. Local branches track origin (GitHub), so a bare git push does not update the cluster:

Remote URL Role origin git@github.com:bigbio/hvantk.git GitHub; PRs and CI hpc hpc:/user/<user>/git/pyvatk.git bare repo on the cluster; the node-side clone pulls from here

After anything lands on main or dev, push GitHub's refs by explicit refspec, never local branch names — git push hpc main dev pushes your local branches, which can be behind while git still reports success, because sending an already-present commit is a legitimate no-op:

git fetch hpc
for b in main dev; do
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "hpc/$b" "origin/$b" && echo "$b: fast-forward, safe"
done

for b in main dev; do git push hpc "origin/$b:refs/heads/$b"; done

Do not trust the push's own output; fetch and diff the refs again afterwards — every line must show the same hash on both sides:

git fetch hpc
for b in main dev; do
  printf '%-5s origin=%s hpc=%s\n' "$b" \
    "$(git rev-parse --short "origin/$b")" "$(git rev-parse --short "hpc/$b")"
done

This matters more than ordinary repo hygiene, because the .sif is built from poetry.lock (§3.2). A stale cluster clone rebuilds the previous dependency set without any error — the build succeeds, it is just the wrong environment. Rebuild the image whenever poetry.lock changes, not only when hvantk/ does. The hpc-sync agent skill automates this whole compare-push-verify sequence.

docs.title: 2. Cluster facts to confirm on first login
docs.text:
Run on the login node to fill in the exact paths/flags used below:

sinfo -o "%P %l %c %m %G"          # partitions: time limit, cores, mem, gres (lscratch?)
module avail 2>&1 | grep -iE "java|apptainer|singularity|spark|globus"
echo $HOME; df -h $HOME            # home quota (code only)
# project/work + scratch paths & quotas are site-specific (check docs / `quota`)
which apptainer || which singularity
apptainer build --fakeroot --help 2>&1 | head -1   # is --fakeroot allowed?
java -version                      # default Java — MUST be 11 for Hail

Note the scratch path (often /scratch/$USER or /lscratch/$SLURM_JOB_ID), whether --fakeroot is permitted (if not, build the image elsewhere and copy it), and the Spark-on-Slurm launcher's name/usage.

docs.title: 3.1 Critical version pins (do not drift)
docs.text:
The repo's poetry.lock encodes a tested triad: Hail 0.2.137 + pyspark 3.5.8 + py4j 0.10.9.9 + numpy 2.2.5 (with the np.bool = np.bool_ shim in hvantk/core/utils/hail_context.py that Hail 0.2.x needs under NumPy 2). Build from the lock; do not regenerate or loosen it. And:

Java 11, not 17. Hail 0.2.137 is built and tested with Java 11 only and warns on any other version. HPC module load java frequently defaults to 17/21, which breaks Hail. Bake Java 11 into the container so the host's Java module is irrelevant.

docs.title: 3.2 hvantk.def (build from the locked environment)
docs.text:
The definition file lives in the repo at containers/hvantk.def — build from that file rather than copying a snippet, so the base image and extras cannot drift from what was last built and validated. It installs the exact locked dependency set, not an unpinned pip install hail.

Two choices in it are load-bearing and must not be "modernised" without re-validating:

  • Base image is ubuntu:22.04 (jammy). Hail 0.2.137 / Spark 3.5 run on Java 8 or 11 only, which rules out a base whose own package repo has moved past both: Debian 12 (bookworm) ships no openjdk-11 package at all — apt-get install openjdk-11-jdk-headless fails, offering openjdk-17-jre-headless instead — and Debian 11 (bullseye), the previous base, left LTS support, so its package index still resolves while every .deb 404s (an apt-get update that succeeds followed by every install failing; retrying does not help). Ubuntu 22.04's own main repository carries both python3.10 and openjdk-11-jdk-headless with security maintenance into 2027, so one vendor covers both constraints with no third-party JDK.
  • Extras include expression. The set hgc ptm ancestry psroc constraint enrichex cohort viz duckdb expression is checked against [project.optional-dependencies] in pyproject.toml and covers every unique package across all extras. Omitting expression builds an image with no scanpy, so hvantk expression … cannot run. ml and interactive are redundant: scikit-learn arrives via ancestry/psroc, plotly via viz.

The %post block ends by printing java -version and importing hail, so a broken image fails at build time rather than at first use.

docs.title: 3.3 Build (rootless) and validate
docs.text:
# Keep build cache/tmp OFF the small home quota
export SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$WORK/containers/cache     # APPTAINER_* if you have apptainer
export SINGULARITY_TMPDIR=$WORK/containers/tmp
mkdir -p "$SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR" "$SINGULARITY_TMPDIR"

# Build from the REPO ROOT: %files paths in the def are relative to the build CWD.
cd <the cluster clone>
singularity build --build-arg HVANTK_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) \
  $WORK/containers/hvantk.sif containers/hvantk.def

The def file's %arguments section and the --build-arg flag need SingularityCE 4.0 or Apptainer 1.2 or later (check with singularity --version or apptainer --version). An older tool stops with unknown flag: --build-arg.

--fakeroot is not usable on every cluster. It needs a /etc/subuid entry for your account; without one the build fails immediately with could not use fakeroot: no valid mapping entry found for <user>, and a plain unprivileged build is refused outright with --remote, --fakeroot, or the proot command are required to build this source as a non-root user. Check before assuming:

grep "^$USER:" /etc/subuid    # empty output => --fakeroot will NOT work here

When there is no subuid entry, SingularityCE (4.0 or later, as above) accepts a static proot instead, which needs no privileges at all:

mkdir -p ~/bin && curl -fsSL -o ~/bin/proot https://proot.gitlab.io/proot/bin/proot
chmod +x ~/bin/proot
export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"       # singularity picks proot up from PATH
singularity build --build-arg HVANTK_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) \
  $WORK/containers/hvantk.sif containers/hvantk.def

Builds take roughly 10 minutes and the image is ~2.2 GB.

Validate the full native + JVM stack on a compute node (not login) — and go through the run wrapper, because Hail cannot initialise inside the container without Spark scratch (see §4.1):

srun -c 4 --mem 16g bash containers/hvantk_run.sh utils check-install
#   expects: Hail version prints, balding_nichols_model smoke test passes.

hvantk utils check-install is the canonical go/no-go for a node — it initializes Hail, prints hl.version(), runs a Hail smoke test, and diagnoses proxy problems.

docs.title: 4.1 Default: Spark local mode on one exclusive fat node
docs.text:
hvantk runs Hail in local Spark mode — every init_hail() call uses local defaults (no master/memory config in the repo). On HPC that maps to one exclusive node, many cores, high memory, with Spark temp on node-local scratch.

SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS is mandatory when running from the container, and its absence is misdiagnosed. Without a writable node-local scratch bound into the image, Hail init dies with DiskBlockManager: ERROR: Failed to create any local dir, followed by Hail initialisation failed: [Errno 111] Connection refused from py4j. The second message is what you see first and it reads like a network or proxy fault; it is not. containers/hvantk_run.sh sets the scratch dir up and binds it, so prefer:

bash containers/hvantk_run.sh utils check-install
HVANTK_BIND="$WORK:$WORK" bash containers/hvantk_run.sh reprocess clinvar:variants ...

containers/hvantk_run.sh runs the image's own installed copy of hvantk, not your checked-out code, and is meant for an interactive check. For a batch job that runs the checkout (so a code change takes effect without rebuilding the image), submit through the hpc-hail-job agent skill instead, which exports PYTHONPATH and sizes the request for you — or write your own sbatch script along these lines:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=hvantk-hail
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=32
#SBATCH --mem=240G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%j.out

# node-local fast scratch for Spark spill + Hail tmp (NEVER home/Lustre/GPFS)
export SCRATCH_DIR=${SLURM_TMPDIR:-/scratch/$USER/$SLURM_JOB_ID}
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_DIR"
export SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS="$SCRATCH_DIR"
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,0.0.0.0,::1   # protect py4j localhost socket

# run the checkout's code; the image has no git, so pass the commit a dataset
# build records as its builder_commit
REPO=$HOME/hvantk
apptainer exec \
  --bind /project/$USER/hvantk:/data \
  --bind "$SCRATCH_DIR" --bind "$REPO" \
  --env PYTHONPATH="$REPO" \
  --env HVANTK_BUILDER_COMMIT="$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse HEAD)" \
  hvantk.sif \
  hvantk hgc pipeline -i /data/gvcfs -o /data/out/hgc

The three settings that prevent the most common failures:

  1. Driver memory must sit below the Slurm --mem cgroup limit. In local mode the driver JVM is the executor, and Hail uses large off-heap/native memory (BLAS, LZ4) plus Python workers that live outside the JVM heap. Setting spark.driver.memory == --mem triggers a silent cgroup OOM-kill. Use ~75–85% of --mem (e.g. --mem=240G → spark.driver.memory=192g).
  2. Pin cores; don't let Spark grab the machine. On an --exclusive node local[*] is fine; on a shared node use local[<cpus-per-task>]. Uncapped local[*] on a shared node causes thread oversubscription and "Executor heartbeat timed out" errors.
  3. Spark/Hail temp on node-local scratch, never the parallel filesystem.

To set these explicitly, wrap your script's init_hail() → hl.init(). A drop-in Hail init for a 240 GB node:

import os, hail as hl
scratch = os.environ["SCRATCH_DIR"]
hl.init(
    master="local[*]",                 # exclusive node → all cores OK
    tmp_dir=scratch,
    spark_conf={
        "spark.driver.memory": "192g",  # ~80% of --mem=240G
        "spark.local.dir": scratch,
        "spark.driver.maxResultSize": "16g",
        "spark.serializer": "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer",
        "spark.kryo.registrator": "is.hail.kryo.HailKryoRegistrator",
    },
)

Avoid small-file storms. Each Hail .ht/.mt partition is a part file; too many tiny parts saturate Lustre/GPFS metadata servers and slow the whole cluster. Coalesce before writing big outputs, and prefer scratch then archive:

mt = mt.naive_coalesce(64)        # ~hundreds-of-MB parts, not thousands of tiny ones
mt.write("/scratch/.../cohort.mt", overwrite=True)
# then tar the .mt directory to project storage rather than leaving 1000s of parts on Lustre

docs.title: 4.2 Escalation: multi-node via the cluster's Spark-on-Slurm launcher
docs.text:
Use this only when one fat node cannot hold the working set. hvantk supports adopting an externally-initialized Spark/Hail session via the HVANTK_SKIP_HAIL_INIT environment variable (checked in hvantk/core/utils/hail_context.py): set it non-empty and init_hail() will not call hl.init(), deferring to a session you created. Pattern:

  1. Launch the cluster's Spark standalone cluster inside a Slurm allocation (per your center's docs — e.g. a spark start ... that yields a spark://host:7077 master).
  2. In a thin wrapper, call hl.init(sc=<existing SparkContext>) (or hl.init(master="spark://host:7077", ...)) before importing hvantk pipelines, then export HVANTK_SKIP_HAIL_INIT=1 so hvantk adopts that backend.
  3. Run inside the container with the Hail jar on the Spark classpath (--jars $HAIL_HOME/hail-all-spark.jar, Kryo serializer + HailKryoRegistrator).

Spark-on-Slurm launchers are cluster-specific and double-allocate resources (Slurm and spark-submit flags must agree); expect operational friction. Stay in §4.1 local mode unless data forces this.

docs.title: 5. Getting data onto the cluster
docs.text: The gitignored local/ tree is not part of the git clone — it must be copied there explicitly. Split it by action rather than copying it wholesale.

docs.title: 5.1 Action split
docs.text:
Action Examples How Transfer (experiment state / gated / source-specific) notebooks + outputs, single-cell .h5ad atlases, EGA gvcfs, interactome BED, GTEx proteomics, UKB-PPP, per-study cardiac data Globus via DTN Refetch on login node raw UCSC Cell Browser dumps, GTEx/iPSC-CM eQTL stats, ArrayExpress, 1000 Genomes, GWAS Catalog, GenCC, ClinVar, Ensembl GTF, gnomAD lof-metrics hvantk download … / skill downloaders Regenerate on-cluster derived Hail .mts (e.g. Expression Atlas, GTEx TPM matrices) hvantk build steps Skip (redundant) uncompressed .tsv where a .bgz exists; raw dumps that a built .h5ad supersedes; duplicate .gz next to .bgz don't copy

Net effect: physically move the experiment state and gated sources, refetch public bulk on the cluster, regenerate derived datasets, and avoid copying redundancy. Globus is fast enough that transferring what you already have is often simpler than re-deriving it — decide per-subtree.

docs.title: 5.2 Filesystem placement
docs.text:
• $HOME (small, backed up): the cloned repo + hvantk.sif + sbatch scripts. Never bulk data.
  • /project (or work): the local/ data tree, e.g. /project/$USER/hvantk/local/, bound into the container as /data. Keep the same local/... substructure so experiment scripts' relative paths work.
  • scratch (purged): Spark/Hail tmp, per-job intermediates, container build cache. Copy results back to project before the purge window (often 30–60 days).

docs.title: 5.3 Moving the data
docs.text:
# Preferred: Globus (resumable, parallel, auto-checksum), endpoint = the cluster DTN
module load globus-cli 2>/dev/null || true
globus transfer --recursive --verify-checksum \
  "$LAPTOP_ENDPOINT:/path/to/pyvatk/local" \
  "$CLUSTER_ENDPOINT:/project/$USER/hvantk/local"

# Fallback: rsync through the Data Transfer Node (NOT the login node)
rsync -avP --partial \
  /path/to/pyvatk/local/ \
  $USER@dtn.cluster.edu:/project/$USER/hvantk/local/
# verify (checksum compare, dry-run)
rsync -avnc /path/to/pyvatk/local/ \
  $USER@dtn.cluster.edu:/project/$USER/hvantk/local/

Add --exclude rules for the §5.1 "skip" rows (e.g. uncompressed .tsv files that duplicate a .bgz) to avoid moving redundant gigabytes.

docs.title: 6. External / streaming data
docs.text:
Several experiment paths stream from external sources at runtime. Where compute nodes have internet they run in-job; the concern is volume and rate limits, so stage the heavy/repeated pulls:

Source Used by Recommendation gnomAD v4.1 (GCS / googleapis) gnomAD-MAPS / constraint experiments Stage once to /project/.../gnomad/ (per-chr sites or a filtered HT); repoint scripts at the local path UCSC phyloP100way bigWig (~9 GB) phyloP per-codon queries Download once to project; point the query at the local .bw (also removes remote-query latency) Ensembl VEP REST VEP annotation experiments keep batch ≤ 200 + honor Retry-After; for big sets use a local VEP install. (Public VEP does not serve AlphaMissense — use the standalone TSV if needed) eQTL Catalogue / Pan-UKB (EBI FTP, AWS S3) coloc / QTL experiments transfer any existing local data_cache so re-streaming is unnecessary Ensembl GTF (ftp.ensembl.org) PTM pipeline transfer the cached GTF; pass the local path to skip the download step

Two operational notes:

  • Drift checks need internet by design. Run hvantk drift / hvantk download on the login node; pass --no-check-drift to hvantk reprocess inside batch jobs if a compute partition is ever firewalled.
  • Proxy: if the cluster routes outbound traffic through an HTTP proxy, set http_proxy/https_proxy and keep NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,0.0.0.0,::1 so Hail's py4j localhost socket is not intercepted.

docs.title: 7.1 A reprocess build (single node)
docs.text:
srun --partition=standard -c 8 --mem 48g -t 4:00:00 \
  apptainer exec --bind /project/$USER/hvantk/local:/data hvantk.sif \
    hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants \
      --raw-dir /data/data/clinvar_ts --output /data/out/clinvar.ht

docs.title: 7.2 Embarrassingly-parallel fan-out (array job)
docs.text:
Ideal for sweeps of one command over many independent inputs, such as one tissue per task. Build a task list and index it with $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=hvantk-fanout
#SBATCH --array=1-3                 # one task per line of tissues.txt
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4 --mem=16G --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out
# tissues.txt: one tissue name per line (Liver, Lung, Thyroid)
TISSUE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" tissues.txt)
apptainer exec --bind /project/$USER/hvantk/local:/data hvantk.sif \
  hvantk qtlcascade cascade --eqtl-ht /data/out/eqtl.ht --pqtl-ht /data/out/pqtl.ht \
    --tissue "$TISSUE" -o "/data/out/cascade_${TISSUE}.ht"

For experiments that stream remote data (e.g. phyloP bigWig, gnomAD), pre-stage those inputs to project storage (§6) and repoint the scripts at the local paths before launching at scale.

docs.title: 8. Reproducibility and provenance
docs.text:
• Pin the container, not just the code. Record the .sif's build date and the poetry.lock hash; a given hvantk.sif reproduces the exact Hail/numpy/native stack. Re-derive the image only by re-running apptainer build against the same lock.
  • Pass --build-arg HVANTK_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) on every build. The image copies only hvantk/ (no .git) and purges git itself. The build arg stamps the commit into the image's own copy of hvantk, so a dataset that copy builds records it as its builder_commit; without it, such a dataset records only the package version.
  • Pass the checkout's commit to a job that runs the checkout. With --env PYTHONPATH=<checkout> the job runs the checkout's code, not the image's, so the image's commit does not describe it. Pass --env HVANTK_BUILDER_COMMIT=$(git -C <checkout> rev-parse HEAD) too (§4.1); the hpc-hail-job templates do both, with -dirty for uncommitted edits under hvantk/. Without it, the job's datasets record hvantk <version>.
  • hvantk stamps provenance on every dataset (ctx.provenance(...)) and has hvantk drift for source fingerprints — keep using both on-cluster so results carry their input lineage.
  • Treat scratch as ephemeral; the project copy of outputs + the .sif + the git SHA are the reproducible record.

docs.title: 9. Runbook (ordered)
docs.text:
1. Login node: git clone the repo into $HOME. Note partitions, scratch path, --fakeroot availability, Spark-on-Slurm launcher (§2).
  2. Build the image: from the repository root (the def file's %files paths are relative to it), set APPTAINER_* to scratch and run apptainer build --fakeroot --build-arg HVANTK_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) hvantk.sif containers/hvantk.def (§3.3; Apptainer 1.2+ or SingularityCE 4.0+), or build on a laptop and copy, or run the hpc-container skill.
  3. Validate: srun ... apptainer exec hvantk.sif hvantk utils check-install.
  4. Move data (§5): Globus the "transfer" set into /project/$USER/hvantk/local/; refetch the public bulk on the login node; regenerate .mts on-cluster; skip the redundant files.
  5. Stage streaming inputs (§6): download the phyloP bigWig + a gnomAD slice to project; repoint the relevant scripts at local paths.
  6. First real run: submit the §4.1 single-fat-node Hail job for a known pipeline; confirm it writes to project and stays under the cgroup memory limit.
  7. Scale out: use array jobs (§7.2) for fan-out; reserve the Spark-on-Slurm path (§4.2) for working sets that exceed a fat node.

docs.title: 10. Gotchas quick-reference
docs.text:
• Java 17 default → Hail breaks. Force Java 11 (baked into the container).
  • A Debian base image → bookworm (12) ships no openjdk-11 at all (apt offers openjdk-17-jre-headless instead), and bullseye (11) left LTS support, so its apt index still resolves while every .deb 404s. Use ubuntu:22.04 (§3.2).
  • --fakeroot with no /etc/subuid entry → no valid mapping entry found, and an unprivileged build is refused. Put a static proot on PATH instead (§3.3).
  • unknown flag: --build-arg → SingularityCE older than 4.0 or Apptainer older than 1.2. Use a newer one (§3.3).
  • Container Hail init: [Errno 111] Connection refused → almost never the network. Look one line up for DiskBlockManager: Failed to create any local dir: Spark has no writable scratch. Use containers/hvantk_run.sh (§4.1).
  • spark.driver.memory == --mem → silent cgroup OOM-kill. Use ~80%.
  • local[*] on a shared node → heartbeat timeouts. Pin to --cpus-per-task, or use --exclusive.
  • Spark/Hail tmp on Lustre/GPFS or $HOME → slow + metadata storms. Use node-local scratch.
  • Over-partitioned .mt/.ht → millions of tiny part files choke the parallel filesystem. naive_coalesce before writing; archive off the parallel FS.
  • HTTP proxy intercepting localhost → Hail/py4j init fails. Set NO_PROXY for localhost.
  • Stray system/conda Python below the 3.10 floor → use the container's Python; never run hvantk against an unmanaged interpreter.
  • Core install ≠ full toolkit — install the right extras (hgc ptm ancestry psroc constraint enrichex cohort viz duckdb expression) in the image. Dropping expression yields an image with no scanpy, so hvantk expression … fails.
  • Scratch is purged — copy results to project/home before the window.

docs.title: Building datasets
docs.text:
This guide covers the data layer: discovering what hvantk can build, building a dataset with hvantk reprocess, checking a source for drift, and browsing the dataset catalog. The analysis tools that consume built datasets (annotation matrices, cohorts, expression, gene sets and the rest) each have a page under Tools; See also links them.

If you haven't installed hvantk yet, see Installation.

docs.title: Discover datasets
docs.text: Every in-tree data source ships as a plugin under hvantk/skills/<provider>/, declared by a plugin.yaml manifest: its datasets, lifecycle (download / parse / build), drift probe, and dataset contract. Every analysis command ships the same way, as a tool.yaml manifest. Two command groups inspect these registries.

docs.title: hvantk plugins
docs.text:
# List every loaded provider and how many datasets each declares
hvantk plugins list

# Full detail for one provider: its datasets, skill paths, drift fingerprints
hvantk plugins describe clinvar

# Name anything that failed to load, and why
hvantk plugins errors

# Validate a plugin.yaml against the schema, offline
hvantk plugins validate hvantk/skills/clinvar/plugin.yaml

list and describe are informational and exit 0 even when something failed to load (describe exits 1 only if the named provider itself is unknown or failed to load as a whole); errors is the one whose exit code reports load failures (1 if it lists anything, 0 if clean); validate exits 1 on a schema violation.

docs.title: hvantk tools
docs.text:
hvantk tools list
hvantk tools describe annotate
hvantk tools errors
hvantk tools validate hvantk/tools/annotation/annotate_cli.tool.yaml

Same shape as plugins: list and describe exit 0; errors exits 1 if it lists anything, 0 if clean; validate exits 1 on a schema violation.

docs.title: Build a dataset
docs.text:
hvantk reprocess <provider>:<dataset> chains a plugin's lifecycle stages (download, parse, build), then runs the dataset's drift probe:

hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants \
  --raw-dir data/clinvar/ \
  --output out/clinvar.ht

A dataset declared acquisition.mode: byo (see Data Sources) treats --skip-download as implicit and instead requires --raw-dir to already hold files -- unless --skip-parse is combined with an explicit --intermediate, in which case the raw directory is never read and does not need to be populated.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Required Description DATASET (argument) yes <provider>:<dataset>, e.g. clinvar:variants. --raw-dir DIRECTORY yes Where to write (or, with --skip-download, read) raw files. --output PATH yes Final builder output path. Extension must match the dataset's native format (see below); a mismatch fails before any stage runs. --intermediate PATH no Path for the parsed intermediate. If the plugin declares lifecycle.parse and you omit this, it defaults to <raw-dir>/<provider>_<dataset>.intermediate and the default is logged. --skip-download no Skip the download stage; read from --raw-dir instead. --skip-parse no Skip the parse stage; the build reads --intermediate if given, else --raw-dir. --skip-build no Skip the build stage. Nothing is written to --output. --plugin-arg KEY=VALUE no, repeatable Forwarded to the plugin's download, parse, and build functions (e.g. --plugin-arg cancer_type=brca for cptac:phospho, --plugin-arg reference_genome=GRCh38 for clinvar). --check-drift / --no-check-drift no Run the post-build drift probe (default: on) or skip it. -v, --verbose no Surface the builder's own INFO logs (e.g. per-chunk progress) on stderr. -q, --quiet no Suppress the per-stage progress lines; errors still print.

--plugin-arg values are coerced before they reach the plugin: true/false (case-insensitive) become bool; an integer string becomes int; a decimal or scientific-notation string becomes float; a value containing a comma becomes a list of its comma-separated parts, each coerced the same way; anything else stays str.

docs.title: Output extension by dataset type
docs.text:
reprocess writes each dataset in its own native format -- there is no cross-format conversion -- so --output's extension must match the dataset's declared artifact_type and backend:

Dataset type Backend Extension Example AnnotationTable hail .ht clinvar:variants AnnotationTable pandas .parquet peptideatlas:phospho ExpressionMatrix anndata .h5ad cptac:phospho VariantMatrix hail .mt onek-genomes:variants GeneSet -- .geneset.json none built by an in-tree plugin yet

docs.title: Existing output and provenance
docs.text:
reprocess always overwrites an existing --output: there is no --overwrite flag and no confirmation prompt. (A few individual tool subcommands -- hvantk genesets and hvantk expression -- do refuse an existing output unless you pass their own --overwrite; that is a property of those commands, not of reprocess.)

Every build writes a sidecar <output>.provenance.json next to the output, recording:

{
  "plugin": "clinvar",
  "dataset": "clinvar:variants",
  "plugin_version": "0.2.0",
  "source_fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "schema_id": "clinvar-variants-v1",
  "build_timestamp": "2026-10-20T12:00:00+00:00",
  "builder_commit": "3f5c1a9e7b2d4c6e8f0a1b3c5d7e9f0a2b4c6d8e",
  "parents": [],
  "build_parameters": {}
}

source_fingerprint is the drift probe's fingerprint at build time. parents is filled only for a dataset derived from other hvantk datasets. build_parameters records the options a builder chose to stamp, and is null only in a sidecar written before the field existed. builder_commit names the hvantk code that ran the build. It is the first of these that applies:

  • the commit of hvantk's own git checkout, with -dirty when files under hvantk/ have uncommitted changes;
  • for the container image's own copy of hvantk, the commit the image was built from (--build-arg HVANTK_COMMIT=<sha>, which the hpc-container skill's templates pass);
  • the HVANTK_BUILDER_COMMIT environment variable, which the hpc-hail-job templates set to the commit of the checkout they run inside the image, since the image has no git;
  • hvantk <version>, for example for a wheel install.

Loading the dataset later (hvantk.core.io.load) re-attaches this Provenance.

docs.title: Drift check at the end of a build
docs.text: With --check-drift (the default), reprocess runs the dataset's drift probe once the build finishes and prints drift: <status> -- this never changes reprocess's own exit code, even for drifted. Use --no-check-drift to skip the probe entirely (e.g. offline), or run hvantk drift <dataset> separately when you need drift status to affect a script's exit code.

docs.title: Downloading without building
docs.text: hvantk download <source> runs one provider's downloader on its own, without the parse/build/drift stages reprocess chains it into. Not every dataset has one -- see Data Sources for which do, and for the ones that are manual-download only.

docs.title: Check a source for drift
docs.text:
hvantk drift <provider>:<dataset> (or --all, optionally filtered with --domain) compares the dataset's live drift-probe output against the fingerprint file committed in the plugin's own tree, as named by its manifest's tests.drift_fingerprint -- for example tests/drift_fingerprint.json for a single-dataset plugin, or, for a multi-dataset one, either a per-dataset subfolder (phospho/tests/drift_fingerprint.json) or a suffixed filename (tests/drift_fingerprint_variants.json):

hvantk drift clinvar:variants
hvantk drift --all --domain genomics --json
Status Meaning clean The live probe output matches the committed fingerprint. drifted The probe ran, but the source has changed since the fingerprint was captured; printed with a diff. probe_failed The probe raised, timed out, or returned something invalid (e.g. unreachable network). stub Documentation-only source with no live probe (not an error; exits clean, with a stderr warning).

Exit code is the worst outcome across the datasets checked:

Exit code Meaning 0 Clean (and, with --all, no load errors). 1 At least one dataset drifted. 2 A probe failed, a dataset's plugin failed to load, or (with --all) nothing was registered to check. 3 The dataset name is unknown. 4 An invalid combination of flags.

--regenerate, --accepted-in, --no-ledger-row, --ledger, and --mark-rebuilt rewrite the committed fingerprint and the rebuild ledger; they are for maintainers promoting a drift result, not for routine checks -- see Contributing.

docs.title: Browse the catalog
docs.text:
hvantk catalog reads the dataset metadata every plugin declares in its own catalog/datasets.json (not every plugin has one):

hvantk catalog list --omics-type genomics --limit 10
hvantk catalog search "clinical significance" --omics-type genomics
hvantk catalog show ClinVar_latest --format json
hvantk catalog stats
Subcommand Key options list --omics-type {transcriptomics,proteomics,genomics,epigenomics}, --data-source TEXT (substring, case-insensitive), --organism TEXT (substring), --limit INTEGER (default 50) search QUERY Matches title, description, and accession. --omics-type, --limit (default 50) show ACCESSION --format {yaml,json} (default yaml) stats No options; aggregate counts by omics type, organism, and data source

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
# Convert standard gzip to BGZF for parallel Hail import
hvantk utils convert-bgz data/scores.tsv.gz --threads 4

# Verify a BGZF file's block integrity
hvantk utils validate-bgzf data/clinvar.vcf.gz --quick

# Smoke-test the install: Hail init, a tiny synthetic MatrixTable, describe()
hvantk utils check-install
Command Options Notes convert-bgz INPUT_FILE -o, --output PATH (default: replaces .gz with .bgz); -t, --threads INTEGER (default 4) No-ops if the input is already BGZF; exits 1 if the input isn't gzip at all. validate-bgzf PATH --quick (header-only; skips CRC32/ISIZE) PATH may be a directory, in which case every *.vcf.gz inside it is checked. Exits 1 if any file fails. check-install none The one utils command that starts Hail/Spark: it initializes Hail, builds a balding_nichols_model MatrixTable (3 populations, 50 samples, 200 variants), and prints its schema.

Hail reads standard gzip (.gz) single-threaded; BGZF (.bgz) parallelizes, which matters for large raw files before hvantk reprocess imports them.

docs.title: Tips and troubleshooting
docs.text:
• A plugin's on-disk directory name and its manifest name: sometimes differ by _ versus - (e.g. the gwas_catalog directory declares name: gwas-catalog). If hvantk plugins describe <provider> or hvantk drift <provider>:<dataset> says "unknown provider" or "unknown dataset", run hvantk plugins errors first -- a provider that failed to load can look identical to a typo.
  • A build that fails immediately with a message about --output's extension is reprocess's own fast-fail check, before any stage runs -- see the extension table above, not a Hail error.
  • A stub result from hvantk drift means the source has no live, programmatic probe (documentation-only acquisition); it is expected, not a failure.
