docs.title: Workflow skills
docs.text:
hvantk ships workflow skills: instructions a coding agent follows to run the toolkit for you, on a laptop or on a Slurm cluster, with the checks a careful operator runs. The agent orchestrates; every command it executes is a deterministic hvantk command, and no language model sits in the data path.

They live in the repository's top-level skills/ folder, one folder per skill, in the Agent Skills layout. The catalog and the install steps are in skills/README.md; the contract they follow is skills/workflow-conventions/SKILL.md.

docs.title: What a skill gives you
docs.text:
• A procedure: the exact commands, in order, with the template scripts to run them.
  • Preflight that refuses to guess: the checkout commit, the image digest and every cluster-specific value are confirmed first, from a site profile you fill in once.
  • Traps: the failure modes we met, each with its cause and fix.
  • Verification: what to check on a real run and a receipt tied to the output's provenance sidecar.
  • A measured task: each skill ships an eval/ folder with a public-data task, a deterministic check and the reference values its positive control produced, so the skill can be tested, by us and by you.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Fill in the site profile on the cluster, in the $HVANTK_REPO checkout:

cp skills/_site/site-profile.example.sh skills/_site/site-profile.local.sh   # gitignored
# fill it in: see skills/_site/SITE-PROFILE.md
export HVANTK_SITE_PROFILE=/path/to/hvantk/skills/_site/site-profile.local.sh
bash skills/_site/check-site-profile.sh

No image yet on this site? check-site-profile.sh otherwise refuses because HVANTK_SIF points nowhere; run the hvantk:hpc-container skill first, or pass it --allow-missing-image while bootstrapping.

Then install the skills into your agent (Claude Code: /plugin install hvantk --marketplace bigbio/hvantk, or on older releases /plugin marketplace add bigbio/hvantk then /plugin install hvantk@hvantk; other harnesses: point them at skills/) and ask it, for example, to build a dataset on the cluster. The shipped skills cover running any Hail-backed hvantk command as a single-node Slurm job from the container image, keeping a cluster clone in step with GitHub, building and promoting the image, joint genotyping, delivering a sample subset of a callset, ancestry inference, building many datasets as one array job with their outputs verified, triaging a drift signal (repairing the plugin, rebuilding, and recording the fingerprint and the rebuild ledger), building the gene index, running a cohort's gene burden and attaching it, ranking a cohort's genes and evaluating the ranking against a label set, and the molecular QTL cascade with colocalisation; the catalog in skills/README.md is the current list. See Running on HPC for the cluster setup those skills assume.

docs.title: The two kinds of skill
docs.text: The per-provider SKILL.md files under hvantk/skills/<provider>/ are resource specs: they tell an agent how to author a data-source plugin against the plugin contract. Workflow skills tell it how to run the toolkit. They reference each other and do not overlap.

docs.title: Ancestry inference
docs.text:
hvantk ancestry-inference assigns a population label to each sample in a query cohort by projecting it against a labeled reference panel (e.g. 1000 Genomes) with PCA, then classifying with a Random Forest trained on the reference panel's known labels.

Figure 1. Ancestry inference: merge with the reference panel, variant filtering, optional LD pruning, PCA fitted on query and reference together, Random Forest training and prediction.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Row key Column key Required fields Query MatrixTable (locus, alleles) s (sample ID) GT genotype calls (or LGT + LA, auto-converted) Reference MatrixTable same as query s GT/LGT as above, plus a categorical ancestry-label column
  • Query and reference must use the same reference genome (GRCh37 or GRCh38) and the same row key structure; mismatches fail immediately with a descriptive error.
  • The reference panel's ancestry-label column is named by --ancestry-col (ancestry_col in Python), default ancestry. It must be a column field on the reference MatrixTable, categorical (e.g. "EUR", "AFR", "EAS", "SAS", "AMR"), with at least 2 distinct populations and at least 10 samples per population (lower via PipelineConfig(min_samples_per_pop=...) in Python; there is no CLI flag for it).
  • hvantk ships no reference panel. To build a 1000 Genomes high-coverage NYGC/CCDG MatrixTable and attach IGSR population labels (super_pop/pop) to use as --ancestry-col, see the 1000 Genomes example and Data sources. Other commonly used panels are 1000 Genomes Phase 3 (2,504 samples, 5 super-populations) and HapMap Phase 3 (1,184 samples, 11 populations) — bring your own copy, keyed and labeled the same way.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
hvantk ancestry-inference \
  -q cohort.mt \
  -r 1kg_reference.mt \
  --ancestry-col super_pop \
  -o ancestry_predictions.ht \
  --generate-report \
  --export-tsv

import hail as hl
from hvantk.algorithms.ancestry import run_ancestry_inference

result = run_ancestry_inference(
    query_mt=hl.read_matrix_table("cohort.mt"),
    reference_mt=hl.read_matrix_table("1kg_reference.mt"),
    ancestry_col="super_pop",
    min_prob=0.75,
)

predictions = result.get_predictions_df()
print(predictions["predicted_ancestry"].value_counts())
result.save("results/ancestry")

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Merge. Inner join query and reference on (locus, alleles); keep only the GT entry field; column-union the samples, tagging each with its source (query or reference). Fails if there are 0 shared variants, or fewer than --min-shared-variants (default 10,000); warns below 50,000.
  2. Filter. Restrict to autosomes (locus.in_autosome()), then biallelic SNPs, then apply Hail's variant_qc: call rate ≥ --min-call-rate (default 0.98) and alternate-allele frequency between --min-af/--max-af (default 0.01/0.99). An optional HWE filter (off by default; --apply-hwe-filter, p ≥ --hwe-p, default 1e-6) can additionally drop likely genotyping errors.
  3. LD prune (skippable with --skip-ld-pruning). hl.ld_prune on GT with r2 = --ld-r2 (default 0.2) and bp_window_size = --ld-window (default 500,000).
  4. PCA. hl.hwe_normalized_pca (Patterson et al., 2006) computes --n-pcs (default 20) principal components jointly on the merged query+reference set — this is not a projection of the query onto a reference-only PC space; query and reference samples share one PCA fit. Loadings are always computed in memory; --save-loadings / result.loadings persist them (see caveats below).
  5. Train. A RandomForestClassifier (n_estimators = --n-estimators, default 100; random_state = --seed, default 42) is fit on the reference rows' first --n-pcs-classify PC scores (default 10) against their known --ancestry-col labels. max_features="sqrt", min_samples_leaf=5, class_weight="balanced" and n_jobs=-1 are fixed and not configurable. Unless --skip-validation, a stratified --n-cv-folds-fold cross-validation (default 5) gives a held-out accuracy estimate; this raises if n_cv_folds exceeds the smallest population's sample count.
  6. Predict. The fitted model scores the query rows' PC scores. A sample's label is the highest-probability class if that probability is ≥ --min-prob (default 0.75), otherwise "unassigned". Reference rows are also re-scored (with no threshold) for reporting and plotting — this is an in-sample fit, not the cross-validated estimate from step 5.

For a fixed reference PC space that later query batches project onto (the approach gnomAD and similar projects use), call compute_pca() on the reference alone and project_samples() with its loadings, instead of run_ancestry_inference's joint PCA. See Python API.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Flag Description -q, --query-mt Path to the query MatrixTable. -r, --reference-mt Path to the reference MatrixTable with known ancestry labels. -o, --output-ht Output path for the predictions Hail Table.

docs.title: Reference panel and output
docs.text: Flag Default Description --ancestry-col ancestry Column with ancestry labels in the reference MT. --output-dir <output-ht parent>/ancestry_results Directory for TSV/model/report/stats outputs.

docs.title: Variant filtering
docs.text: Flag Default Description --min-af 0.01 Minimum alternate-allele frequency. --max-af 0.99 Maximum alternate-allele frequency. --min-call-rate 0.98 Minimum variant call rate. --apply-hwe-filter off Apply a Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium filter. --hwe-p 1e-6 HWE p-value threshold (variants below are removed).

docs.title: LD pruning
docs.text: Flag Default Description --ld-r2 0.2 LD pruning r² threshold. --ld-window 500000 LD pruning window, in base pairs. --skip-ld-pruning off Skip LD pruning (faster; may affect accuracy).

docs.title: PCA and classification
docs.text: Flag Default Description --n-pcs 20 Number of principal components to compute. --n-pcs-classify 10 Number of PCs used as RF features (clamped to --n-pcs if larger). --n-estimators 100 Number of trees in the Random Forest. --min-prob 0.75 Minimum probability for an assignment; below this, "unassigned". --seed 42 Random seed.

docs.title: Validation and merge
docs.text: Flag Default Description --skip-validation off Skip cross-validation. --n-cv-folds 5 Number of stratified CV folds. --min-shared-variants 10000 Minimum shared query/reference variants required.

docs.title: Output formats and checkpointing
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --generate-report off Write an HTML report (needs the visualization extras). --export-tsv off Export predictions as TSV. --save-model off Pickle the trained Random Forest. --save-loadings off Write the PCA loadings Hail Table. --checkpoint-path none Directory for intermediate checkpoints. --overwrite off Overwrite existing outputs and checkpoints.

There is no --log-level option. Verbosity is the top-level flag, which must come before the subcommand: hvantk -v ancestry-inference ... (INFO) or hvantk -vv ancestry-inference ... (DEBUG).

docs.title: Predictions Hail Table (-o/--output-ht)
docs.text:
Row-keyed by s, containing both query and reference samples (_ancestry_source distinguishes them):

Field Type Description predicted_ancestry str Assigned population label, or "unassigned". ancestry_probability float Maximum class probability. prob_<POP> float Per-population probability, one column per class. PC1...PC<n_pcs_classify> float The PCs used for classification (not all --n-pcs computed — see Method). _ancestry_source str "query" or "reference". _known_ancestry str Original label (reference rows only; missing for query).

docs.title: Additional files (under --output-dir)
docs.text:
File Written when predictions.tsv --export-tsv (same columns as the predictions table). rf_model.pkl --save-model. pca_loadings.ht --save-loadings (loadings from the joint PCA — see caveats). ancestry_report.html --generate-report. pipeline_stats.json always.

result.save(output_path, save_model=True, save_loadings=True) (Python only) writes a related but not identical set directly under output_path: predictions.ht and predictions.tsv unconditionally, pc_scores.ht (all --n-pcs PCs, for every sample) unconditionally, rf_model.pkl/pca_loadings.ht unless disabled, and pipeline_stats.json — the last one additionally carries an "eigenvalues" key that the CLI's own pipeline_stats.json does not.

docs.title: HTML report (--generate-report)
docs.text: Summary cards (query/reference sample counts, assigned/unassigned, populations, shared variants); an ancestry distribution table and bar chart; a two-panel PCA plot (full view + one zoomed population) plus a variance-explained chart; cross-validation accuracy and confusion matrix (or a notice that validation was skipped); a probability-distribution histogram; a table of the top query predictions by probability; and the full pipeline configuration.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.ancestry import run_ancestry_inference, PipelineConfig

result = run_ancestry_inference(
    query_mt: hl.MatrixTable,
    reference_mt: hl.MatrixTable,
    ancestry_col: str = "ancestry",
    config: PipelineConfig = None,
    **kwargs,  # overrides individual PipelineConfig fields, e.g. min_prob=0.80
) -> AncestryInferenceResult

PipelineConfig fields mirror the CLI options above 1:1, plus min_samples_per_pop (default 10, Python-only — no CLI flag).

AncestryInferenceResult methods:

# Data access
result.get_predictions_df() -> pd.DataFrame
result.get_scores_df() -> pd.DataFrame          # all computed PCs, every sample
result.get_query_predictions() -> pd.DataFrame
result.get_reference_predictions() -> pd.DataFrame
result.get_accuracy() -> float | None           # cross-validation accuracy
result.variance_explained() -> list[float]
result.prediction_summary() -> dict[str, int]   # query-only counts by predicted_ancestry

# Visualization (each returns a matplotlib Figure, or None if not applicable)
result.plot_pca(pc_x=1, pc_y=2, show_query_as_undefined=False, **kwargs)
result.plot_pca_panel(show_query_as_undefined=False, **kwargs)
result.plot_ancestry_proportions(**kwargs)
result.plot_probability_distribution(**kwargs)
result.plot_variance_explained(n_pcs=10, **kwargs)
result.plot_confusion_matrix(normalize=True, **kwargs) -> Figure | None

# Output
result.generate_report(output_path, title="Ancestry Inference Report", **kwargs) -> Path
result.save(output_path, save_model=True, save_loadings=True) -> dict[str, str]

# MatrixTable annotation
result.annotate_matrixtable(mt: hl.MatrixTable) -> hl.MatrixTable

annotate_matrixtable adds predicted_ancestry, ancestry_probability and PC1...PC<n_pcs_classify> column annotations to mt, joined on its column key — useful for an ancestry-stratified downstream analysis:

annotated_mt = result.annotate_matrixtable(query_mt)
eur_mt = annotated_mt.filter_cols(annotated_mt.predicted_ancestry == "EUR")

Advanced: projecting onto a fixed reference PC space. run_ancestry_inference always fits PCA jointly. To instead fit PCA on the reference only and project query (or later) samples onto that fixed space without recomputing it:

from hvantk.algorithms.ancestry import compute_pca, project_samples

pca_result = compute_pca(reference_mt_filtered, n_pcs=10, compute_loadings=True)
query_scores = project_samples(query_mt_filtered, loadings=pca_result.loadings, n_pcs=10)

project_samples requires the loadings table to carry an af field (present when compute_pca ran with variant_qc annotated, which it is here); it is not called by run_ancestry_inference itself.

docs.title: Interpretation and caveats
docs.text:
• Joint PCA, not reference-fixed projection. The default pipeline's PCA axes are influenced by the query cohort, not just the reference. A query batch run twice (alone, and alongside a different second batch) can land at slightly different PC coordinates. If you need a stable, reusable PC space across runs, use the compute_pca() + project_samples() path above instead.
  • --save-loadings saves the joint run's loadings, not a reference-only fit. Using them later with project_samples() projects onto this run's combined PC space, not a clean reference-only one.
  • The variant-frequency filter is on alternate-allele frequency, not minor allele frequency — a variant with alt AF 0.95 passes the default --max-af 0.99 filter even though its minor allele frequency is 0.05.
  • Random Forest hyperparameters are mostly fixed. Only tree count (--n-estimators) and the random seed are configurable; max_features, min_samples_leaf and class_weight="balanced" are not exposed.
  • --min-prob is inclusive: a probability exactly equal to the threshold is assigned, not marked unassigned.
Threshold Behavior 0.50 Aggressive; may misclassify admixed individuals. 0.75 Balanced (default). 0.90 Conservative; more "unassigned" but higher confidence.
  • Reference rows' predicted_ancestry in the output table is an in-sample prediction from the model trained on all reference data, not a held-out estimate. For an honest accuracy figure, use result.get_accuracy() or the report's confusion matrix, both from cross-validation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No shared variants, or too few. merge_matrixtables raises if query and reference share 0 variants (check both use the same reference genome and that variants are normalized the same way) or fewer than --min-shared-variants (default 10,000) — the error names the actual count. Lowering the threshold is possible but not recommended; a genotyping-platform mismatch is a more likely root cause than a bad threshold.

A population has too few samples. Training requires at least 2 populations and min_samples_per_pop (default 10, Python-only) samples in each; the error names the underprovisioned population(s). Merge rare populations into a broader label, or exclude them from the reference panel.

KeyError: 's' while merging or predicting. Both MatrixTables must have their column key named literally s (Hail's import_vcf default). Re-key with mt.key_cols_by("s") (renaming the existing key field first if needed) before calling run_ancestry_inference.

Many samples "unassigned". Likely admixed individuals, or a query cohort that does not match the reference panel's populations well. Try a lower --min-prob, or check that the panel actually covers your cohort's ancestries.

Cross-validation accuracy is low. Reference populations may overlap in PC space. Try more PCs (--n-pcs-classify 15 or higher, up to --n-pcs) or a panel with better population separation; some populations (e.g. closely related regional groups) are inherently hard to separate from PCA alone.

Large datasets. Use --checkpoint-path so a failed run can resume past the expensive merge/filter/LD-prune/PCA steps; --skip-ld-pruning if variants are already LD-pruned; and fewer --n-pcs if memory-constrained.

docs.text:

  3. 1000 Genomes Project Consortium. (2015). A global reference for human genetic variation. Nature. 526(7571):68-74.

docs.title: Gene annotation matrix
docs.text: hvantk annotate turns already-built datasets into one gene x feature matrix ("Layer 1"). It is three commands run in order -- spine, prepare, compose -- because each stage is independently re-runnable and the expensive middle stage (prepare) is per-source, so it is the one worth parallelizing across a cluster.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it once you have a canonical gene table and the per-source datasets you want to join onto it (built separately with hvantk reprocess), and you want them combined into a single gene_id-keyed table, for example as the feature axes of hvantk rerank or any other analysis that expects one row per gene.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• ensembl-gene:structure -- the canonical gene table (--gene-table), keyed on gene_id.
  • hgnc:lookup -- the HGNC gene catalog (--hgnc), used both to build the spine and, in prepare, to resolve any source key that isn't already gene_id.
  • A feature-spec YAML (--spec) naming each source, its join key, and the columns to keep -- see Feature spec reference below.
  • Per axis, the built source itself: an AnnotationTable (.ht) for a gene_id / hgnc_id / symbol / uniprot_id / variant entry, or an ExpressionMatrix (.h5ad) for a matrix entry.

docs.title: 1. Build the spine
docs.text:
hvantk annotate spine \
  --gene-table out/ensembl_structure.ht \
  --hgnc out/hgnc_lookup.ht \
  --output out/spine.ht

--biotype defaults to protein_coding; pass --biotype all to keep every biotype. The hgnc_id join is a left join on purpose: a protein-coding Ensembl gene with no HGNC record stays in the spine with a missing hgnc_id rather than being dropped.

docs.title: 2. Declare the sources
docs.text:
name: chd-features
layer1:
  - {axis: constraint, source: gnomad-metrics:metrics, key: gene_id, columns: [mis_z]}
  - {axis: gevir,      source: gevir:metrics,          key: gene_id, columns: [gevir_pct]}

layer1: is a literal key, not a label you choose -- it names the gene-level evidence axes. Each axis label must be unique: it addresses the entry in the next two stages (--axis constraint, --prepared constraint=...) and names the {axis}_present column compose adds.

docs.title: 3. Prepare each axis, then compose
docs.text:
hvantk annotate prepare --spec features.yaml --axis constraint \
  --input out/gnomad_metrics.ht --spine out/spine.ht --output out/constraint.ht

hvantk annotate prepare --spec features.yaml --axis gevir \
  --input out/gevir_metrics.ht --spine out/spine.ht --output out/gevir.ht

hvantk annotate compose --spec features.yaml --spine out/spine.ht \
  --prepared constraint=out/constraint.ht \
  --prepared gevir=out/gevir.ht \
  --output out/features.ht

compose requires exactly one --prepared per axis the spec declares -- missing one is a click.UsageError before any Hail call; naming one the spec doesn't declare is the same. The manifest JSON lands next to the output (out/features.ht.manifest.json unless --manifest says otherwise).

docs.title: annotate spine
docs.text: Option Required Description --gene-table TEXT yes Path to the ensembl-gene:structure table. --hgnc TEXT yes Path to the hgnc:lookup table. --output TEXT yes Output path for the spine table. --biotype TEXT no Gene biotype to keep. Default protein_coding; pass all to keep every biotype.

docs.title: annotate prepare
docs.text: Option Required Description --spec TEXT yes Path to the feature-spec YAML. --axis TEXT yes Which layer1 entry (by its axis label) to prepare. --input TEXT yes The built source: an AnnotationTable (.ht), or an AnnData (.h5ad) for a matrix entry. --spine TEXT yes Path to the gene spine table (.ht). --output TEXT yes Output path for the prepared table (.ht). --hgnc TEXT only when the rule below requires it Path to the hgnc:lookup table.

docs.title: annotate compose
docs.text:
Option Required Description --spec TEXT yes Path to the feature-spec YAML. --spine TEXT yes Path to the gene spine table (.ht). --prepared TEXT yes, repeatable axis=path, one per spec layer1 axis. --output TEXT yes Output path for the composed matrix (.ht). --manifest TEXT no Output path for the manifest JSON. Default <output>.manifest.json.

None of the three commands has an --overwrite flag: each always overwrites an existing --output (ht.write(..., overwrite=True)), with no confirmation prompt.

docs.title: The --hgnc rule
docs.text:
prepare --hgnc is required exactly when the axis can't resolve onto gene_id on its own:

  • key: hgnc_id, key: symbol, or key: uniprot_id -- always needs --hgnc.
  • key: variant with an aggregate.to other than gene_id -- needs --hgnc to carry the aggregated id the rest of the way onto gene_id.
  • key: variant aggregating straight to gene_id, or a plain key: gene_id entry -- does not need it.
  • A matrix block (expression-atlas-shaped sources) is always key: symbol (the schema enforces this when loading the spec), so it always needs --hgnc.

hvantk annotate prepare --help states the rule in its own words; the logic lives in needs_hgnc in hvantk/tools/annotation/annotate_cli.py.

docs.title: Feature spec reference
docs.text:
Validated against feature_spec.schema.json. Two keys are functional: name and layer1 (a non-empty list). Each layer1 entry:

Field Required Notes axis yes Unique label; see above. source yes A provider:dataset string, used in log lines and error messages; --input on prepare is what actually locates the file, not this field. key yes One of gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol, uniprot_id, variant. columns yes Output column names, non-empty. For a variant entry these must exactly match what aggregate produces (see below); for a matrix entry they are checked against, but not limited to, what the reducer emits. min_mapping_rate no Default 0.9. prepare raises if the axis maps below this fraction of its input rows onto the spine. collapse no One of max, min, mean, sum. Required whenever a source maps many-to-one onto a gene_id (e.g. several UniProt accessions for one gene); omitting it is an error, not a silent drop. origin, ablate_separately no Accepted by the schema and stored on the parsed entry; nothing in prepare or compose currently reads either one. aggregate required iff key: variant See below. matrix only for an expression-atlas-shaped source Requires key: symbol. group_axis, atlas required; tissue_tag, stats (mean/fraction_expressed/frac), drop_groups, specificity optional.

A variant entry's aggregate block (by, to, scores required): groups rows by by (a ;-delimited gene-string column, dbNSFP's shape -- a single value still works), reduces each named score to a scalar per variant (reduce: max, the default, collapses a per-transcript dict; reduce: identity passes an already-scalar column through), then aggregates to to (one of gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol, uniprot_id) with the declared stats (mean, max, min, count, or frac_gt_<threshold>). Each {score}_{stat} pair becomes one output column (e.g. revel_mean), plus a row-count column named by count_name (default n_possible_missense). filter accepts only the named predicate "missense" -- this is a closed vocabulary, not a free-form expression.

The schema also accepts top-level spine and exclude keys, but load_spec (in hvantk/algorithms/annotation/spec.py) never reads either -- they currently have no effect on the build.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Spine (annotate spine): keyed on gene_id; columns gene_name, chromosome, gene_start, gene_end, gene_biotype, cds_length, n_coding_exons, n_transcripts, mane_select, hgnc_id, gene_group.
  • Prepared (annotate prepare): keyed on gene_id; exactly the axis's declared columns, restricted to genes on the spine.
  • Composed (annotate compose): the spine's columns, every axis's declared columns, and one {axis}_present boolean per axis (true iff that gene had a row in the axis's prepared table -- a value can be missing and {axis}_present false, distinguishing "absent from source" from any other reason a value is null).
  • Manifest (<output>.manifest.json): {"n_genes": N, "axes": {"<axis>": {"<column>": {"non_null_rate": ..., "positive_rate": ...}}}} -- non-null rate is over all spine genes, positive rate is the fraction of non-null values that are > 0.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
import hail as hl
from hvantk.core.utils.hail_context import init_hail
from hvantk.algorithms.annotation.spec import load_spec
from hvantk.algorithms.annotation.spine import build_spine, spine_mapping_rate
from hvantk.algorithms.annotation.prepare import prepare_source
from hvantk.algorithms.annotation.mapping import enforce_rate
from hvantk.algorithms.annotation.compose import compose

init_hail()

spine = build_spine(
    hl.read_table("out/ensembl_structure.ht"),
    hl.read_table("out/hgnc_lookup.ht"),
    biotype="protein_coding",
)
print(spine_mapping_rate(spine))  # fraction of spine genes with an hgnc_id

spec = load_spec("features.yaml")  # the two-axis spec above
spine_ids = spine.gene_id.collect()

prepared_by_axis = {}
for axis, source_ht in [
    ("constraint", hl.read_table("out/gnomad_metrics.ht")),
    ("gevir", hl.read_table("out/gevir_metrics.ht")),
]:
    entry = spec.entry(axis)
    prepared, report = prepare_source(source_ht, spine_ids, entry)
    enforce_rate(report, entry.min_mapping_rate)  # raises MappingRateError below the threshold
    prepared_by_axis[axis] = prepared

composed, manifest = compose(spine, prepared_by_axis, spec)  # compose needs every axis

This mirrors the CLI one-to-one: the CLI is a thin wrapper over these same functions. prepare_variant_source and prepare_matrix_source (same module) take the same (source, spine_gene_ids, entry, *, hgnc=None) shape for key: variant and matrix entries respectively.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• compose raises if two axes declare the same output column name -- checked once in pure Python against the spec, and again against the prepared tables' actual columns (a matrix axis's per-group vector columns aren't known until then).
  • Two matrix axes may not share an atlas label: their vector columns are named {atlas}_{group} with no axis component, so a shared atlas would collide. This is checked at spec-load time, before any Hail call.
  • Scheduling is deliberately external: all three commands run in-process, and hvantk never imports a scheduler -- an sbatch wrapper submits them.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Building datasets -- build the per-source datasets this consumes
  • External cohorts -- attach a cohort's own results onto this matrix
  • Re-rank -- re-rank genes using this matrix plus a cohort and labels

docs.title: External cohorts
docs.text: hvantk cohort brings a cohort's own gene-level results alongside the Layer-1 annotation matrix (built by hvantk annotate), without imputing or mixing cohorts. A cohort is declared by a manifest, not by flags: a gene key, a cohort-derived prior statistic (and its direction), and optionally labels and feature axes.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it to fold an external cohort's burden results, or any other gene-level table, into the same gene_id-keyed universe as your annotation matrix -- as a precursor to hvantk rerank, or to inspect a cohort's own coverage on its own.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• A cohort manifest YAML -- see Manifest reference below.
  • The cohort's own table: TSV or comma-separated (sniffed from the header line; gzip/bgzf transparently decompressed), with one row per gene and no duplicate gene keys. It must carry the manifest's key_column plus every column the manifest declares (the prior column and every cohort_axes column).
  • Optionally, a labels pointer: a GeneSetCollection JSON (the format hvantk genesets and its Python API produce).
  • For hvantk cohort burden: a clean, split bi-allelic case/control MatrixTable with genotypes (GT), a gene column, a variant-route column, and a boolean case/control column -- sample and variant QC are upstream of this command, not its job.
  • attach additionally needs the Layer-1 matrix (--layer1, a .ht from hvantk annotate compose) and, when the cohort's key is hgnc_id or symbol or the manifest declares labels, the hgnc:lookup table (--hgnc).

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
# Check the manifest against its table (and labels) before anything reads it
hvantk cohort validate --cohort cohort.yaml

# Join the cohort's declared columns onto the Layer-1 matrix
hvantk cohort attach --cohort cohort.yaml --layer1 out/features.ht --output out/attached.ht

# Originate a gene-level prior from a clean case/control MatrixTable instead
hvantk cohort burden \
  --mt data/cc_clean.mt --gene-col gene_id --route-col route --arm-col is_case \
  --key gene_id --carrier-mode het --output out/burden.tsv --emit-manifest out/cohort.yaml

validate first is the point: it fails on a key column that isn't present, or a declared axis column missing from the table, rather than letting a silently-empty join propagate into the matrix.

docs.title: cohort validate
docs.text:
Option Required Description --cohort TEXT yes Path to the cohort manifest YAML.

Prints the manifest's key, prior, and axes, loads the labels (if declared), and exits nonzero with a specific message on the first thing that doesn't match the table.

docs.title: cohort attach
docs.text:
Option Required Description --cohort TEXT yes Path to the cohort manifest YAML. --layer1 TEXT yes Path to the composed Layer-1 matrix (.ht). --output TEXT yes Output path for the attached table (.ht). --report TEXT no Output path for the report JSON. Default <output>.report.json. --hgnc TEXT only when the cohort key is hgnc_id/symbol, or labels are declared Path to the hgnc:lookup table.

No --overwrite flag: attach always overwrites an existing --output.

docs.title: cohort burden
docs.text:
Option Required Description --mt TEXT yes Clean case/control genotype MatrixTable (.mt). --gene-col TEXT yes Row field holding the gene key. --route-col TEXT yes Row field holding the variant-class "route" (str or array<str>; a variant tagged with several routes contributes to each). --arm-col TEXT yes Column field: boolean case/control, True = case. Must be defined and non-constant for every sample. --key [gene_id\|hgnc_id\|symbol] yes Identifier space --gene-col values live in. --carrier-mode [het\|hom\|chet\|homs_chet] no Default het. See below. --score-field TEXT no Row field with a per-variant score (e.g. REVEL); reduced into mean_score_case. --mtc [bh\|bonferroni] no Multiple-testing correction on the gene-level min-p; adds p_adj. --output TEXT yes Output gene table (TSV). --emit-manifest TEXT no Also write a ready-to-use cohort.yaml stub pointing at --output.

--carrier-mode sets the per-sample "qualifies" rule for a gene (and route): het -- the sample has at least one heterozygous genotype there; hom -- at least one homozygous-variant genotype; chet -- at least two heterozygous genotypes in that gene, in that same sample (a compound-het proxy -- not two different carrier samples); homs_chet -- either of the last two.

For each gene and route, burden counts the cases and the controls that qualify and runs a two-sided Fisher's exact test on that 2×2 table (qualifying or not, case or control). The gene keeps the route with the smallest p-value as minp, with that route's odds ratio. minp is not adjusted for the number of routes tried; --mtc corrects across genes only.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
attach -- the Layer-1 columns, the cohort's declared columns (never imputed: a gene absent from the cohort table keeps missing values), and cohort_tested (true iff the gene had a row in the cohort table), plus label when the manifest declares labels. The report JSON:

{
  "cohort": "my-cohort",
  "n_genes": 20000,
  "n_tested": 180,
  "key": "symbol",
  "key_column": "gene",
  "mapping_rate": 0.97,
  "prior": {"column": "minp", "direction": "lower_is_better", "non_null_rate": 0.009, "positive_rate": 1.0},
  "axes": {"architecture": {"n_case_var": {"non_null_rate": 0.009, "positive_rate": 0.95}, "...": {}}}
}

A labels block (gene_set, set_name, n_in, n_mapped, mapping_rate) is added when the manifest declares labels. positive_rate is null for a declared column Hail typed as non-numeric (one dirty cell, e.g. <0.001 or Inf, is enough -- a warning names the column).

burden -- a TSV, one row per gene (its winning, min-p route): gene, route, minp, odds_ratio, n_case_var, conc, driver_af, mean_score_case, frac_case_private, plus p_adj when --mtc is set. conc is the share of the gene's (and route's) total case-carrier count held by its single most-carried variant -- a within-cases recurrence/concentration signal; controls play no part in it. driver_af is that same top variant's control-carrier frequency (an upper-bound leak signal, not a population allele frequency). With --emit-manifest, the stub's cohort_axes: [{axis: architecture, columns: [n_case_var, conc, driver_af]}] is exactly what hvantk rerank's CaseControlArchitectureAudit looks for -- it flags a gene recurrent_variant when conc >= 0.6 and driver_af > 5e-5.

No --overwrite flag on either command: both always overwrite an existing output.

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text:
Validated against cohort_manifest.schema.json:

name: my-cohort
key: symbol              # or gene_id / hgnc_id
key_column: gene         # the column in `table` holding that key
table: cohort.tsv
prior:
  column: minp
  direction: lower_is_better
cohort_axes:
  - axis: architecture
    columns: [n_case_var, conc, driver_af]
Field Required Notes name yes key yes One of gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol -- the identifier space. key_column no The column in table that actually holds those values. Defaults to key; set it explicitly whenever the table's column is named differently (a symbol-keyed table commonly names its column gene, not symbol). table yes Path to the cohort's own table. min_mapping_rate no Default 0.9. prior.column / prior.direction yes direction is lower_is_better or higher_is_better -- never inferred, since guessing silently inverts the ranking. labels.gene_set only if declaring labels Path to a GeneSetCollection JSON. labels.set_name no Required only when the collection holds more than one set. labels.min_mapping_rate no Default 0.9. cohort_axes[].axis / .columns no Repeatable; each axis label must be unique, and every declared column (the prior's and every axis's) must be unique across the whole manifest.

docs.title: Bridging to hvantk rerank
docs.text:
rerank does not read a cohort manifest's table directly; it takes its own YAML config that points at the manifest and adds the feature axes and labels:

cohort: cohort.yaml        # the manifest above
features:
  - {name: constraint, path: constraint.tsv}
labels:
  path: labels.txt

rerank's config accepts five top-level keys -- name, cohort, features, labels and min_label_coverage (see Re-rank for the full reference); an older config with a top-level prior: block is rejected with a hint to delete it -- the prior now comes from the cohort manifest's own prior: block. The manifest's prior.column is carried through to rerank's output as prior_stat. See examples/rerank for a complete runnable configuration, and Re-rank for the rest of its options.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.cohort.spec import load_cohort
from hvantk.algorithms.cohort.checks import (
    read_header, check_key_column_exists, check_declared_columns_exist, detect_delimiter,
)
from hvantk.algorithms.cohort.attach import attach

manifest = load_cohort("cohort.yaml")
header = read_header(manifest.table)
check_key_column_exists(manifest, header)        # raises ValueError, not click.UsageError
check_declared_columns_exist(manifest, header)

import hail as hl
cohort_ht = hl.import_table(manifest.table, delimiter=detect_delimiter(manifest.table),
                             impute=True, missing=["NA", ""], key=manifest.key_column)
attached, report = attach(hl.read_table("out/features.ht"), cohort_ht, manifest)

attach() itself does not run the checks functions, and does not reject a blank or NA key cell -- the CLI (cohort attach) runs both before calling it. A Python caller of attach() directly should run them too, in this order, or a malformed manifest or table surfaces later as a raw Hail error instead of a clear message.

For hvantk cohort burden's pipeline: hvantk.algorithms.burden.pipeline.run_from_mt(mt, *, gene_col, route_col, arm_col, key, carrier_mode="het", score_field=None, mtc=None) returns the same pandas.DataFrame the CLI writes; hvantk.algorithms.burden.manifest.render_cohort_manifest(*, name, key, table, key_column="gene", prior_column="minp") renders the same manifest stub text.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The cohort table must have exactly one row per gene key; attach raises, naming the duplicated keys, rather than silently picking one row.
  • A manifest column that collides with attach's own reserved output names (cohort_tested, and label when labels are declared) is rejected before any Hail call, as is a declared column that already exists in the Layer-1 matrix -- attach never silently overwrites either side.
  • burden's --mt must already satisfy the clean-input contract (split bi-allelic rows; the given columns present; the arm column defined and not all-one-value for every sample); it fails fast with a specific message rather than computing on dirty input.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Gene annotation matrix -- build the Layer-1 matrix a cohort attaches onto
  • Re-rank -- re-rank genes using this cohort plus features and labels
  • Gene sets -- build the GeneSetCollection JSON a cohort's labels point at

docs.title: EnrichEx: gene-set enrichment and burden testing
docs.text:
EnrichEx tests a collection of gene sets (cell-type markers, pathways, disease panels) in two ways:

  • Overlap (hvantk enrichex overlap): is a gene list, such as GWAS hits or differentially expressed genes, over- or under-represented in each gene set relative to a background universe? One Fisher's exact test per gene set. No Hail needed.
  • Burden (hvantk enrichex burden): in a cohort MatrixTable, is a sample's count of genes in the set that carry a qualifying variant associated with a binary or continuous phenotype? One Hail logistic or linear regression per gene set, with optional variant-class strata and a competitive permutation test. hvantk enrichex burden-pipeline runs the same test over several gene-set collections and variant classes in one pass.

Figure 1. (A) Overlap enrichment with Fisher's exact test. (B) Burden testing with Hail regression, with optional variant-class strata and a competitive permutation test.

docs.title: Query gene list
docs.text: Used by overlap. Plain text, one gene per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped, surrounding whitespace is stripped and duplicates collapse. Matching against the gene sets and the background is exact and case-sensitive, so use one identifier type (symbols or Ensembl IDs) everywhere.

docs.title: Gene-set collection (JSON)
docs.text:
Used by all three commands:

{
  "gene_sets": {
    "Microglia": {
      "name": "Microglia",
      "genes": ["TREM2", "CD33", "MS4A6A", "TYROBP"],
      "source": "Lake et al. 2018",
      "metadata": {"tissue": "brain"}
    },
    "Astrocytes": {"name": "Astrocytes", "genes": ["GFAP", "AQP4", "S100B"]}
  },
  "background_genes": ["TREM2", "CD33", "MS4A6A", "TYROBP", "GFAP", "AQP4", "S100B", "..."],
  "source_description": "Brain cell-type markers",
  "metadata": {}
}
  • Each set needs name and genes; source and metadata are optional. Results are labelled with each set's name field.
  • background_genes is the universe for overlap, and overlap needs it: without it (or with an empty list) the command logs "No query genes found in background universe!" and writes no output. burden ignores the background.
  • The counts that GeneSetCollection.save() adds (n_genes, n_gene_sets, n_background) are ignored when the file is read.

Build the file with the hvantk genesets commands (ClinGen, GenCC, COSMIC, or your own two-column TSV through hvantk genesets prepare; see Gene sets) or from Python (see Python API). The CLI reads JSON only: convert a GMT file with GeneSetCollection.load_gmt("sets.gmt").save("sets.json").

Choose the overlap background deliberately

hvantk genesets clingen, gencc, cosmic and prepare (without --background), and the Python helpers load_gene_sets_from_dict(), load_marker_genes() and GeneSetCollection.load_gmt(), set the background to the union of the genes in the sets. With that background, query genes outside every set drop out of the test, and the test asks how the query is distributed among the sets rather than whether it is enriched genome-wide. For the genome-wide question, use the universe the query was drawn from (for example all protein-coding genes, or every gene tested in the GWAS): pass it to hvantk genesets prepare with --background.

docs.title: Cohort MatrixTable
docs.text:
Used by burden and burden-pipeline: one row per variant, one column per sample.

Field Where Default name (option) Requirement Gene row SYMBOL (--gene-field) Top-level string field, one gene per row, same identifiers as the gene-set JSON. Rows with a missing gene are dropped. Allele frequency row gnomad_af (--af-field) Numeric. Read only when an AF threshold is set. Prediction score row cadd_phred (--score-field) Numeric, such as CADD PHRED or REVEL. Read only when --min-score is set. Consequence row consequence (--consequence-field) One string per row (for example the most severe consequence), matched exactly. Read only when consequences or variant classes are set. filters row Set of strings. Read only by burden-pipeline --pass-only, which skips the check when the field is absent. GT entry Genotype call.

The AF, score and consequence options accept dot paths into structs (vep.CADD_PHRED); the gene field does not.

EnrichEx assumes a QC'd MatrixTable. It applies no genotype (GQ, DP), sample or variant QC of its own. Do that upstream: hvantk hgc filter-qc covers sample and variant QC (see HGC), and genotype filters are one Hail call:

mt = mt.filter_entries((mt.GQ >= 20) & (mt.DP >= 10))

Filtered genotypes and no-calls count as non-carriers.

docs.title: Phenotype table
docs.text:
• A Hail Table (a path ending in .ht) keyed by sample ID, or a TSV (any other path), read with type imputation and keyed by --sample-id-field (default sample_id).
  • The key must match the MatrixTable column key in value and type. In a TSV, numeric-looking IDs are imputed as integers; if the MatrixTable keys samples by string, write the phenotypes to a Hail Table with a string key first.
  • Binary phenotype: boolean, or 0/1. Continuous phenotype: numeric. Covariates: numeric or boolean, so code a categorical covariate such as sex as 0/1.
  • MatrixTable samples without a phenotype value are dropped. Hail's regression also excludes samples with any missing covariate.

burden-pipeline can read the phenotype and covariates from MatrixTable column fields instead (omit -p).

docs.title: How the overlap test works
docs.text:
For each gene set S, with query list Q and background U:

  1. Q and S are intersected with U. n_query = |Q ∩ U|, n_gene_set = |S ∩ U|, n_background = |U|. A set with no genes in U is skipped; if no query gene is in U, nothing is tested.

  2. The 2×2 table is

    In the set Not in the set In the query a = n_overlap b = n_query − a Not in the query c = n_gene_set − a d = n_background − n_query − n_gene_set + a

  3. A two-sided Fisher's exact test (scipy.stats.fisher_exact) gives p_value. A small p-value means over- or under-representation; read the direction from the odds ratio.

  4. odds_ratio is the sample odds ratio ad/(bc): 0 when a = 0, infinite when b or c is 0.
  5. The 95% confidence interval uses Woolf's log method, exp(ln OR ± 1.96 √(1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d)), when all four cells are above zero, and is reported as [0, inf] otherwise.
  6. p_adjusted applies Benjamini-Hochberg (default), Bonferroni or no correction across the gene sets actually tested.
  7. significant is p_adjusted < --alpha.

docs.title: Run overlap
docs.text:
mkdir -p results
hvantk enrichex overlap \
  -g gwas_genes.txt \
  -s brain_cell_types.json \
  -o results/overlap.tsv \
  --generate-report
Option Default Description -g, --gene-list required Query gene list file. -s, --gene-sets required Gene-set collection JSON with background_genes. -o, --output required Output path (see below). --correction benjamini-hochberg bonferroni, benjamini-hochberg or none. --alpha 0.05 Threshold for significant and the console summary. --output-format tsv tsv, json or both. --generate-report off Write a dot plot and an HTML report (see Reports and plots).

docs.title: Overlap output
docs.text:
• tsv writes the table to -o, adding .tsv if missing; json writes to -o, adding .json if missing. For both, give -o without an extension: -o results/overlap writes results/overlap.tsv and results/overlap.json. The directory that holds these files (-o's parent) is created if it does not exist yet.
  • With --generate-report, the report and its plot are written next to -o, in that same directory. The report always reads a TSV: when --output-format wrote one this run, it is reused; otherwise (json only) a copy named overlap_results.tsv is written there for the report to read. Both are refreshed on every run, so rerunning into the same -o never reports a previous run's results.
  • When nothing can be tested, the command prints "No results generated" and writes no file.

One row per tested gene set, sorted by p_value:

Column Meaning gene_set_name The set's name. n_query Query genes in the background (the same on every row). n_gene_set Set genes in the background. n_overlap Genes in both (a). n_background Background size. p_value Two-sided Fisher's exact p-value. odds_ratio ad/(bc). ci_lower, ci_upper 95% CI (Woolf); 0 and inf when a cell is zero. overlap_genes Overlapping genes, sorted, comma-separated. p_adjusted Corrected p-value. significant p_adjusted < --alpha.

The JSON output is an array of the same records; overlap_genes stays a comma-separated string and an infinite ci_upper becomes null.

docs.title: How the burden test works
docs.text:
1. Select qualifying variants. With no filter option, every variant in the MatrixTable counts. Each filter you set keeps a row only when its condition holds:

    • allele frequency ≤ --max-af (no AF filter when unset or 1.0 or more);
    • score ≥ --min-score (no score filter when unset, or 0 or less);
    • consequence in --consequences.

    A row with a missing value for an active filter is dropped. With --max-af, for example, variants that have no gnomAD AF are excluded; fill the field with 0 upstream to keep them. If a filter's field does not exist, that filter is skipped and only a log warning says so.

  2. Decide, per gene and sample, whether the sample qualifies (--genotype-aggregation):

    Model The sample qualifies for a gene when it has hets (default) ≥ 1 heterozygous qualifying genotype. Homozygous-alternate genotypes do not count. homs ≥ 1 homozygous-alternate qualifying genotype. multi_het ≥ 2 heterozygous qualifying genotypes. Genotypes are unphased, so two variants in cis also count; this approximates compound heterozygosity. homs_multi_het Either of the two above (a recessive model).

  3. Sum per gene set. A sample's burden for a set is the number of genes in the set for which it qualifies. With --normalize-by-length, each qualifying gene adds 1/L instead of 1, where L is the gene length in kb from --gene-lengths (genes missing from that file use L = 1) or, without the file, the number of qualifying variant sites in the gene.

  4. Regress the phenotype on burden, one model per gene set, over the samples with a phenotype:

    • binary (--phenotype-type binary): logistic regression with a Wald test (hl.logistic_regression_rows, at most 25 iterations), logit P(case) = β₀ + β·burden + Σ γₖ·covariateₖ. odds_ratio = exp(β), with 95% CI exp(β ± 1.96 SE);
    • continuous: linear regression with a t-test (hl.linear_regression_rows), y = β₀ + β·burden + Σ γₖ·covariateₖ + ε.

    This is a self-contained test: the null hypothesis is that burden in the set is not associated with the phenotype.

Before the regression, gene sets that list fewer genes than --min-gene-set-size are dropped, and so are sets with fewer carriers (samples with burden above zero) than --min-carriers. A set in which no gene has a qualifying variant never reaches the regression and is absent from the output.

p_adjusted applies --correction with m equal to the number of gene sets in the JSON, including the sets dropped above (like R's p.adjust(p, n = m)), so pre-filtering does not lower the penalty. significant is p_adjusted < --alpha. A gene set whose regression does not converge keeps a missing p_value, is left out of the correction, and gets p_adjusted = NaN and significant = false.

docs.title: Variant classes
docs.text:
--variant-classes repeats the whole test once per class, each with its own consequence filter. --consequences is then ignored; --max-af, --min-score and the field options apply to every class. The presets use VEP Sequence Ontology terms:

Class Qualifying consequences Score filter lof stop_gained, frameshift_variant, splice_donor_variant, splice_acceptor_variant --min-score when set missense_constrained missense_variant Always score ≥ 25, whatever --min-score says synonymous synonymous_variant --min-score when set

Any other name is a custom class whose only qualifying consequence is the name itself, for a precomputed grouping field: --variant-classes hcLOF,missC,syn --consequence-field csq_group.

Each class is corrected on its own (m = gene sets in the JSON), not across classes. The synonymous class is a negative control: when any gene set reaches nominal p < 0.05 for synonymous variants, a warning is logged, because that points to confounding (gene length, batch, ancestry) rather than biology.

docs.title: Competitive permutation test
docs.text:
A self-contained test can flag many sets at once when cases carry more rare variants overall, for example after a batch or ancestry difference. --permutation (--competitive in burden-pipeline) adds a test whose null hypothesis is that the set is no more associated than a random set of the same size:

  1. Per-gene qualifying indicators, with the same filter and model as the main test, are computed in Hail for every gene in the MatrixTable and collected to the driver.
  2. The observed statistic is the Wald z (binary, refitted in NumPy with the same covariates) or the t statistic (continuous) of the set's burden.
  3. Each permutation draws a random set with as many genes as the set has in the MatrixTable. Draws are length-matched: genes are binned into up to 10 quantile bins of their carrier count, and each set gene is replaced by a random gene from its bin (with replacement). With fewer than 10 genes in the MatrixTable, draws are uniform.
  4. The empirical p-value is (1 + the number of permutations whose absolute statistic is at least the observed one) / (N + 1), a two-sided test. With --variant-classes the test runs once per class.

The smallest attainable p-value is 1/(N + 1), so choose --n-permutations large enough to pass your multiple-testing threshold. Empirical p-values are not corrected for multiple testing, --min-carriers and --min-gene-set-size do not apply, and run time grows with gene sets × permutations.

docs.title: Run burden
docs.text:
hvantk enrichex burden \
  -m cohort.mt \
  -p phenotypes.ht \
  -s gene_sets.json \
  --covariates PC1,PC2,PC3,PC4,PC5,age,sex \
  --max-af 0.001 \
  --consequences stop_gained,frameshift_variant,splice_donor_variant,splice_acceptor_variant \
  --min-carriers 5 \
  -o results/burden/

Stratified by variant class, with the competitive test and a report, and phenotypes from a TSV:

hvantk enrichex burden \
  -m cohort.mt \
  -p phenotypes.tsv \
  --sample-id-field sample_id \
  -s gene_sets.json \
  --covariates PC1,PC2,PC3,sex \
  --max-af 0.001 \
  --variant-classes lof,missense_constrained,synonymous \
  --permutation \
  --permutation-seed 42 \
  --generate-report \
  -o results/burden_by_class/

A quantitative trait uses linear regression:

hvantk enrichex burden \
  -m cohort.mt \
  -p phenotypes.ht \
  -s gene_sets.json \
  --phenotype-type continuous \
  --phenotype-field ldl \
  --covariates PC1,PC2,PC3,age,sex \
  --max-af 0.001 \
  -o results/burden_ldl/
Option Default Description -m, --cohort-mt required Cohort MatrixTable. -p, --phenotypes required Phenotype .ht, or a TSV. -s, --gene-sets required Gene-set collection JSON. -o, --output required A directory, created if needed, that receives burden_results.tsv; or a results .tsv path, whose directory is created if needed. --phenotype-field is_case Phenotype field. --phenotype-type binary binary (logistic) or continuous (linear). --covariates none Comma-separated covariate fields, no spaces. --genotype-aggregation hets hets, homs, multi_het or homs_multi_het. --max-af none Keep variants with AF ≤ this value. --min-score none Keep variants with score ≥ this value; 0 or less disables it. --consequences none Comma-separated qualifying consequences, no spaces. Ignored with --variant-classes. --gene-field SYMBOL Row field holding the gene. --af-field gnomad_af Row field holding the allele frequency. --score-field cadd_phred Row field holding the prediction score. --consequence-field consequence Row field holding the consequence. --correction benjamini-hochberg bonferroni, benjamini-hochberg or none. --alpha 0.05 Threshold for significant. --sample-id-field sample_id Sample ID column of a TSV phenotype file. --variant-classes none Comma-separated variant classes (see above). --permutation off Add the competitive permutation test. --n-permutations 10000 Permutations per gene set. --permutation-seed none Random seed for the permutations. --normalize-by-length off Length-normalised burden (see step 3). --gene-lengths none TSV with a header row: gene in the first column, length in bp in the second. --min-carriers 0 Drop gene sets with fewer carriers. --min-gene-set-size 0 Drop gene sets that list fewer genes. --dry-run off Print the inputs and settings, then exit without reading the data. --generate-report off Write a forest plot and an HTML report.

docs.title: Burden output
docs.text:
Files go to the directory of -o when it ends in .tsv, otherwise to -o itself:

File Written The -o file, or burden_results.tsv Always; all classes together with --variant-classes. burden_<class>.tsv Per class, with --variant-classes. permutation_results.tsv, or permutation_<class>.tsv per class With --permutation. enrichex_burden.png, enrichex_burden_report.html With --generate-report.

When no gene set is testable, the command writes an empty results file and stops there: no permutation test, no report.

The results table has one row per tested gene set, sorted by p_value:

Column Phenotype Meaning gene_set_name both The set's name. gene_set_size both Genes listed in the set. n_genes_found both Set genes with at least one qualifying variant in the MatrixTable. gene_coverage_pct both n_genes_found / gene_set_size × 100, one decimal. A warning is logged for sets below 50%. beta, standard_error, p_value both Effect of one unit of burden, its SE and p-value. z_stat binary Wald z statistic. fit.n_iterations, fit.converged, fit.exploded binary Logistic fit diagnostics. When the fit does not converge, the statistics are missing. odds_ratio, ci_lower, ci_upper binary exp(β) and its 95% CI. n, sum_x, y_transpose_x continuous Samples used, sum of burden, and Σ y·burden. t_stat continuous t statistic. p_adjusted, significant both Corrected p-value, and p_adjusted < --alpha. variant_class both With --variant-classes.

The permutation tables have gene_set_name, n_genes_tested (set genes present in the MatrixTable), observed_statistic, empirical_p_value, n_permutations and n_exceeded, plus variant_class per class.

docs.title: Burden pipeline
docs.text:
hvantk enrichex burden-pipeline loads the cohort once and runs the burden test for every pair of gene-set collection and variant class. The statistics are those of burden; inputs, defaults and outputs differ.

hvantk enrichex burden-pipeline \
  -m cohort.mt \
  -p phenotypes.ht \
  --gene-sets heart:gene_sets/heart.json \
  --gene-sets brain:gene_sets/brain.json \
  --variant-classes lof,missense_constrained,synonymous \
  --max-af 0.001 \
  --covariates PC1,PC2,PC3,sex \
  --competitive \
  --generate-report \
  -o results/celltype_burden/

With the phenotype and covariates stored as MatrixTable column fields, omit -p and use dot paths; the leaf names (is_case, PC1, ...) are used for the regression:

hvantk enrichex burden-pipeline \
  -m cohort.mt \
  --gene-sets heart:gene_sets/heart.json \
  --phenotype-field phe.is_case \
  --covariates phe.PC1,phe.PC2,phe.sex \
  --variant-classes lof,synonymous \
  -o results/burden/

--max-af, --min-score, --pass-only and the three field options always apply, with or without --variant-classes: without it, the pipeline still makes one unstratified run per collection, named all, using those filters.

Where it differs from burden:

Option burden-pipeline burden Gene sets --gene-sets NAME:PATH, repeatable, required, no short flag -s PATH, one file -p, --phenotypes Optional; when omitted, read from MatrixTable column fields Required -o --output-dir, a directory --output, a file or a directory --min-carriers 5 0 --max-af 0.01 none --min-score Applied as given; leave it unset to disable 0 or less disables it --pass-only / --no-pass-only --no-pass-only; --pass-only keeps rows whose filters set is empty Not available Permutation test --competitive --permutation --consequences Not available; use --variant-classes Available

The remaining options (--phenotype-field, --phenotype-type, --covariates, --gene-field, --genotype-aggregation, --correction, --alpha, --min-gene-set-size, --n-permutations, --permutation-seed, --normalize-by-length, --gene-lengths, --af-field, --score-field, --consequence-field, --sample-id-field, --dry-run, --generate-report) behave as in burden, except that --covariates tolerates spaces after commas. --dry-run prints the run plan without starting Hail or writing anything to disk, in both commands (it still checks that the input paths exist).

Each run (one collection, one class) is corrected on its own, with m = gene sets in that collection. A gene set whose regression fails keeps a missing p_adjusted.

results/celltype_burden/
├── burden_combined.tsv                      # every run, with variant_class and collection columns
├── per_run/
│   ├── burden_<collection>_<class>.tsv      # class "all" when unstratified
│   └── permutation_<collection>_<class>.tsv # with --competitive
├── plots/                                   # created empty
├── enrichex_burden.png                      # with --generate-report
└── enrichex_burden_report.html              # with --generate-report

docs.title: Reports and plots
docs.text:
--generate-report needs matplotlib, from the enrichex extra (pip install 'hvantk[enrichex]'). The report is one HTML file with the plot embedded; the PNG is also written next to it.

  • overlap writes enrichex_overlap_report.html and enrichex_overlap.png: a table of the 20 sets with the smallest p_adjusted, the overlapping genes of each, and a dot plot of those among them with at least one overlapping gene (height −log10 p_adjusted, colour odds ratio, size n_overlap).
  • burden and burden-pipeline write enrichex_burden_report.html and enrichex_burden.png: a forest plot of the 25 sets with the smallest p_adjusted (odds ratio or β with 95% CI) and a table.

Each report opens with an overview that counts the rows whose significant column is true, and ends with a short methods note. The overlap and burden reports also summarise the gene-set collection.

The same output from Python:

import pandas as pd

from hvantk.algorithms.enrichex import (
    generate_report,
    plot_burden_forest,
    plot_enrichment_dotplot,
)

overlap = pd.read_csv("results/overlap.tsv", sep="\t")
plot_enrichment_dotplot(overlap, output_path="plots/overlap_dotplot.png", top_n=25)

burden = pd.read_csv("results/burden/burden_results.tsv", sep="\t")
plot_burden_forest(
    burden, output_path="plots/burden_forest.pdf", format="pdf", phenotype_type="binary"
)

generate_report(
    output_path="report/enrichex_report.html",
    overlap_results="results/overlap.tsv",
    burden_results="results/burden/burden_results.tsv",
    gene_sets_path="gene_sets.json",
    title="EnrichEx report",
)

Each plot function saves to output_path with the extension replaced by format (default png) and returns the matplotlib figure. plot_burden_forest needs ci_lower and ci_upper, which binary results have; for continuous results add beta ± 1.96 × standard_error yourself and pass sort_by="p_value". The other plots are plot_enrichment_barplot, plot_burden_volcano, plot_celltype_burden_heatmap (one cell per gene set and variant class, from burden_combined.tsv) and plot_celltype_forest (one gene set across variant classes).

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: Everything below is importable from hvantk.algorithms.enrichex.

docs.title: Overlap and gene sets
docs.text:
Overlap runs on plain Python, without Hail:

from hvantk.algorithms.enrichex import (
    GeneSetCollection,
    compute_overlap_enrichment_pandas,
)

gene_sets = GeneSetCollection.load("brain_cell_types.json")
query = ["APOE", "CLU", "CR1", "PICALM", "BIN1", "TREM2", "CD33", "MS4A6A"]

df = compute_overlap_enrichment_pandas(
    query, gene_sets, correction_method="benjamini-hochberg"
)
print(df.loc[df["significant"], ["gene_set_name", "n_overlap", "odds_ratio", "p_adjusted"]])

compute_overlap_enrichment() takes the same arguments and returns a list of OverlapResult objects sorted by p_value. Their attributes are the table columns, with overlap_genes as a list and no significant attribute.

To build a collection:

from hvantk.algorithms.enrichex import load_gene_sets_from_dict

with open("protein_coding_genes.txt") as fh:
    background = {line.strip() for line in fh if line.strip()}

collection = load_gene_sets_from_dict(
    {"Microglia": ["TREM2", "CD33", "MS4A6A"], "Astrocytes": ["GFAP", "AQP4", "S100B"]},
    background_genes=background,
)
collection.save("brain_cell_types.json")

load_marker_genes(path, cluster_column="cluster", gene_column="gene") makes one set per cluster from a marker TSV, such as Seurat FindAllMarkers output. GeneSetCollection.load_gmt(path, background_genes=None) reads GMT. GeneSet(name, genes, source="", metadata={}) and GeneSetCollection(gene_sets, background_genes, source_description="", metadata={}) build collections by hand; a collection supports len(), iteration over its GeneSet objects, get(name), names(), save(), save_gmt() and to_dict().

docs.title: Burden
docs.text:
import hail as hl

from hvantk.algorithms.enrichex import (
    GeneSetCollection,
    VariantFilter,
    apply_correction,
    run_burden_analysis,
)
from hvantk.core.utils.hail_context import init_hail

init_hail()
mt = hl.read_matrix_table("cohort.mt")
pheno = hl.read_table("phenotypes.ht")
gene_sets = {
    gs.name: sorted(gs.genes) for gs in GeneSetCollection.load("gene_sets.json")
}

lof = VariantFilter(
    max_af=0.001,
    min_score=None,
    consequences=["stop_gained", "frameshift_variant"],
    pass_only=False,
)
result = run_burden_analysis(
    cohort_mt=mt,
    gene_sets=gene_sets,
    phenotype_ht=pheno,
    phenotype_field="is_case",
    phenotype_type="binary",
    covariate_fields=["PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "age", "sex"],
    variant_filter=lof,
    genotype_aggregation="hets",
    min_carriers=5,
)
if result is not None:
    df = result.to_pandas()
    df["p_adjusted"] = apply_correction(
        df["p_value"].astype(float).tolist(),
        method="benjamini-hochberg",
        n_total=len(gene_sets),
    )
  • run_burden_analysis() returns the regression table without p_adjusted and significant (the CLI adds those), or None when nothing is testable.
  • VariantFilter() defaults are stricter than the CLI's: max_af=0.01, min_score=20.0 on cadd_phred, and pass_only=True. Pass min_score=None and pass_only=False to select by consequence and AF only. Its min_gq and min_dp fields are accepted but the burden functions never apply them.
  • apply_correction(p_values, method, n_total=None) takes a list, not a NumPy array.
Function or class What it does compute_geneset_burden_mt(mt, gene_sets, ...) Steps 1 to 3: a MatrixTable with one row per gene set (gene_set_size, n_genes_found, gene_coverage_pct), one column per sample and a burden entry; None when no set gene has a qualifying variant. logistic_burden_test(mt_burden, phenotype_field, covariates, pass_through), linear_burden_test(...) Step 4 on such a MatrixTable; the phenotype and covariates must already be column fields of mt_burden. compute_per_gene_burden_mt(mt, gene_field, variant_filter) Per-gene MatrixTable with hets, homs and multi_het entries. run_stratified_burden_analysis(..., variant_classes) run_burden_analysis per class; returns a dict of class name to table (with variant_class). build_variant_classes_from_presets(names, base_filter=None) Dict of class name to VariantFilter. Without base_filter: no AF, PASS or score filter, except the fixed score ≥ 25 of missense_constrained. permutation_burden_test(..., n_permutations=10000, length_matched=True, seed=None) The competitive test; returns a pandas DataFrame. BurdenConfig, BurdenPipeline The burden-pipeline engine: BurdenPipeline(config).show_plan() and .run(), which returns the combined DataFrame. BurdenConfig.generate_report defaults to True, unlike the CLI flag. generate_synthetic_burden_cohort(...) A synthetic cohort with planted signal: returns the MatrixTable, a phenotype table with is_case, and the signal gene sets. check_type_i_error(p_values, alpha=0.05, tolerance=2.0) Calibration check under the null: calibrated is true when the rejection rate lies within [alpha/tolerance, alpha × tolerance] and a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of uniformity gives p > 0.001.

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text:
• Overlap is two-sided. An odds ratio below 1 with a small p-value is depletion.
  • Overlap depends on the background (see the warning under Gene-set collection). Fisher's test also treats genes as exchangeable: it ignores gene length and the genes that sets share. The Woolf interval is approximate and can disagree with the exact p-value at small counts.
  • The burden effect is per qualifying gene. odds_ratio (or β) is the effect of one more gene in the set in which a sample qualifies, or of one unit of the length-normalised rate with --normalize-by-length. An odds ratio of 1.5 means each additional qualifying gene multiplies the odds of being a case by 1.5; it does not mean that cases carry 50% more variants.
  • Sparse sets. With few carriers or complete separation the logistic fit fails (fit.converged false, missing statistics) or gives unstable, wide intervals. Raise --min-carriers, merge small sets or use broader variant classes.
  • Self-contained and competitive tests answer different questions. A significant self-contained result says the set's burden tracks the phenotype; only the competitive test says the set stands out from random sets. Check the synonymous class: signal there points to confounding.
  • Gene length. Long genes collect more qualifying variants, so sets of long genes look burdened. Use --normalize-by-length, or rely on the length-matched permutation null.
  • Missing annotations. Active filters drop variants with a missing value. Check n_genes_found and gene_coverage_pct to see how much of each set was testable.
  • Differential QC. No-calls count as non-carriers, so a call-rate difference between cases and controls biases burden. Joint-call and QC cases and controls together, and include ancestry principal components among the covariates.
  • Many strata. Variant classes and collections are corrected separately. When you test several, account for the total number of tests when you report.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Gene sets: build the gene-set JSON (hvantk genesets prepare, ClinGen, GenCC and COSMIC sets).
  • HGC: joint calling and sample and variant QC before burden testing.
  • Ancestry inference: principal components to use as covariates.
  • External cohorts: a per-gene Fisher's exact burden test on a case-control MatrixTable (hvantk cohort burden).
  • EnrichEx examples and the scripts in examples/enrichex/.
  • Running on HPC: Spark settings for large cohorts.

docs.title: Expression analysis
docs.text: hvantk expression inspects, summarizes, and extracts marker genes from expression AnnData (.h5ad) files -- built by the Expression Atlas, UCSC Cell Browser, or CPTAC plugins, or any other gene-keyed AnnData.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• describe -- a quick look at an AnnData's observation metadata (what you can group or filter by) before running anything else.
  • summarize -- collapse cells/samples into a per-group x per-gene pseudo-bulk AnnData, e.g. as a matrix: source for hvantk annotate prepare.
  • markers -- per-group differential expression, written as a GeneSetCollection (see Gene sets) for hvantk psroc / hvantk enrichex.
  • summarize-ucsc -- the same output as summarize, fused with UCSC's own streaming reader so a raw exprMatrix.tsv(.gz) + metadata TSV never materializes an intermediate cells x genes .h5ad.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: An expression AnnData with obs = cells/samples and var = genes, and --group-by / --filter-by naming columns that exist in obs. summarize and markers require var to be gene-keyed (adata.var.index.name must not be "transcript_id"); describe only inspects, so it never refuses -- it just labels the variable axis "transcripts" instead of "genes" for a transcript-keyed file. summarize-ucsc takes the UCSC raw files directly instead: -e (exprMatrix.tsv[.gz]) and -m (the cell metadata TSV).

docs.title: The expression extra
docs.text: describe and summarize-ucsc work on a base install. summarize and markers need scanpy -- install the expression extra (see Installation) -- and it does not install on Intel macOS (llvmlite ships no x86_64 macOS wheel); run them on Linux, Apple Silicon, or the cluster instead.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
# Inspect what you can group or filter by
hvantk expression describe -m data/heart_sc.h5ad

# Collapse into a per-cell-type summary
hvantk expression summarize \
  -m data/heart_sc.h5ad \
  --group-by cell_type \
  -o out/heart_celltype_summary.h5ad

# Extract Wilcoxon marker genes per cell type
hvantk expression markers \
  -m data/heart_sc.h5ad \
  --group-by cell_type \
  --top-n 200 \
  -o out/heart_markers.json

# Same shape as `summarize`, streamed straight from UCSC's raw files
hvantk expression summarize-ucsc \
  -e data/exprMatrix.tsv.gz -m data/meta.tsv \
  --group-by Class \
  -o out/class_summary.h5ad

docs.title: expression describe
docs.text:
Option Required Description -m, --matrix-table PATH yes Path to an expression AnnData (.h5ad).

Prints n_obs/n_vars and, per obs column, its dtype plus (for a categorical column) its level count or (for a numeric column) its min/max. Uses a pre-computed adata.uns["column_summary"] when present (instant); otherwise computes it on the fly.

docs.title: expression summarize
docs.text: Option Required Description -m, --matrix-table PATH yes Path to an expression AnnData (.h5ad). --group-by TEXT yes, repeatable obs field(s) to group by. --filter-by TEXT no, repeatable FIELD=VALUE; a cell/sample is kept only if obs[FIELD] equals (one of) the given value(s) -- exact match, not substring. --min-cells INTEGER no Drop groups with fewer cells. Default 10. -o, --output PATH yes Must end in .h5ad. --overwrite no Without it, an existing --output is a hard error.

docs.title: expression markers
docs.text: Option Required Description -m, --matrix-table PATH yes Path to an expression AnnData (.h5ad). --group-by TEXT yes A single obs field for differential expression. --filter-by TEXT no, repeatable FIELD=VALUE, as above. --method [wilcoxon\|t-test\|t-test_overestim_var\|logreg] no Passed to scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups. Default wilcoxon. --top-n INTEGER no Maximum markers per group. Default 200. -o, --output PATH yes .json or .gmt. --results-tsv PATH no Also save the full per-gene results table. --overwrite no Without it, an existing --output is a hard error.

docs.title: expression summarize-ucsc
docs.text: Option Required Description -e, --expression-matrix PATH yes UCSC expression TSV (plain or gzipped). -m, --metadata PATH yes UCSC cell metadata TSV. --group-by TEXT yes, repeatable Metadata column(s) to group by. --filter-by TEXT no, repeatable FIELD=VALUE, as above (against the metadata). --min-cells INTEGER no Drop groups with fewer cells. Default 10. --gene-column TEXT no Default gene. --delimiter TEXT no Default tab. --split-gene-field / --no-split-gene-field no Default on: split a pipe-delimited UCSC gene label (e.g. A\|B) into one row per gene. -o, --output PATH yes Must end in .h5ad. --overwrite no Without it, an existing --output is a hard error.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
summarize / summarize-ucsc write an AnnData shaped (n_groups, n_genes) with layers mean, sum, count_nonzero, fraction_expressed, and obs["n_cells"] holding the per-group cell count. Multi-field --group-by joins group labels with _. summarize-ucsc's output has the same schema, so downstream consumers don't need to branch on which command produced it.

markers writes a GeneSetCollection (one GeneSet per group, the top --top-n genes by the chosen method) as .json or .gmt -- see Gene sets for the format. With --results-tsv, the full scanpy.get.rank_genes_groups_df table is also written.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.core.io.anndata_io import load_anndata
from hvantk.algorithms.expression.matrix_utils import describe_expression_ad, summarize_expression_ad

adata = load_anndata("data/heart_sc.h5ad")
info = describe_expression_ad(adata)  # {"n_obs", "n_vars", "fields": [...]}

summary = summarize_expression_ad(
    adata, group_by=["cell_type"], filter_by={"region": "LV"}, min_cells_per_group=10,
)  # raises TranscriptKeyedError / ImportError exactly as the CLI does

filter_by_metadata_ad(adata, filters) (same module) is the standalone pre-filter markers applies before ranking. require_scanpy() returns the scanpy module or raises ImportError naming the expression extra; summarize_expression_ad and the CLI both call it, so the message is identical either way.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• --filter-by/--group-by values are matched exactly against obs/metadata values as strings; there is no substring or regex mode.
  • summarize/summarize-ucsc drop any cell with a missing value in a --group-by column before aggregating (logged, not an error) -- otherwise it would form a literal "nan" group.
  • A transcript-keyed AnnData (from an Expression Atlas build without --plugin-arg level=gene) is refused by summarize and markers, with the rebuild command in the error message; describe still works, labeling the axis "transcripts". See Data Sources for the expression-atlas:dataset acquisition details.
  • --min-cells is applied after aggregation, not as a pre-filter on raw cells.
