docs.title: Gene sets
docs.text: hvantk genesets extracts or prepares GeneSetCollection JSON files: named sets of genes with a shared background universe. Three subcommands (clingen, gencc, cosmic) extract sets from a curated gene-disease table you've already built; prepare converts a plain-text gene panel into the same format.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use it whenever an analysis tool needs a gene set as input rather than a single annotation column: hvantk psroc's --gene-sets, hvantk enrichex's burden -s / overlap -s, or a cohort manifest's labels.gene_set.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• clingen / gencc / cosmic each take --ht, the provider's built gene-disease table (hvantk reprocess clingen:gene-disease / gencc:submissions / cosmic-cgc:submissions).
  • prepare takes -i, a headerless two-column TSV: gene_set_name<TAB>gene_symbol, one membership per line (# comments and blank lines ignored). It expects HGNC-style human gene symbols -- see Caveats.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
# Extract ClinGen gene sets by Gene Curation Expert Panel
hvantk genesets clingen \
  --ht out/clingen_gene_disease.ht \
  --group-by gcep --min-genes 20 \
  -o out/clingen_gcep.json

# Convert a plain panel TSV, validating symbols against HGNC
hvantk genesets prepare \
  -i panels.tsv -o out/panels.json \
  --hgnc out/hgnc_lookup.ht --export-gmt out/panels.gmt

docs.title: Options reference
docs.text: All four subcommands share -o, --output PATH (.json or .gmt; .gmt loses the metadata JSON carries) and --overwrite (without it, an existing output is a hard error).

docs.title: genesets clingen / gencc / cosmic
docs.text:
Option Required Description --ht PATH yes The provider's built gene-disease table. --group-by [...] no clingen: gcep (default), disease, keyword. gencc: submitter (default), disease, keyword. cosmic: tumour-type (default), role, tissue, keyword. --min-classification [...] no clingen: Definitive/Strong/Moderate (default)/Limited/Disputed/Refuted. gencc: Definitive/Strong/Moderate (default)/Supportive/Limited/Disputed Evidence/Refuted Evidence. cosmic: Tier 1 (default) / Tier 2. --mutation-context [somatic\|germline\|both] cosmic only Default both. --min-genes INTEGER no Drop groups below this size. Default 0. --categories-json PATH only with --group-by keyword JSON mapping a category name to a list of disease-label keywords (passed to aggregate_by_disease_category).

--group-by gcep/submitter/tumour-type/role/tissue groups directly on the table's own field; disease groups on each individual disease label; keyword aggregates diseases into the categories you declare.

docs.title: genesets prepare
docs.text: Option Required Description -i, --input PATH yes The panel TSV. --hgnc PATH no A built HGNC Hail Table (.ht) for symbol validation and alias resolution. --min-genes INTEGER no Drop gene sets below this size, after HGNC validation. Default 0. --background PATH no Text file, one symbol per line; default is the union of genes across all sets. --export-gmt PATH no Also write a .gmt alongside the JSON.

docs.title: The GeneSetCollection JSON format
docs.text:
Verified against hvantk/core/utils/gene_sets.py (GeneSetCollection.to_dict/from_dict):

{
  "gene_sets": {
    "T_cell": {"name": "T_cell", "genes": ["CD3D", "CD3E", "CD3G"], "source": "...", "n_genes": 3, "metadata": {}}
  },
  "background_genes": ["CD19", "CD3D", "CD3E", "CD3G", "CD79A", "CD79B"],
  "n_gene_sets": 1,
  "n_background": 6,
  "source_description": "...",
  "metadata": {}
}

genes and background_genes are always sorted lists, for a reproducible diff. The clingen/gencc/cosmic extractors and prepare all set each GeneSet.source and the collection's source_description to the same string (e.g. clingen_gcep); the extractors always default background_genes to the union of genes across the sets they produced -- only prepare --background lets you supply an external universe. prepare additionally stamps metadata with created_by, input_file, hgnc_validated, and (when --hgnc was given) aliases_resolved / unrecognized_symbols.

docs.title: GMT export
docs.text: .gmt is <set_name><TAB><description><TAB><gene1><TAB><gene2>..., one line per set, sorted by name; description is a chosen metadata field or the set's source, empty string if neither is set. GMT has no field for the background universe or collection metadata -- round-tripping through .gmt loses both (load_gmt's background then defaults to the union of genes in the file, same rule as the JSON path).

docs.title: HGNC validation
docs.text: prepare --hgnc classifies every symbol as canonical, a resolvable alias/previous symbol (rewritten to the canonical form, de-duplicating within its set), or unrecognized (kept as-is, with a warning -- it will not match any gene downstream). Without --hgnc, prepare still hard-rejects a symbol it can tell isn't a human gene symbol at all before writing anything (see Caveats); it just skips alias resolution.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text: Consumer How hvantk psroc --gene-sets <collection.json> hvantk enrichex burden / overlap -s <collection.json> hvantk cohort a manifest's labels.gene_set (see External cohorts) hvantk expression markers produces one (see Expression analysis)

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.core.utils.geneset_io import parse_geneset_tsv, validate_with_catalog
from hvantk.core.utils.gene_sets import load_gene_sets_from_dict, GeneSetCollection
from hvantk.skills.hgnc.streamers import HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer

result = parse_geneset_tsv("panels.tsv")        # ParseResult(gene_sets, warnings, ...)

catalog = HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer.from_path("out/hgnc_lookup.ht")
vr = validate_with_catalog(result.gene_sets, catalog)  # ValidationResult

collection = load_gene_sets_from_dict(vr.gene_sets, source="prepare-geneset")
collection.save("panels.json")
collection.save_gmt("panels.gmt")

reloaded = GeneSetCollection.load("panels.json")  # or .load_gmt(...)

parse_geneset_tsv and validate_with_catalog live in hvantk.core.utils.geneset_io; everything else -- GeneSet, GeneSetCollection, load_gene_sets_from_dict, load_gene_set (a plain-text single set), load_gene_sets (format-sniffing .json/.gmt loader), load_marker_genes, extract_marker_gene_sets -- lives in hvantk.core.utils.gene_sets.

docs.title: The ClinGen / GenCC streamer exports
docs.text:
The query/aggregation base class (hvantk.core.streamers.gene_disease_table.GeneDiseaseTableStreamer) backs ClinGenGeneDiseaseTableStreamer, GenCCGeneDiseaseTableStreamer, and CosmicCGCGeneDiseaseTableStreamer alike, so export_for_enrichex, to_gene_set, and ID translation work the same way regardless of provider:

from hvantk.skills.clingen.streamers import ClinGenGeneDiseaseTableStreamer

streamer = ClinGenGeneDiseaseTableStreamer("out/clingen_gene_disease.ht")

definitive = streamer.get_genes_by_classification("Definitive")

cancer_genes = streamer.get_genes_by_disease(
    ["cancer", "carcinoma", "tumor"], match_mode="contains", min_classification="Moderate",
)

stats = streamer.compute_stats()
summary = streamer.classification_summary()

streamer.export_for_enrichex("out/clingen_gene_sets.json", min_classification="Moderate")

# Translate to Ensembl gene IDs using the HGNC catalog
from hvantk.skills.hgnc.streamers import HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer

catalog = HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer.from_path("out/hgnc_lookup.ht")
ensembl_ids = streamer.get_genes_by_classification(
    min_classification="Definitive", gene_catalog=catalog, output_id_type="ensembl_gene_id",
)
hgnc_ids = streamer.to_gene_set(
    min_classification="Moderate", gene_catalog=catalog, output_id_type="hgnc_id",
)

GenCC's provider-specific grouping is by submitter instead of GCEP:

from hvantk.skills.gencc.streamers import GenCCGeneDiseaseTableStreamer

streamer = GenCCGeneDiseaseTableStreamer("out/gencc_submissions.ht")
by_submitter = streamer.get_geneset_per_submitter(min_classification="Moderate", min_genes=20)
consensus = streamer.consensus_genes(min_submitters=2)  # genes >=2 submitters agree on

output_id_type accepts whatever the gene_catalog you pass supports; for HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer that is hgnc_id, gene_symbol, ensembl_gene_id, entrez_id, or uniprot_id.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• hvantk.core.models.GeneSet (one of the four dataset types) is unrelated to GeneSetCollection's GeneSet (hvantk.core.utils.gene_sets.GeneSet), despite the shared name. Everything on this page is the latter. No in-tree plugin currently builds the dataset-type GeneSet (.geneset.json).
  • prepare (with or without --hgnc) hard-rejects a panel containing Ensembl gene or transcript IDs, bare numeric (Entrez-looking) tokens, or whitespace inside a symbol, and rejects the whole file if more than half of its unique symbols look like mouse gene symbols (Abc1-shaped) -- it is a human-HGNC-symbol format, not a general identifier container.
  • --group-by keyword (on any of clingen/gencc/cosmic) requires --categories-json; without it the command exits before touching the table. On cosmic, --mutation-context applies in every --group-by mode, including keyword.

docs.title: HGC: joint genotyping
docs.text:
HGC (Hail-based Genotype Combiner) joint-genotypes a cohort of per-sample gVCFs: it combines them into a Variant DataSet (VDS), converts that to a MatrixTable (MT), runs quality control, and exports a cohort VCF. It is built on Hail.

Figure 1. HGC: gVCF combining, VDS to MatrixTable conversion, sample and variant QC, optional filtering, and cohort VCF export.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
Entry point Use it when hvantk hgc pipeline You have a directory of gVCFs and want VDS → MT → cohort VCF with QC tables in one command; you can resume it by hand from the stage outputs. Individual commands (gvcf-combine, vds-combine, vds2mt, mt2vcf, compute-qc, filter-qc, qc-report, qc-summary) You already have a VDS or MT, want QC filter thresholds the pipeline doesn't expose (see Filter by QC metrics), or want to rerun a single stage without re-running the rest.

Every command takes -h/--help. Every command except qc-summary, which reads text files and never starts Hail, also takes --dry-run: it prints what the command would do without starting Hail.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. gVCFs -> VDS -> MatrixTable -> cohort VCF
hvantk hgc pipeline -i /path/to/gvcfs -o /path/to/output

# 2. QC the MatrixTable the pipeline produced, and build an HTML report.
#    compute-qc's -o is an output DIRECTORY (see "Compute QC metrics" below).
hvantk hgc compute-qc -i /path/to/output/cohort.mt -o /path/to/output/qc
hvantk hgc qc-report -i /path/to/output/qc/qc_metrics_with_qc.mt \
    -o /path/to/output/qc/report.html

Preview either command's plan first with --dry-run. For a region-restricted run (a single chromosome, an exome, a gene panel), see Performance and sizing before running the combine step — the default partitioning is sized for whole genomes and can leave most of your cores idle on a smaller region.

docs.title: Combine gVCFs into a VDS
docs.text:
hvantk hgc gvcf-combine -g /data/gvcfs -o cohort.vds
Option Meaning Default -g, --gvcf-dir TEXT Directory of .g.vcf.gz files, each with a .tbi index none (need this or -v) -v, --vds-paths TEXT Existing VDS to combine with the gVCFs (repeatable) none -o, --output TEXT Output VDS path required --temp-dir, --tmp TEXT Temporary directory for intermediate files $HGC_TEMP_DIR, else the system temp dir -s, --save-path TEXT Where to save the combiner's execution plan (JSON) <output>.plan --import-interval-size INT Interval size in bp; Hail derives one partition per interval Hail's genome default, 1.2 Mb --use-genome-default-intervals Explicit genome interval size (1.2 Mb) already the default --use-exome-default-intervals Hail's exome interval size (60 Mb) off --gvcf-batch-size INT gVCFs merged per tree-merge batch Hail default, 50 --branch-factor INT Branch factor of the hierarchical merge Hail default, 100 --dry-run Preview without executing off

--import-interval-size, --use-genome-default-intervals and --use-exome-default-intervals are mutually exclusive. See Performance and sizing for when to change the interval size.

docs.title: Combine VDS datasets
docs.text:
Merge several VDS directories (for example, per-batch VDSes from incremental cohort building — see Worked examples):

hvantk hgc vds-combine -i /data/vds_datasets -o merged.vds
Option Meaning Default -i, --input-dir TEXT Directory containing VDS subdirectories (each ending in .vds) required -o, --output TEXT Output path for the merged VDS required --validate / --no-validate Validate the merged VDS with Hail's validator validate --overwrite / --no-overwrite Overwrite existing output no-overwrite --dry-run Preview without executing off

docs.title: Convert a VDS to a MatrixTable
docs.text:
hvantk hgc vds2mt -i cohort.vds -o cohort.mt --adjust-genotypes
Option Meaning Default -i, --input TEXT Input VDS required -o, --output TEXT Output MatrixTable path required --adjust-genotypes / --no-adjust-genotypes Annotate the adj entry field (see adjusted-genotype thresholds) adjust --skip-split-multi Skip the VDS-level multi-allelic split off (split runs) --skip-validation Skip the biallelic audit and genotype repair (see below) off --skip-keying-by-cols Keep the VDS's own column order instead of keying and sorting columns by sample ID off --overwrite / --no-overwrite Overwrite existing output no-overwrite --n-partitions INT Coalesce the dense MatrixTable to this many partitions before writing (reduces only) keep the VDS's own layout --dry-run Preview without executing off

Two things worth knowing before you reach for --skip-validation or --n-partitions:

  • The densify runs exactly once. Hail is lazy and does not cache, so any eager action on the dense MatrixTable (a count, an aggregate) re-executes the whole densify. vds2mt is written so that only the final write touches the dense matrix: the biallelic audit (out-of-bounds GT indices, AD length mismatches) runs on the sparse variant data before densification, and the repair is a lazy expression that fuses into the write. The audit is cheap (it scans only the sparse records), so there is rarely a reason to skip it.
  • --n-partitions matters more as your cohort grows. A VDS's on-disk layout is derived from its reference-block count, which saturates as sample count grows, while the dense matrix keeps growing. Past that point the VDS's partition count stops tracking the size of what it partitions, and tasks get too thin to amortise overhead. Size --n-partitions from the dense matrix you're producing, not the VDS.

Also: VDS-level splitting already produces biallelic GT/AD, so there is no manual LGT→GT downcoding step to worry about. Adjusted-genotype annotation needs no extra dependency — annotate_adj is ported from gnomAD's gnomad_methods (MIT) into hvantk/algorithms/hgc/adj.py, with gnomAD's published thresholds kept verbatim.

docs.title: Export a MatrixTable to VCF
docs.text:
hvantk hgc mt2vcf -i cohort.mt -o cohort.vcf.bgz --min-ac 1
Option Meaning Default -i, --input TEXT Input MatrixTable required -o, --output TEXT Output VCF path — use .vcf.bgz (block gzip), not .vcf.gz required --filter-adj / --no-filter-adj Keep only adj genotypes (recommended) filter --min-ac INT Minimum alternate allele count 1 --split-multi / --no-split-multi Split multi-allelic variants if not already split split --check-adj / --no-check-adj Verify adj is not systematically MISSING before filtering check --dry-run Preview without executing off

Use .vcf.bgz: block gzip is what bcftools, tabix and GATK expect, and mt2vcf warns if you give it a plain .vcf.gz path. Keep --check-adj on: Hail's filter_entries treats a MISSING adj as not-passing, so if adj were ever systematically missing (for example, from a MatrixTable built before a dependent field like DP was reliably populated), --filter-adj would silently delete genotypes instead of failing loudly. --check-adj catches that before it happens.

The exported VCF carries standard INFO fields: AF, AC, AN, and call_rate (fraction of samples with a called genotype).

docs.title: Run the full pipeline
docs.text:
hvantk hgc pipeline -i /data/gvcfs -o /data/output --output-prefix cohort

Stages (each can be skipped independently):

  1. Combine gVCFs → VDS
  2. Convert VDS → MatrixTable
  3. Compute sample QC metrics
  4. Compute variant QC metrics
  5. Export → cohort VCF

Required

Option Meaning -i, --input-dir PATH Directory of gVCF files (must exist) -o, --output-dir PATH Output directory

Stage control and combiner/conversion tuning (same meaning as the matching gvcf-combine/vds2mt options above)

Option Meaning Default --skip-combine-gvcfs Skip stage 1 (needs --vds-path) off --skip-vds-to-mt Skip stage 2 (needs --mt-path) off --skip-compute-sample-qc Skip stage 3 off --skip-compute-variant-qc Skip stage 4 off --skip-export-pvcf Skip stage 5 off --skip-validation Skip vds2mt's biallelic audit and repair off --vds-path PATH Existing VDS to resume from - --mt-path PATH Existing MatrixTable to resume from - --import-interval-size / --use-exome-default-intervals / --gvcf-batch-size / --branch-factor Stage-1 combiner tuning see gvcf-combine --n-partitions INT Stage-2 MatrixTable partition count keep the VDS's layout

Processing and output

Option Meaning Default --reference-genome [GRCh37\|GRCh38] Reference build GRCh38 --tmp-dir PATH Temporary directory system default --overwrite Overwrite existing output files off --output-prefix TEXT Prefix for every output file cohort --apply-qc-filters Filter before exporting the cohort VCF and write <prefix>_filtered.mt (see below) off --min-sample-call-rate FLOAT Sample call-rate threshold (used only with --apply-qc-filters) 0.85 --min-variant-call-rate FLOAT Variant call-rate threshold (used only with --apply-qc-filters) 0.85 --generate-qc-report Generate an HTML QC report after computing QC off --dry-run Print the execution plan and stop, without creating files or starting Hail off

--apply-qc-filters drops samples below --min-sample-call-rate, and variants below --min-variant-call-rate, with no alternate allele call (AC < 1), or with a Hardy-Weinberg p-value below 1e-6. The AC and HWE thresholds are fixed; use filter-qc to change them.

--apply-qc-filters and --generate-qc-report read the QC tables stages 3 and 4 write, qc/<prefix>_sample_qc.ht and qc/<prefix>_variant_qc.ht. A table comes from this run, or, when its stage is skipped, from an earlier run in the same output directory; with hvantk -v the log says which. --apply-qc-filters needs both tables: when a skipped stage left no table, the run stops before any stage and names the missing table; to get it, run without that --skip-compute-* flag. --generate-qc-report uses the tables it finds, and logs a warning and writes no report when there are none.

Resuming. The pipeline does not auto-resume: it always runs every stage you haven't explicitly --skip-*'d. .pipeline_state.json in the output directory records what completed and the error, if any, purely for you to inspect — to resume, read it, then re-run with the matching --skip-* flags and --vds-path/--mt-path pointing at the stage outputs that already succeeded:

cat /data/output/.pipeline_state.json

hvantk hgc pipeline -i /data/gvcfs -o /data/output \
    --skip-combine-gvcfs --vds-path /data/output/cohort.vds \
    --overwrite

--overwrite is usually needed on a resumed run, since the stage you're re-entering at will try to write a path that already exists.

A resumed run with --skip-compute-sample-qc --skip-compute-variant-qc reuses the QC tables the earlier run left in qc/, for both --apply-qc-filters and --generate-qc-report.

docs.title: Compute QC metrics
docs.text:
hvantk hgc compute-qc -i cohort.mt -o qc_results/

-o/--output-dir is an output directory, not a file path — compute-qc writes <prefix>_sample_qc.csv, <prefix>_variant_qc.tsv and (unless --no-save-mt) <prefix>_with_qc.mt into it (<prefix> from --prefix, default qc_metrics). Feed that _with_qc.mt to filter-qc or qc-report — a plain .mt without QC annotations fails qc-report's "No QC annotations found" check immediately.

Option Meaning Default -i, --input TEXT Input MatrixTable required -o, --output-dir TEXT Output directory (see above) required --sample-qc / --no-sample-qc Compute sample-level metrics on --variant-qc / --no-variant-qc Compute variant-level metrics on --call-field TEXT Entry field to call genotypes from GT --prefix TEXT Output file prefix qc_metrics --save-mt / --no-save-mt Also write the QC-annotated MatrixTable save --adj-filter / --no-adj-filter Filter to adj genotypes before computing QC, so the metrics describe the filtered callset rather than the densified matrix off --remove-star-alleles / --keep-star-alleles Drop rows whose alt allele is the gVCF placeholder <*>/<NON_REF> or the spanning-deletion * — not real variants, and on a densified gVCF callset they can be around half of all rows remove --dry-run Preview without executing off

At least one of --sample-qc/--variant-qc must stay enabled. --adj-filter requires an adj entry field (from vds2mt --adjust-genotypes); if the MatrixTable has adj but you don't pass --adj-filter, compute-qc warns that the reported call rate describes the unfiltered matrix, not what you'd actually export.

docs.title: Filter by QC metrics
docs.text:
hvantk hgc filter-qc -i qc_results/qc_metrics_with_qc.mt -o cohort_filtered.mt \
    --min-sample-call-rate 0.9 --min-ac 5
Option Meaning Default -i, --input TEXT MatrixTable with QC annotations (e.g. <prefix>_with_qc.mt) required -o, --output TEXT Output filtered MatrixTable path required --min-sample-call-rate FLOAT 0.85 --min-variant-call-rate FLOAT 0.85 --min-ac INT Minimum alt allele count 1 --max-ac INT none --min-af FLOAT none --max-af FLOAT none --hwe-threshold FLOAT Minimum p_value_hwe 1e-6 --min-mean-dp FLOAT none --max-mean-dp FLOAT none --min-mean-gq FLOAT none --sample-qc-name TEXT Name of the sample QC annotation to read sample_qc --variant-qc-name TEXT Name of the variant QC annotation to read variant_qc --overwrite / --no-overwrite no-overwrite --dry-run Preview without executing off

docs.title: Generate an HTML QC report
docs.text:
hvantk hgc qc-report -i qc_results/qc_metrics_with_qc.mt -o report.html
Option Meaning Default -i, --input TEXT MatrixTable with QC annotations required -o, --output TEXT Output HTML path required --title TEXT Report title Quality Control Report --include-plots CHOICE (repeatable) sample_overview, variant_overview, sample_call_rates, variant_call_rates, allele_frequencies, hwe, titv all seven --dry-run Preview without executing off

The report is self-contained (plots embedded as base64 PNGs). There is no standalone plotting/dashboard CLI; for ad hoc or custom plots, export the QC metrics as pandas DataFrames and plot them directly (see Worked examples).

docs.title: Summarize QC metrics
docs.text:
hvantk hgc qc-summary -d qc_results/ -o summary.md --format markdown
Option Meaning Default -d, --qc-dir TEXT Directory containing QC metric files required --sample-file TEXT Specific sample QC file auto-detected: the first *sample_qc*.csv in --qc-dir --variant-file TEXT Specific variant QC file auto-detected: *variant_qc*.tsv, falling back to *variant_qc*.csv -o, --output TEXT Write the summary here, creating missing parent directories none: print only each file's name, row count and column count --format [csv\|json\|markdown] Format of the -o file markdown

No --dry-run on this command. The statistics are in the -o file only: describe()-style statistics (count/mean/std/min/25%/50%/75%/max) per numeric metric column, not a QC pass/fail. On the pipeline's qc/ directory the variant statistics cover only the 10,000 variants of its preview file (see Outputs).

docs.title: Sample metrics
docs.text: Field names in sample_qc, from Hail's hl.sample_qc: call_rate, n_called, n_not_called, n_filtered, n_hom_ref, n_het, n_hom_var, n_non_ref, n_snp, n_insertion, n_deletion, n_singleton, n_transition, n_transversion, n_star, r_ti_tv, r_het_hom_var, r_insertion_deletion, plus nested dp_stats/gq_stats (mean/stdev/min/max) when DP/GQ are present. hvantk additionally adds flat sibling columns sample_qc_mean_dp / sample_qc_mean_gq (not nested under sample_qc) — these are what filter-qc's --min-mean-dp/--max-mean-dp/ --min-mean-gq filter on.

docs.title: Variant metrics
docs.text: Field names in variant_qc, from Hail's hl.variant_qc: AF, AC, homozygote_count (arrays, one element per allele including the reference), AN, call_rate, n_called, n_not_called, n_filtered, n_het, n_non_ref, het_freq_hwe, p_value_hwe, p_value_excess_het, plus dp_stats/gq_stats and the same flat variant_qc_mean_dp / variant_qc_mean_gq siblings. filter-qc reads the alt-allele element of the arrays (AC[1], AF[1]), so it assumes biallelic data — run after vds2mt's split, not before.

docs.title: Adjusted-genotype (adj) thresholds
docs.text: From vds2mt --adjust-genotypes (hvantk/algorithms/hgc/adj.py, ported from gnomAD's annotate_adj, thresholds kept verbatim): GQ >= 20, DP >= 10 (DP >= 5 for a haploid call), and allele balance >= 0.2 for each called allele on a heterozygous call (homozygous calls skip the allele-balance test).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Data formats

Format What it is On disk gVCF Single-sample calls plus reference blocks .g.vcf.gz + .tbi VDS Hail's storage-optimized format; separates reference data from variant data directory ending .vds MatrixTable (MT) Hail's dense analysis format; rows = variants, columns = samples directory ending .mt VCF Standard variant format, exported by mt2vcf .vcf.bgz (block gzip)

compute-qc output directory (filenames use --prefix, default qc_metrics):

qc_results/
├── qc_metrics_sample_qc.csv     # comma-separated, every sample
├── qc_metrics_variant_qc.tsv    # TAB-separated (alleles/struct fields contain
│                                 # commas Hail doesn't quote); every variant,
│                                 # exported directly by Hail, not collected
└── qc_metrics_with_qc.mt         # QC-annotated MatrixTable (unless --no-save-mt)

pipeline output directory (filenames use --output-prefix, default cohort):

output_directory/
├── cohort.vds/                  # Stage 1
├── cohort.mt/                   # Stage 2
├── cohort_filtered.mt/          # Stage 5, only with --apply-qc-filters
├── cohort.vcf.bgz               # Stage 5
├── qc/
│   ├── cohort_sample_qc.ht      # Stage 3, Hail Table, every sample
│   ├── cohort_sample_qc.csv     # same data, comma-separated
│   ├── cohort_variant_qc.ht     # Stage 4, Hail Table, every variant
│   ├── cohort_variant_qc.tsv    # first 10,000 variants, TAB-separated
│   └── cohort_qc_report.html    # only with --generate-qc-report
├── logs/
│   └── pipeline_<timestamp>.log # the run's log, see below
└── .pipeline_state.json         # inspect this to resume manually, see above

cohort_filtered.mt is written here even when --mt-path points elsewhere. It holds the filtered genotypes, without the QC annotations the filters used.

cohort_sample_qc.csv (every sample, comma-separated) and cohort_variant_qc.tsv use the same names, delimiters and columns as compute-qc's files. The variant TSV is a preview of the first 10,000 variants; the full per-variant table is cohort_variant_qc.ht, and compute-qc exports every variant when you need the text. There is no _with_qc.mt here: unlike compute-qc, the pipeline never writes a QC-annotated copy of the MatrixTable, which would be a full extra write of the whole cohort on every run, since the QC stages run by default. --apply-qc-filters annotates cohort.mt with cohort_sample_qc.ht and cohort_variant_qc.ht, and --generate-qc-report reads only those two tables.

The log holds the messages of every HGC module during the run (stages, QC, combiner, converters), at the level the console shows: warnings and errors by default, and the stage-by-stage progress with the global -v option (hvantk -v hgc pipeline ...).

docs.title: Performance and sizing
docs.text:
Combiner parallelism (stage 1). Hail's gVCF combiner creates one partition per genomic interval, so the interval size caps how many cores can do useful work. The default — Hail's whole-genome default, 1.2 Mb — is sized for whole-genome gVCFs. For a region-restricted run it produces far fewer partitions than you likely have cores:

Input region Partitions at the 1.2 Mb default chr20 (64.4 Mb) 54 chr1 (249.0 Mb) 208 whole genome (3.1 Gb) ~2,584

Keep partitions at roughly 2-4x your core count. On a 128-core run of chr1, lower the interval size so partitions clear that target (600 kb -> ~415 partitions on chr1, ~3x 128 cores):

hvantk hgc gvcf-combine -g /data/chr1_gvcfs -o chr1.vds \
    --import-interval-size 600000

MatrixTable partitioning (stage 2). A VDS's on-disk partition count is derived from its reference blocks, which is a property of the genome and saturates as sample count grows — while the dense matrix you're producing keeps growing. Past that point the VDS's layout stops tracking the data it partitions, and vds2mt/the pipeline's stage 2 keeps using it unless you override it with --n-partitions, sized from the dense matrix you expect, not the VDS.

Memory. Set Hail's driver memory for larger cohorts: export PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS="--driver-memory 32g pyspark-shell".

Storage, as rough ratios of the input gVCF size (not a measured benchmark — actual ratios depend on cohort size, ploidy and compression): VDS ~50-70%; MatrixTable ~100-150% of the VDS; temporary space during combine, 2-3x the input gVCFs.

Actual runtimes vary too much by hardware, storage and gVCF size to state here. examples/hgc/scalability/ and examples/hgc/cpu_scaling/ include benchmark scripts if you want numbers for your own setup.

docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.hgc import (
    combine_gvcfs,
    combine_vdses,
    convert_vds_to_mt,
    convert_mt_to_multi_sample_vcf,
)
Function Returns combine_gvcfs(gvcf_dir, vds_output_path, tmp_path, save_path, vdses, kwargs, reference_genome="GRCh38") None combine_vdses(vdses_dir, output_path, validate=True, overwrite=False) None convert_vds_to_mt(vds_path, output_path, adjust_genotypes=True, skip_split_multi=False, skip_validation=False, skip_keying_by_cols=False, overwrite=False, n_partitions=None) None convert_mt_to_multi_sample_vcf(mt_path, vcf_path, filter_adj_genotypes=True, min_ac=1, split_multi=True, check_adj=True) None

docs.title: QC functions
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.hgc import (
    QCMetrics,
    compute_sample_qc,
    compute_variant_qc,
    compute_full_qc,
    extract_qc_metrics,
    filter_samples_by_qc,
    filter_variants_by_qc,
    get_qc_summary_stats,
    prepare_qc_for_visualization,
    save_qc_metrics,
)
Function Returns compute_sample_qc(mt, name="sample_qc", call_field="GT") MatrixTable compute_variant_qc(mt, name="variant_qc", call_field="GT") MatrixTable compute_full_qc(mt, sample_qc_name="sample_qc", variant_qc_name="variant_qc", call_field="GT") QCMetrics extract_qc_metrics(mt, sample_qc_name="sample_qc", variant_qc_name="variant_qc", max_variant_rows=500_000) (DataFrame, DataFrame) filter_samples_by_qc(mt, min_call_rate=0.85, min_mean_dp=None, max_mean_dp=None, min_mean_gq=None, sample_qc_name="sample_qc") MatrixTable filter_variants_by_qc(mt, min_call_rate=0.85, min_ac=1, max_ac=None, min_af=None, max_af=None, hwe_threshold=1e-6, variant_qc_name="variant_qc") MatrixTable get_qc_summary_stats(qc_df, metrics=None) DataFrame prepare_qc_for_visualization(qc_metrics, sample_metrics=None, variant_metrics=None) Dict[str, DataFrame] save_qc_metrics(qc_metrics, output_dir, prefix="qc_metrics", save_mt=True) Dict[str, str]

QCMetrics (returned by compute_full_qc) holds .mt, .sample_qc, .variant_qc (Optional[hl.Table]), .has_sample_qc/.has_variant_qc, .count_samples()/ .count_variants(), .get_sample_metrics_df(), .get_variant_metrics_df(max_rows=500_000) (subsamples above the row budget — a real dense chromosome can be ~10-11M variants, and collecting every row to the driver has killed real runs; the full table is always on disk via save_qc_metrics/compute-qc), and .generate_html_report(output_path, **kwargs).

qc_results = compute_full_qc(mt)
report_path = qc_results.generate_html_report("qc_report.html")

sample_df = qc_results.get_sample_metrics_df()
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.hist(sample_df["sample_qc.call_rate"], bins=30)
ax.axvline(0.85, color="red", ls="--", label="min call rate")
ax.set_xlabel("Sample call rate")
ax.legend()
fig.savefig("call_rate.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")

docs.title: Pipeline API
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.hgc.pipeline import PipelineConfig, PipelineRunner

config = PipelineConfig(
    input_dir="/data/gvcfs",
    output_dir="/data/output",
    output_prefix="cohort",
    reference_genome="GRCh38",
)

errors = config.validate()
if errors:
    raise SystemExit(errors)

runner = PipelineRunner(config)
runner.show_plan()       # optional preview
state = runner.run()

print(state.outputs)      # {"vds": ..., "mt": ..., "compute_sample_qc": ..., ...}
print(state.errors)

Constructing PipelineRunner(config) creates nothing and does not start Hail, so .show_plan() is a true dry run. .run() creates the output, qc/ and logs/ directories, writes the run's log file, and initializes Hail through the same idempotent init_hail the rest of hvantk uses, so more than one run in a process is safe.

PipelineConfig is a dataclass with every option the CLI exposes (see Run the full pipeline); PipelineRunner.run() returns a PipelineState with .completed_stages, .outputs and .errors, and persists itself to <output_dir>/.pipeline_state.json. PipelineState.load(path) reads that file back, also one written by an older hvantk: it ignores configuration keys this version no longer has. Nothing in the CLI calls it automatically — see Resuming above. PipelineStage is the stage-name enum (COMBINE_GVCFS, VDS_TO_MT, COMPUTE_SAMPLE_QC, COMPUTE_VARIANT_QC, EXPORT_PVCF).

docs.title: Utility functions
docs.text:
Imported from hvantk.algorithms.hgc: validate_vcfs_paths(directory, pattern=None) and validate_vds_paths(vdses) (both -> List[str]), check_path_exists_and_readable(path) -> str, and sort_mts_cols(mts, ref_index=0) -> List[MatrixTable].

Two advanced functions need a direct import from hvantk.algorithms.hgc.combiners rather than the package root: combine_matrix_table_rows(mt_paths, output_path, n_partitions, force_sort_cols=False, overwrite=False, kwargs=None) and combine_matrix_table_cols(mt_paths, output_path, n_partitions, overwrite=False, kwargs=None) (both -> None), for combining already-built MatrixTables by variant or by sample.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Incremental cohort building — combine in batches, then merge:

from hvantk.algorithms.hgc import combine_gvcfs, combine_vdses

for batch in ("batch1", "batch2"):
    combine_gvcfs(
        gvcf_dir=f"data/{batch}",
        vds_output_path=f"output/{batch}.vds",
        tmp_path="tmp",
        save_path=f"output/{batch}_plan.json",
        vdses=[],
        kwargs={},
    )

combine_vdses(
    vdses_dir="output",  # contains batch1.vds and batch2.vds
    output_path="output/merged.vds",
    validate=True,
)

Custom filtering with Hail expressions — when filter_samples_by_qc/ filter_variants_by_qc's fixed set of thresholds isn't enough, filter the QC-annotated MatrixTable directly:

import hail as hl

mt = hl.read_matrix_table("qc_metrics_with_qc.mt")
mt = mt.filter_rows(
    (mt.variant_qc.AC[1] > 2) & (mt.variant_qc.call_rate > 0.95)
)
mt = mt.filter_cols(mt.sample_qc.call_rate > 0.90)
mt.write("cohort_filtered.mt")

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
ValueError: Call field 'GT' not found in MatrixTable entries — raised by compute_sample_qc/compute_variant_qc (and so by compute-qc) when the MatrixTable has no plain GT entry field and no split-dataset LPGT fallback either. This happens if vds2mt --skip-split-multi was used on data that still carries only local allele fields (LGT/LA). Re-run vds2mt without --skip-split-multi, or pass --call-field LPGT if the MatrixTable does carry per-split local genotypes.

Out of memory during gVCF combination or densify — raise the driver memory before running: export PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS="--driver-memory 64g pyspark-shell".

A gVCF's .tbi index is missing — gvcf-combine/pipeline validate every gVCF's companion index and raise FileNotFoundError for the missing one. Create it with tabix -p vcf <file>.g.vcf.gz.

qc-report says "No QC annotations found in MatrixTable. Run compute-qc first." — the input MatrixTable lacks sample_qc/variant_qc columns. This is expected for a plain vds2mt output (feed it compute-qc's <prefix>_with_qc.mt instead) and for the pipeline's own <prefix>.mt, which never carries them either: the pipeline keeps QC separate (qc/<prefix>_sample_qc.ht/variant_qc.ht) rather than writing a QC-annotated copy of the whole MatrixTable. Pass --generate-qc-report to the pipeline itself instead of running qc-report against <prefix>.mt directly.

An exported _variant_qc.tsv doesn't parse downstream (numeric columns come back as strings or empty) — Hail's Table.export formats floats using the JVM's default locale. On a machine whose locale uses a comma decimal separator, call_rate is written 1,0000e+00 instead of 1.0000e+00, and every numeric column reads as text. compute-qc and the pipeline's QC stages both detect this and raise instead of writing a silently broken file; fix it by starting the JVM with -Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US (for example via PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS="--driver-java-options='-Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US'").

docs.title: PS-ROC: pathogenicity score evaluation
docs.text:
PS-ROC measures how well each pathogenicity predictor in dbNSFP separates ClinVar pathogenic variants from benign ones, within a gene list, an explicit variant list, or each gene set of a collection. hvantk psroc joins a ClinVar table with a dbNSFP table, labels the variants from ClinVar and reports, for every score, the ROC AUC with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval, an optimal threshold with its sensitivity and specificity, and how often the score is missing.

Figure 1. PS-ROC stages, from loading the ClinVar and dbNSFP tables to the output files.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input How to get it What PS-ROC reads ClinVar table hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants (downloads the VCF) info.CLNSIG, info.CLNREVSTAT, info.GENEINFO dbNSFP table hvantk reprocess dbnsfp:variants, from a file you download yourself the fields named in --scores Variant scope exactly one of --genes, --genes-file, --variants, --gene-sets see below 
hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants --raw-dir data/clinvar/ --output data/clinvar.ht
# dbNSFP is bring-your-own: put the combined .bgz file in data/dbnsfp/ first
hvantk reprocess dbnsfp:variants --raw-dir data/dbnsfp/ --output data/dbnsfp.ht

Data sources covers the dbNSFP download and the step that combines its per-chromosome files. PS-ROC joins the two tables on (locus, alleles) and does no liftover, so build both on the same reference genome.

Choose the variants with one of:

  • --genes BRCA1,BRCA2,TP53 or --genes-file genes.txt (one symbol per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped): one run over all the genes.
  • --variants variants.txt: one chr:pos:ref:alt per line. A missing chr prefix is added, lines starting with # are skipped and lines without four :-separated fields are ignored. hvantk ptm export-strata writes lists in this format.
  • --gene-sets collection.json (or .gmt): one independent run per named gene set. Gene sets shows how to build a collection from ClinGen, GenCC, COSMIC or your own panels, for example:
hvantk genesets clingen --ht data/clingen.ht --group-by gcep --min-genes 20 \
  -o gene_sets/clingen_gcep.json

Gene symbols are matched exactly (case-sensitive) to ClinVar's. Pass --hgnc data/hgnc.ht (the table from hvantk reprocess hgnc:lookup) to add each symbol's HGNC aliases and previous symbols, and the approved symbol of any alias you list, before filtering.

PS-ROC needs the psroc extra (scikit-learn, matplotlib); see Installation.

docs.title: How variants are labelled and scored
docs.text: The stages run in this order: select variants → review-status filter → labels → join scores → missingness → ROC → outputs.

docs.title: Selecting variants
docs.text: The gene of a ClinVar variant is the first symbol in GENEINFO (BRCA1:672|NBR2:10230 gives BRCA1), so a variant whose GENEINFO lists your gene second is not selected. With --variants, a variant is kept when its contig:position:ref:alt equals a line of the file.

docs.title: Review status and labels
docs.text:
With --min-stars above 0 (the default is 1), CLNREVSTAT is converted to review stars and variants below the minimum or without a review status are dropped. --min-stars 0 turns the filter off. hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants stores CLNREVSTAT as Hail reads it from the VCF: an array split at commas, so criteria_provided,_single_submitter becomes ["criteria_provided", "_single_submitter"]; PS-ROC joins it back into one string with , before the lookup below, so array- and string-typed tables are scored the same way.

CLNREVSTAT Stars practice_guideline 4 reviewed_by_expert_panel 3 criteria_provided,_multiple_submitters,_no_conflicts 2 criteria_provided,_single_submitter; criteria_provided,_conflicting_classifications (or _interpretations) 1 any other value 0

The label comes from CLNSIG (its first element when the field is an array), matched exactly:

  • pathogenic: Pathogenic, Likely_pathogenic, Pathogenic/Likely_pathogenic
  • benign: Benign, Likely_benign, Benign/Likely_benign

Every other value (Uncertain_significance, Conflicting_classifications_of_pathogenicity, not_provided, risk_factor and so on), or no value, gets the label Uncertain/Conflicting. Whatever --min-stars is, these variants stay in the annotated table and are counted as excluded, but they enter neither the missingness check nor the ROC.

docs.title: Scores and missingness
docs.text:
Each variant gets its dbNSFP row by (locus, alleles). Every name in --scores must be a field of the dbNSFP table (names are case-sensitive), or the run stops and lists the fields it found. Any numeric field works, including the *_rankscore columns; common choices are REVEL_score, MetaRNN_score, ClinPred_score, BayesDel_addAF_score, AlphaMissense_score, VEST4_score, PrimateAI_score and CADD_phred.

The dbNSFP plugin stores every *_score field and CADD_phred per transcript. PS-ROC reduces such a score to its most damaging transcript value: the maximum, or the minimum for a score where lower is more damaging (see Score direction).

Variants with none of the requested scores (indels, and any variant dbNSFP does not cover) are dropped and counted as out of scope (n_out_of_scope in the Python result). For each score, the missing rate over the remaining pathogenic and benign variants, the ones the ROC uses, then decides inclusion: a score missing for more than --max-missingness of them (default 0.3; a rate equal to the threshold passes) is left out of the ROC but still reported. Uncertain/Conflicting variants do not count, so a score missing only for them still passes.

docs.title: ROC, confidence interval and threshold
docs.text:
Only pathogenic (1) and benign (0) variants enter the ROC. If fewer than --min-variants of them remain (default 10), PS-ROC logs a warning and writes its outputs without AUCs. Otherwise each included score is evaluated on the variants where it is present, with scikit-learn's roc_curve and roc_auc_score:

  • If the variants where a score is present are all pathogenic or all benign, the run stops with an error.
  • The AUC 95% confidence interval is a stratified percentile bootstrap: pathogenic and benign variants are resampled separately, with replacement, --n-bootstrap times (default 2000) from a fixed seed, so a rerun on the same data gives the same interval.
  • The optimal threshold is a point on the ROC curve chosen by --threshold-method:
--threshold-method Picks the ROC point that youden (default) maximises Youden's J = TPR − FPR closest_to_corner minimises the distance to the perfect classifier (FPR 0, TPR 1) f1 maximises F1 with precision approximated as TPR / (TPR + FPR), which equals the real precision only when both classes are the same size

The threshold is a value on the score's own scale: variants scoring at or above it are called pathogenic, or at or below it for a score where lower is more damaging. Sensitivity and specificity are read at that point, on the same variants that chose it. PS-ROC computes no p-values: there is no DeLong or permutation test for the difference between two AUCs, and no precision-recall curve.

docs.title: Score direction
docs.text:
PS-ROC knows six raw scores where lower means more damaging: SIFT_score, SIFT4G_score, PROVEAN_score, FATHMM_score, LRT_score and ESM1b_score. It evaluates such a score on its negated values, so the ROC, the AUC and its confidence interval are on the usual scale (above 0.5 for a useful predictor), and reports the thresholds on the score's own scale. Each result records the direction in higher_is_pathogenic: variants are called pathogenic at or above the threshold when it is true, at or below it when it is false. The console summary and the dashboard write a lower-is-damaging threshold with <=, for example threshold<=0.050.

Every other score is treated as higher = more damaging. Check the direction of any other raw score you request: one that runs the other way comes out with 1 minus its real AUC unless you set it in score_directions (Python API, see below). The dbNSFP rank scores need no setting: in every *_rankscore, such as SIFT_converted_rankscore, a higher value is more damaging, and the plugin stores it as one value per variant. Their threshold is a rank between 0 and 1, not a cut-off on the predictor's own scale.

docs.title: Run PS-ROC
docs.text:
# One gene list
hvantk psroc \
  --genes BRCA1,BRCA2,TP53 \
  --clinvar-ht data/clinvar.ht \
  --dbnsfp-ht data/dbnsfp.ht \
  --scores "REVEL_score,AlphaMissense_score,MetaRNN_score,SIFT_converted_rankscore" \
  --output-dir results/psroc_brca

# Every gene set of a collection, with HGNC alias expansion
hvantk psroc \
  --gene-sets gene_sets/clingen_gcep.json \
  --hgnc data/hgnc.ht \
  --clinvar-ht data/clinvar.ht \
  --dbnsfp-ht data/dbnsfp.ht \
  --scores "REVEL_score,AlphaMissense_score,MetaRNN_score,SIFT_converted_rankscore" \
  --output-dir results/psroc_gcep

Add --dry-run to validate the inputs and print the plan without running the stages: it does not start Hail, create the output directory, or read the --hgnc table. Stage progress is logged at INFO level, which the CLI hides by default: add the global -v option before psroc (hvantk -v psroc ...) to see it, and --log-file FILE next to it to also write the log to a file.

Option Default Description --genes TEXT Comma-separated gene symbols --genes-file PATH File with one gene symbol per line --variants PATH File with one chr:pos:ref:alt per line --gene-sets PATH Gene set collection (.json or .gmt); one run per set --hgnc PATH HGNC table (.ht) for alias expansion of gene symbols --clinvar-ht PATH required ClinVar Hail table --dbnsfp-ht PATH required dbNSFP Hail table --scores TEXT required Comma-separated dbNSFP field names -o, --output-dir PATH required Output directory --min-stars INTEGER 1 Minimum ClinVar review stars; 0 turns the filter off --max-missingness FLOAT 0.3 Leave out scores missing for more than this fraction of the pathogenic and benign variants (0 to 1) --threshold-method youden youden, closest_to_corner or f1 --min-variants INTEGER 10 Minimum pathogenic + benign variants for the ROC step --n-bootstrap INTEGER 2000 Bootstrap resamples for the AUC 95% CI; 0 disables the CI --output-prefix TEXT psroc Prefix of every output file name --export-tsv off Also write the annotated variants as TSV --no-plots off Skip the plots --dry-run off Print the execution plan and stop

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
results/psroc_brca/
├── psroc_metrics.json        # ROC metrics per score
├── psroc_missingness.json    # missingness per requested score
├── psroc_annotated.ht/       # one row per variant: label and scores
├── psroc_annotated.tsv       # the same rows as TSV (--export-tsv)
├── plots/
│   ├── psroc_roc_curves.png
│   ├── psroc_auc_comparison.png
│   ├── psroc_missingness.png
│   └── psroc_dashboard.png
├── logs/                     # psroc_<timestamp>.log: the run's log, at the console's level (INFO with -v)
└── .pipeline_state.json      # configuration, completed stages, errors and timings

A rerun into the same directory with the same prefix replaces these files.

With --gene-sets, each set gets a subdirectory named after it (characters other than letters, digits, _ and - become _), and its files carry the prefix <prefix>_<set>:

results/psroc_gcep/
├── Hereditary_Cancer/
│   ├── psroc_Hereditary_Cancer_metrics.json
│   ├── plots/psroc_Hereditary_Cancer_dashboard.png
│   └── ...
├── Hearing_Loss/
│   └── ...
└── plots/
    └── psroc_collection_heatmap.png   # AUC per score (rows) and gene set (columns)

The heatmap is drawn when plots are on and at least two sets produced AUCs. A set whose run fails, for example because a score is present in only one class, is skipped with a warning; the command fails only when every set fails. A set with fewer than --min-variants labelled variants is kept, without AUCs.

{prefix}_metrics.json maps each score that reached the ROC to its result (values illustrative):

{
  "REVEL_score": {
    "score_name": "REVEL_score",
    "auc": 0.998,
    "optimal_threshold": 0.454,
    "higher_is_pathogenic": true,
    "sensitivity_at_optimal": 0.98,
    "specificity_at_optimal": 1.0,
    "n_variants_used": 87,
    "missingness": {
      "n_total": 90,
      "n_present": 87,
      "n_missing": 3,
      "missingness_rate": 0.0333,
      "included_in_analysis": true,
      "exclusion_reason": null
    },
    "auc_ci_lower": 0.994,
    "auc_ci_upper": 1.0
  }
}
  • higher_is_pathogenic: the score's direction (see Score direction). true: pathogenic at or above optimal_threshold; false: at or below it.
  • n_variants_used: pathogenic and benign variants where this score is present.
  • missingness: over the pathogenic and benign variants, as in {prefix}_missingness.json.
  • auc_ci_lower, auc_ci_upper: present only when --n-bootstrap is above 0.

{prefix}_missingness.json covers every requested score, computed over the pathogenic and benign variants in the annotated table (values from the PS-ROC example, with 90 of them):

{
  "CADD_phred": {
    "n_total": 90, "n_present": 83, "n_missing": 7, "missingness_rate": 0.0778,
    "included_in_analysis": true, "exclusion_reason": null
  },
  "VEST4_score": {
    "n_total": 90, "n_present": 52, "n_missing": 38, "missingness_rate": 0.4222,
    "included_in_analysis": false,
    "exclusion_reason": "missingness_rate (0.42) exceeds max_missingness (0.30)"
  }
}

The annotated table (and TSV) is keyed by locus and alleles and holds label (Pathogenic, Benign or Uncertain/Conflicting) and one column per requested score, with per-transcript scores already reduced to one value. The plots are 300-dpi PNGs: ROC curves with the optimal points marked and AUC [CI] in the legend, AUCs with CI bars, missingness against the threshold, and a dashboard combining the three with the gene, pathogenic and benign counts. The ROC, AUC and dashboard plots need at least one AUC. A plot that fails is logged as a warning and does not stop the run.

When reading the results:

  • Compare AUCs together with their CIs and n_variants_used. Each score is evaluated on the variants where it is present, so two scores can be measured on different variants (see Caveats).
  • The console summary of a single run prints the variant counts, each score's AUC [CI] and threshold (threshold<= for a lower-is-damaging score), and the scores left out for missingness. "Excluded" counts the Uncertain/Conflicting variants kept in the table.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.psroc import PSROCConfig, PSROCPipeline
from hvantk.skills.clinvar.streamers import ClinVarVariantTableStreamer

config = PSROCConfig(
    genes=["BRCA1", "BRCA2", "TP53"],
    clinvar_ht="data/clinvar.ht",
    dbnsfp_ht="data/dbnsfp.ht",
    scores=["REVEL_score", "AlphaMissense_score", "MetaRNN_score"],
    output_dir="results/psroc_brca",
    # Required: the ClinVar label vocabulary (the CLI passes the same lists).
    pathogenic_labels=ClinVarVariantTableStreamer.PATHOGENIC_LABELS,
    benign_labels=ClinVarVariantTableStreamer.BENIGN_LABELS,
)
pipeline = PSROCPipeline(config)  # validates, creates the output dirs, starts Hail
result = pipeline.run()
print(result.summary())
for name, roc in result.metrics.items():
    print(name, round(roc.auc, 3), roc.auc_ci_lower, roc.auc_ci_upper)

PSROCConfig takes the CLI options as fields (genes, genes_file, variants_path, gene_set_collection, clinvar_ht, dbnsfp_ht, scores, output_dir, output_prefix, min_stars, max_missingness, threshold_method, hgnc_path, export_tsv, generate_plots, min_variants, n_bootstrap), with the same defaults, plus:

  • pathogenic_labels, benign_labels: required; without them PSROCPipeline raises Configuration validation failed.
  • score_directions: {score: bool} setting a score's direction (True = higher is more damaging, False = lower is), on top of the six lower-is-damaging scores PS-ROC knows. The direction picks the per-transcript value and orients the ROC (see Score direction). run_collection() passes it on to every per-set run.

For a gene set collection, pass a dict of sets and call run_collection(). Alias expansion needs a gene catalog passed to the pipeline; hgnc_path alone only records the path:

from hvantk.algorithms.psroc import PSROCConfig, PSROCPipeline
from hvantk.skills.clinvar.streamers import ClinVarVariantTableStreamer
from hvantk.skills.hgnc.streamers import HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer

config = PSROCConfig(
    gene_set_collection={
        "cardiac": {"MYH7", "TNNT2", "LMNA"},
        "epilepsy": {"SCN1A", "SCN2A", "KCNQ2"},
    },
    clinvar_ht="data/clinvar.ht",
    dbnsfp_ht="data/dbnsfp.ht",
    scores=["REVEL_score", "AlphaMissense_score"],
    output_dir="results/psroc_panels",
    pathogenic_labels=ClinVarVariantTableStreamer.PATHOGENIC_LABELS,
    benign_labels=ClinVarVariantTableStreamer.BENIGN_LABELS,
)
catalog = HGNCGeneCatalogStreamer.from_path("data/hgnc.ht")
results = PSROCPipeline(config, gene_catalog=catalog).run_collection()  # {set: PSROCResult}

A PSROCResult holds metrics (score → ROCResult), missingness (score → ScoreMissingness), n_pathogenic, n_benign, n_excluded, n_total, n_out_of_scope, n_genes, scores_included, scores_excluded, max_missingness_threshold, output_dir and annotated_ht_path, plus summary() and to_dict(). A ROCResult holds fpr, tpr, thresholds, auc, auc_ci_lower, auc_ci_upper, optimal_threshold, higher_is_pathogenic, sensitivity_at_optimal, specificity_at_optimal, n_variants_used and missingness; thresholds and optimal_threshold are on the score's own scale. scores_included lists the scores that passed the missingness check, which still get no AUC when the ROC step is skipped for too few labelled variants, so iterate over metrics for the scores that have one.

The ROC functions also work on plain arrays, without Hail tables:

import numpy as np
from hvantk.algorithms.psroc import compute_roc_metrics, plot_roc_curves

labels = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1])  # 1 = pathogenic, 0 = benign
scores = {
    "score_a": np.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.35, 0.8, 0.3, np.nan]),  # NaN = missing
    "score_b": np.array([2.0, 1.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 2.5]),
    "score_c": np.array([0.9, 0.6, 0.7, 0.02, 0.1, 0.3]),  # lower = more damaging
}
results = compute_roc_metrics(
    labels,
    scores,
    threshold_method="youden",
    n_bootstrap=1000,
    score_directions={"score_c": False},
)
for name, roc in results.items():
    print(name, roc.auc, roc.optimal_threshold, roc.auc_ci_lower, roc.auc_ci_upper)
plot_roc_curves(results, output_path="roc_curves.png")

compute_roc_metrics defaults to n_bootstrap=0 (no CI), unlike the CLI. It treats a score as higher = more damaging unless score_directions maps it to False: unlike the pipeline, it does not know the six lower-is-damaging dbNSFP scores. The package also exports compute_all_missingness, compute_score_missingness, filter_scores_by_missingness, find_optimal_threshold, plot_roc_curve_single, plot_auc_comparison, plot_missingness_summary and plot_psroc_summary_dashboard; the collection heatmap is plot_collection_heatmap in hvantk.algorithms.psroc.plots. Each plot function returns the matplotlib figure and, given output_path, saves it as a PNG (the .png suffix is optional).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Circularity. Many predictors were trained on ClinVar or HGMD variants (REVEL, MetaRNN and ClinPred among them), so their AUC against ClinVar labels is optimistic and favours them over predictors trained without disease labels. PS-ROC does not correct for this. The scores: block of the dbNSFP plugin manifest records the training data of most rank scores.
  • Different variants per score. A score that is also defined for nonsense and splice-site SNVs (such as CADD_phred) is evaluated on a different, often easier, set than a missense-only predictor. Because a variant stays when any requested score is present, adding such a score also raises the other scores' missingness. For a like-for-like comparison, request scores with similar coverage and check n_variants_used.
  • Score direction. Only six raw scores are known to run lower = more damaging (see Score direction). Any other raw score that runs that way gets 1 minus its real AUC, below 0.5, unless you set its direction in score_directions or request its *_rankscore instead.
  • Coverage of uncertain variants. Missingness is measured on the pathogenic and benign variants only, so a score that is often missing for the Uncertain/Conflicting variants, the ones you may want it to classify, still passes. Check their scores in the annotated table.
  • Label imbalance. AUC does not depend on the ratio of pathogenic to benign variants, but thresholds do: the f1 method assumes equal class sizes, and a threshold chosen in a gene set dominated by one class may not transfer to another.
  • Small gene sets. --min-variants is the floor for running the ROC, not a sample size that makes an AUC reliable. With few variants per class the bootstrap interval is wide and unstable; check the class counts and the CI before ranking predictors.
  • In-sample thresholds. The optimal threshold and its sensitivity and specificity are chosen and measured on the same variants; validate them on independent data before using them as a cut-off.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Message Meaning and fix Requested scores not found in dbNSFP table A --scores name is not a field of the table. Names are case-sensitive; the message lists the fields found. Score '<name>' has only one class after filtering missing values Where this score is present, every variant is pathogenic (or every one benign). Widen the gene set, lower --min-stars, or drop the score. With --gene-sets, only that set is skipped. Too few labeled variants (N) for ROC analysis Fewer than --min-variants pathogenic and benign variants remain; the outputs are written without AUCs. No scores passed the missingness threshold Every score is missing for more than --max-missingness of the pathogenic and benign variants. Check {prefix}_missingness.json, raise the threshold or choose scores with better coverage. No valid variants found in <file> The --variants file has no chr:pos:ref:alt lines.

docs.title: PTM constraint analysis
docs.text:
hvantk ptm constraint compares the population allele frequencies (AF) of PTM variants with those of non-PTM variants. It stratifies the comparison by the group in which each gene is most expressed (a tissue, a cell type, or any categorical field of an expression dataset), by tissue specificity and by gene constraint. It reports group-level statistics, not per-variant scores.

PTM variants are the site and proximal variants defined by hvantk ptm annotate; see How variants are classified. To fit mixed models on a table you have already split into strata, use hvantk ptm test (Per-stratum mixed models).

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
hvantk ptm constraint \
  --variants-ht data/variants_ptm.ht \
  --expression-source anndata \
  --expression-path data/atlas.h5ad \
  --grouping cell_type \
  --output-dir results/ptm-constraint/

The command needs the constraint extra: tspex computes tissue specificity, and matplotlib and seaborn draw the plots (Installation). If plotting fails, the tables and summary.json are still written.

docs.title: Variant table
docs.text:
--variants-ht takes the Hail Table written by hvantk ptm annotate, or the same rows as a .parquet, .pkl, .csv or .tsv file; a .csv or .tsv may be compressed (.gz or .bgz).

Column Set with (default) Required is_ptm_site, is_ptm_proximal fixed names Yes; a tabular file may omit is_ptm_site Gene identifier --gene-field (gene_symbol) Yes AF --af-field (gnomad_af_genomes) Yes, unless --include-zero-af; then a missing column counts as AF 0 Label --label-field (rf_label) Yes, unless --label-filter all LOEUF --loeuf-field (loeuf) No; without it the factorial table is empty PTM categories --ptm-category-field (ptm_types) No; without it the category table is empty

annotate adds only the PTM fields. Add the gene, AF, LOEUF and label columns to the variant table yourself and pass their names. --label-filter keeps the rows whose label is exactly TN (benign, the default) or TP (pathogenic), the values the ClinVar training-set labelling writes to rf_label; pass all to keep every row.

docs.title: Expression data
docs.text:
--expression-source --expression-path --grouping --expression-metric --min-cells-per-group counts hail-mt MatrixTable directory; values in the entry field x, genes in the first row key A column field mean only Samples anndata .h5ad file with gene identifiers as var_names; values from X An obs column median, mean or median_nonzero Cells tabular Gene × group matrix as .parquet or .pq, .pkl or .pickle, .tsv or .txt, or .csv; genes in the index (the first column of a text file) Required but ignored: the columns are the groups Ignored Ignored
  • With hail-mt, pass --expression-metric mean. The default, median, stops with an error.
  • With anndata, mean aggregates through scanpy, which the expression extra installs. median and median_nonzero (the median of the positive values) do not need it. An AnnData keyed by transcript (var.index.name is transcript_id) is rejected. hvantk expression describe -m data/atlas.h5ad lists the obs fields you can group by.
  • Values are used as stored, without a log transform. Non-numeric values become missing, genes with no value are dropped, the remaining missing values become 0, and negative values are clipped to 0. The matrix must have between 2 and 200 groups.

docs.title: Matching genes and groups
docs.text:
• Gene identifiers are compared after removing version suffixes (ENSG00000141510.17 becomes ENSG00000141510) on both sides. When the two inputs use different identifiers, pass --gene-id-mapping: a TSV with a header row, the expression identifier without its version suffix in the first column and the variant table's identifier in the second. Identifiers missing from the file are kept as they are. Genes that end up with the same identifier are merged, keeping the highest value per group.
  • --group-mapping collapses group labels, for example GTEx tissues into organ systems: a TSV with a header row, the raw label in the first column and the analysis group in the second. It changes only each gene's primary group; tissue specificity and the expression filter still use the original groups. Labels missing from the file are kept.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Load the variants and apply --label-filter. A variant is a PTM variant if is_ptm_site or is_ptm_proximal is true. A missing AF counts as 0.
  2. Aggregate expression into a gene × group matrix. Groups with fewer than --min-cells-per-group samples or cells are dropped.
  3. For each gene, compute τ, the tissue-specificity index of Yanai et al. (2005), with tspex; its primary group, the group with the highest value (after --group-mapping); and that highest value.
  4. Keep the variants whose gene is in the matrix with a highest value of at least --expressed-threshold. With --af-observed-only (the default), keep only variants with an AF above 0.
  5. Each variant takes its gene's primary group, τ and LOEUF, so it belongs to exactly one group.

The first four analyses compare a set of PTM variants with a set of non-PTM variants in the same way:

  • ratio is (median non-PTM AF + 1e-8) / (median PTM AF + 1e-8), and log2_ratio its base-2 logarithm. A ratio above 1 (log2 above 0) means the PTM variants have lower AF. mean_ratio and log2_mean_ratio repeat this with means.
  • p_value comes from a one-sided Mann-Whitney U test that non-PTM AFs are greater than PTM AFs. It needs at least 3 variants on each side and is empty otherwise.
  • n_ptm, n_non, med_ptm, med_non, mean_ptm and mean_non give the counts, medians and means.
Analysis (file) PTM and non-PTM variants compared within A row is skipped when Per-group ranking (per_group_ranking.tsv), sorted by log2_ratio, largest first Each primary group The group has fewer than --min-variants-per-group variants τ quartiles (tau_quartile.tsv) Each quartile of τ over the variants: Q1_housekeeping, Q2, Q3, Q4_tissue_specific The quartile has fewer than --min-variants-per-group variants. The table is empty if τ does not split into four bins τ × LOEUF factorial (loeuf_factorial.tsv) Each cell of two median splits over the variants: τ broad or tissue_specific, and LOEUF constrained (lower half) or unconstrained The cell has fewer than --min-variants-per-group variants PTM category × group (category_group_heatmap.tsv) Each group, comparing the PTM variants of one category with all non-PTM variants of the group The group has fewer than 3 non-PTM variants, or fewer than half of --min-variants-per-group; or the category has fewer than 3 PTM variants

In the category analysis, categories are lowercased, a variant counts in every category of its set, and PTM variants without a category are left out. In a tabular input, set-like strings such as {'phosphorylation'} or phosphorylation;acetylation are split into categories.

The fifth analysis, the within-gene comparison (within_gene_paired.tsv), takes every gene with at least one PTM and one non-PTM variant and computes delta, the median non-PTM AF minus the median PTM AF. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test asks whether the deltas are above 0; it needs at least 3 genes. Its result is in summary.json under within_gene_paired: n_genes, statistic, p_value, pct_genes_depleted (the fraction of genes with a delta above 0, between 0 and 1) and median_delta.

No p-value is adjusted for multiple testing. Quartiles and median splits are taken over variants, not genes, so genes with many variants weigh more.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
<output-dir>/
├── summary.json                    # counts, top 10 groups, rows of the other tables, within-gene test, configuration
├── per_group_ranking.tsv
├── tau_quartile.tsv
├── loeuf_factorial.tsv
├── category_group_heatmap.tsv      # long form: one row per group and category
├── within_gene_paired.tsv          # gene, n_ptm, n_non, med_ptm, med_non, delta
├── plots/
│   ├── per_group_ranking.png       # log2 ratio of up to 25 groups
│   ├── tau_quartile.png
│   ├── loeuf_factorial.png         # needs seaborn
│   └── category_group_heatmap.png  # needs seaborn
└── report.html                     # plots embedded, with the top rows of each table

The first four tables start with their stratum columns (group; tau_quartile; tau_bin and loeuf_bin; group and category), followed by the comparison columns above. A test with no rows writes an empty TSV, and its plot is skipped. The command prints one summary line: the number of variants, groups and genes, and the top group's ratio.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --variants-ht required Annotated variants: a Hail Table directory or a tabular file --expression-source required hail-mt, anndata or tabular --expression-path required Expression data --grouping required Group field: a column field (hail-mt) or an obs column (anndata); ignored for tabular -o, --output-dir required Output directory --label-filter TN TN, TP or all --label-field rf_label Label column --gene-field gene_symbol Gene identifier column --af-field gnomad_af_genomes AF column --loeuf-field loeuf LOEUF column --ptm-category-field ptm_types PTM category column --gene-id-mapping none TSV mapping expression gene identifiers to the variant table's --group-mapping none TSV mapping group labels to analysis groups --expression-metric median median, mean or median_nonzero --min-cells-per-group 50 Minimum samples or cells per group (hail-mt and anndata) --min-variants-per-group 20 Minimum variants per group, quartile or factorial cell --expressed-threshold 1.0 Minimum highest group value for a gene to be kept --af-observed-only / --include-zero-af --af-observed-only Keep only variants with an AF above 0, or also those with an AF of 0

The choices are case-insensitive.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Bulk tissues from a GTEx-style MatrixTable (hail-mt aggregates by mean only)
hvantk ptm constraint \
  --variants-ht data/variants_ptm.ht \
  --expression-source hail-mt \
  --expression-path data/gtex_tpm.mt \
  --grouping SMTSD \
  --expression-metric mean \
  --output-dir results/ptm-gtex/

# A pre-aggregated gene x group matrix keyed by Ensembl ID; --grouping is not used
hvantk ptm constraint \
  --variants-ht data/variants_ptm.parquet \
  --expression-source tabular \
  --expression-path data/gene_by_celltype.tsv \
  --grouping cell_type \
  --gene-id-mapping data/ensembl_to_symbol.tsv \
  --output-dir results/ptm-custom/

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Nothing adjusts for mutation rate. Codons of modified residues may mutate at different baseline rates from other codons.
  • Each gene belongs to one group, the one where it is most expressed, so a broadly expressed gene contributes to that group only.
  • The gene identifiers of the two inputs must match. A join that matches no gene stops with an error that suggests checking symbols against Ensembl IDs.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.ptm import PTMConstraintConfig, run_ptm_constraint

config = PTMConstraintConfig(
    variants_ht_path="data/variants_ptm.ht",
    expression_source="anndata",  # lower case, as on the command line
    expression_path="data/atlas.h5ad",
    grouping="cell_type",
    output_dir="results/ptm-constraint/",
    label_filter="TN",  # exactly "TN", "TP" or "all"
)
result = run_ptm_constraint(config)  # validates the config and writes every output
print(result.summary())
