docs.title: PTM variant classification
docs.text:
hvantk ptm places post-translational modification (PTM) sites on their GRCh38 codons, classifies variants by where they fall relative to those codons, and analyzes the classes. This page covers the sites table, the classification and every subcommand except constraint, which has its own page: PTM constraint. For a run from start to finish, see the PTM example.

Figure 1. From UniProt sites and the Ensembl GTF to the sites table, the variant annotation, the landscape, strata and population analyses, and the report. test and constraint are not drawn.

Command What it does Writes build Maps UniProt PTM sites, plus optional PeptideAtlas and CPTAC phosphosites, to GRCh38 codons Sites Hail Table, mapped TSVs annotate Adds the PTM fields to a variant table Hail Table landscape Compares ClinVar P/LP and B/LB variants at and near PTM sites JSON, PNGs population Summarizes allele frequency by PTM class JSON, PNG export-strata Writes PTM and non-PTM variant lists for hvantk psroc Two text files report Renders the landscape and population results as one HTML page HTML, PNGs test Fits a mixed model of allele frequency on PTM status in each stratum TSV constraint Allele-frequency depletion by tissue or cell type, see PTM constraint TSVs, PNGs, HTML

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• build, annotate, landscape, population and export-strata need only the base install; they run on Hail. build downloads from UniProt and Ensembl unless you pass local files.
  • report, and --save-plots on landscape and population, need matplotlib, which the viz extra installs.
  • test and constraint need the constraint extra. Without statsmodels, test stops with a message that names it.
  • CPTAC sites come from hvantk download cptac-phospho, which needs the ptm extra.

Installation lists the extras.

docs.title: How variants are classified
docs.text:
annotate compares each variant's position with every codon in the sites table. landscape and population run the same step on their input table.

  • A site occupies its codon: the three bases from codon_start. A codon split by an intron is treated as the three contiguous bases from codon_start.
  • The site's window extends --flanking-codons × 3 bp (default 5 codons, 15 bp) beyond each end of the codon. It is counted in genomic bases, so it can reach into an intron, and it is clipped at the contig ends.
  • A variant inside any site's codon is a site variant. Otherwise, a variant inside any site's window is proximal. Every other variant is non-PTM. Site takes precedence, so the two flags are never both true.
  • Only the position counts: every allele at a position gets the same class.

The variant table needs a GRCh38 locus field (the sites table is GRCh38). annotate keeps all its fields and adds:

Field Type Value is_ptm_site bool The variant lies in a PTM codon is_ptm_proximal bool The variant lies in a window but in no codon ptm_distance int32 Distance to the nearest codon in codons, ceil(bp / 3): 0 in a codon, at most --flanking-codons in a window. Counted in genomic bases, so it is not the residue distance when an intron lies between ptm_types set\<str> The ptm_category of every site whose codon or window covers the position, not only the nearest ptm_evidence array\<struct> One struct per row of the nearest site or sites, with source_db, evidence_type, n_observations, uniprot_id, gene_symbol, residue_pos, amino_acid and ptm_type. Added only when the sites table has at least one of these fields; a table from build has all of them

For a non-PTM variant both flags are False and the other three fields are missing. landscape, export-strata and constraint treat site and proximal variants together as PTM variants; population reports the three classes separately.

docs.title: Build the sites table
docs.text:
hvantk ptm build --output-dir data/ptm/ --output-ht data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht

build downloads the UniProt sites and the Ensembl GTF into --output-dir (or reuses them), maps every site to its codon, and writes the Hail Table with the uniprot-ptm:sites plugin builder. hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites builds the same table from UniProt alone (see Data sources); build is the command that also adds PeptideAtlas and CPTAC sites.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Source How build gets it Sites n_observations UniProt (always) Downloads uniprot-ptm-human-<date>.tsv, or takes --ptm-tsv (written by hvantk download uniprot-ptm) Modified residue (MOD_RES) features of reviewed (Swiss-Prot) human proteins, on the canonical sequence 0 PeptideAtlas --peptideatlas-tsv, written by hvantk download peptideatlas-phospho Phosphorylated S, T and Y observed on canonical proteins in one PeptideAtlas build Observations summed over the phosphopeptide forms that carry the site CPTAC --cptac-tsv, written by hvantk download cptac-phospho Phosphorylated S, T and Y quantified in CPTAC tumor and normal samples; tissue_type is tumor or normal Samples with a measured intensity

The UniProt search endpoint has no versioned archive, so a later download can give a different table. Keep the downloaded TSV and pass it with --ptm-tsv to rebuild the same table. A file downloaded the same day is reused.

PeptideAtlas: hvantk download peptideatlas-phospho -o data/ptm/ writes peptideatlas-phospho-<build_date>-<build_id>.tsv and prints its path. A TSV written by hvantk before 0.4.0 over-counts n_observations, and the download reuses an existing TSV, so delete the old file (or pass --overwrite) and download again.

CPTAC: hvantk download cptac-phospho needs --cancer-type or --all. Pass cptac-phospho-<cancer_type>.tsv (tumor and normal rows) or, after --all, cptac-phospho-pancancer.tsv. The -tumor.tsv and -normal.tsv files have the same layout and hold one tissue type each. The -matrix.csv and -metadata.csv files are for the cptac:phospho dataset, not for build.

docs.title: Mapping sites to codons
docs.text:
Each protein maps through one Ensembl transcript from the pinned GTF (Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz), chosen in this order:

  1. xref_mane: a transcript in the protein's UniProt Ensembl cross-references that is MANE Select.
  2. xref_any: the first cross-referenced transcript with a CDS.
  3. gene_mane: the MANE Select transcript of the protein's gene symbol.

A protein with no match is unresolved, and its sites fail. PeptideAtlas and CPTAC rows carry no cross-references, so they map only through gene_mane.

Residue p maps to bases 3p - 2 to 3p of the transcript's CDS, on either strand. codon_start and codon_end are the lowest and highest genomic positions of those bases, so a codon split by an intron spans the intron. A residue beyond the end of the CDS fails. The mapper does not check that the codon encodes the source's amino acid: a site lands on the right codon only when the source protein sequence matches the transcript.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
ptm_category comes from the start of the site's description (ptm_type):

Category Description starts with phosphorylation Phosphoserine, Phosphothreonine, Phosphotyrosine acetylation N6-acetyllysine methylation N6-methyllysine, N6,N6-dimethyllysine, N6,N6,N6-trimethyllysine, Asymmetric dimethylarginine, Symmetric dimethylarginine, Omega-N-methylarginine other Anything else

PeptideAtlas and CPTAC sites are all phosphorylation. UniProt records glycosylation, SUMOylation and ubiquitination as Glycosylation and Cross-link features, which the download does not fetch, so a table from build never contains them.

docs.title: Combining sources
docs.text: Each source is mapped on its own, to ptm_sites_mapped.tsv.bgz (UniProt), peptideatlas_sites_mapped.tsv.bgz and cptac_sites_mapped.tsv.bgz in --output-dir. With more than one source, build concatenates them into ptm_sites_combined.tsv.bgz and builds the table from that file. Rows are not merged: a residue reported by two sources, or by CPTAC in both tumor and normal tissue, keeps one row per report, each with its own source_db, evidence_type (curated for UniProt, mass_spectrometry otherwise), n_observations and tissue_type. The classification pools all rows at a position, so these duplicates change only ptm_evidence.

docs.title: The sites table
docs.text:
The table is keyed by locus, the position of codon_start. Contigs get a chr prefix (MT becomes chrM), rows on contigs outside GRCh38 are dropped, and several rows can share a locus. Its fields are chrom, codon_start, codon_end, strand, uniprot_id (the source's protein accession), gene_symbol, residue_pos, amino_acid, ptm_type, ptm_category, source_db, evidence_type, n_observations, tissue_type and flanking_interval (the codon extended by --flanking-codons × 3 bp). No command reads flanking_interval: annotate, landscape and population apply their own --flanking-codons.

build prints a summary like this one (Resolution counts proteins, not sites):

Sources: UniProt (<n> mapped), PeptideAtlas (<n> mapped)
Mapping complete: <mapped>/<total> mapped (<percent>%), <failed> failed
Resolution: {'xref_mane': <n>, 'xref_any': <n>, 'gene_mane': <n>, 'unresolved': <n>}
Mapped TSV: data/ptm/ptm_sites_combined.tsv.bgz
Hail Table: data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht

A source that maps no site is logged as a warning; it usually means the wrong file. If no site maps at all, build exits with an error and writes no table. Without --overwrite, an existing --output-ht stops the run before anything is downloaded.

Option Default Description -o, --output-dir required Directory for the downloads and the mapped TSVs --output-ht required Sites table to write --gtf-path download Ensembl GRCh38 GTF to use instead of downloading Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz --ptm-tsv download UniProt TSV to use instead of downloading one --peptideatlas-tsv none PeptideAtlas site TSV to add --cptac-tsv none CPTAC site TSV to add --flanking-codons 5 Width of the stored flanking_interval, in codons --overwrite off Download the GTF and UniProt TSV again instead of reusing them, and replace an existing --output-ht

docs.title: Annotate a variant table
docs.text:
hvantk ptm annotate \
  --variants-ht data/clinvar.ht \
  --ptm-ht data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht \
  -o data/clinvar_ptm.ht

annotate writes the fields described in How variants are classified and prints how many variants are site and proximal variants.

Option Default Description --variants-ht required Variant Hail Table with a GRCh38 locus field --ptm-ht required Sites table from build -o, --output-ht required Annotated table to write --flanking-codons 5 Window beyond each end of a codon, in codons --overwrite off Replace an existing output table

docs.title: Landscape
docs.text:
hvantk ptm landscape \
  --clinvar-ht data/clinvar.ht \
  --ptm-ht data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht \
  -o results/landscape/ \
  --save-plots

landscape classifies a ClinVar table (built with hvantk reprocess clinvar:variants, or any table with info.CLNSIG) and labels each variant by its CLNSIG, taking the first value when the field is an array:

  • P/LP: Pathogenic, Likely_pathogenic or Pathogenic/Likely_pathogenic.
  • B/LB: Benign, Likely_benign or Benign/Likely_benign.
  • Any other value counts only in the total, n_variants.

It then computes:

  • Enrichment: the 2×2 table of P/LP against B/LB variants by PTM (site or proximal) against non-PTM. The odds ratio is scipy's conditional maximum-likelihood estimate with its 95% confidence interval; the p-value is from a two-sided Fisher's exact test.
  • Per-category enrichment: for each category in ptm_types, the same test among PTM variants only, comparing the variants with that category against those without it. A variant with several categories counts in each.
  • The P/LP count per category and per ptm_distance (0 means in a codon).
File in -o Contents landscape_summary.json n_variants, n_pathogenic, n_benign; ptm_site and ptm_proximal (P/LP and B/LB counts); enrichment (odds_ratio, ci_low, ci_high, p_value); overlap_by_category; category_enrichment (counts, odds ratio, interval and p-value per category); distance_distribution landscape_summary.png P/LP and B/LB counts per class with the odds ratio, and the P/LP share per class against the overall rate (--save-plots) overlap_by_category.png P/LP count per category (--save-plots) distance_distribution.png P/LP count per distance (--save-plots) Option Default Description --clinvar-ht required ClinVar Hail Table --ptm-ht required Sites table from build -o, --output required Output directory --flanking-codons 5 Window beyond each end of a codon, in codons --save-plots off Also write the PNG plots

docs.title: Population
docs.text:
hvantk ptm population \
  --gnomad-ht data/gnomad_sites.ht \
  --ptm-ht data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht \
  --af-field AF \
  -o results/population/ \
  --save-plots

population classifies a variant table with an allele-frequency (AF) field and summarizes each class. The option is named --gnomad-ht, but any variant table works.

  • --af-field must name a top-level numeric field. gnomAD release tables keep frequencies in the freq array; copy the entry you want into a top-level field first. A row with a missing value is skipped, not an error: it is excluded from the mean/count statistics and from the kept AF sample used for the plot.
  • Non-PTM means every other variant in the table. Nothing restricts it to coding positions, so filter the table first if that is the comparison you want.
  • For each class it reports the variant count and mean AF, and for site variants the number with an AF of exactly 0. It runs no statistical test.
  • It keeps up to 5,000 AF values per class for the plot. These are an arbitrary subset, not a random sample.
File in -o Contents population_summary.json n_variants, n_ptm_site, n_ptm_proximal, n_non_ptm, mean_af per class, n_zero_af_ptm, and the kept values (ptm_site_afs, proximal_afs, non_ptm_afs) population_af.png The kept AF values per class on a log scale with their medians, and the share below 1e-4 per class (--save-plots) Option Default Description --gnomad-ht required Variant Hail Table with an AF field --ptm-ht required Sites table from build --af-field AF AF field name -o, --output required Output directory --flanking-codons 5 Window beyond each end of a codon, in codons --save-plots off Also write the PNG plot

docs.title: Export strata for psroc
docs.text:
hvantk ptm export-strata --annotated-ht data/clinvar_ptm.ht -o strata/

export-strata reads a table from annotate and writes ptm_variants.txt (site and proximal variants) and non_ptm_variants.txt (all others) to -o. Each line is one contig:pos:ref:alt with the contig as stored (for example chr1) and the first alternate allele; there is no header. Pass each list to hvantk psroc with --variants to compare predictor performance between the strata (PS-ROC); the PTM example runs both.

Option Default Description --annotated-ht required Table from annotate -o, --output required Output directory

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
hvantk ptm report \
  -o results/ptm_report.html \
  --landscape-json results/landscape/landscape_summary.json \
  --population-json results/population/population_summary.json

report needs at least one of the two JSON files. The page holds summary cards, a short "Key findings" list generated from the numbers, the landscape plots and per-category enrichment table, the population plot, and a methods paragraph. The plots are redrawn from the JSON, embedded in the page and also written next to it as ptm_landscape_summary.png, ptm_overlap_by_category.png, ptm_distance_distribution.png and ptm_population_af.png. The methods paragraph is fixed text that does not reflect the options you ran; for example, it always states the tool's default flanking width, not the --flanking-codons value a landscape or population run actually used.

Option Default Description -o, --output required HTML file to write --landscape-json none landscape_summary.json from landscape --population-json none population_summary.json from population --title PTM-Variant Analysis Report Page title --description none Paragraph shown under the title

docs.title: Per-stratum mixed models
docs.text:
hvantk ptm test --test lmm \
  --input variants.tsv \
  --stratum-col tissue \
  -o results/tissue_lmm.tsv

test fits one linear mixed model for each value of --stratum-col, typically a tissue or cell type you assigned to each variant. It reads a CSV or TSV, plain, .gz or .bgz (a .csv name is read as CSV, any other as TSV), with one row per variant: the gene (--gene-col), the AF (--af-col), the PTM status as a boolean or 0/1 (--is-ptm-col) and the stratum. No ptm command writes this table. Export it yourself, for example from an annotate output with is_ptm true for site and proximal variants.

Rows missing the gene, AF or PTM status, and rows with an AF of 0 or less, are dropped. The response is log_af = log10(AF + 1e-8), each gene gets a random intercept, and the fit uses statsmodels mixedlm with REML.

  • --test lmm fits log_af ~ is_ptm + (1|gene). A stratum is fitted only with at least 30 PTM variants, 30 non-PTM variants and 10 genes that have both; otherwise its row has empty estimates and a note. beta_ptm is the PTM effect on log10 AF (negative means lower AF at PTM variants), with its standard error se_ptm and Wald p-value p_ptm.
  • --test lmm-binned fits log_af ~ is_ptm * expr_bin + (1|gene) and needs a gene × stratum expression matrix: --expression-pkl, a pickled pandas DataFrame (load only pickles you trust), or --expression-tsv, with genes in the first column and one column per stratum. The pickle wins if you pass both. In each stratum a variant takes its gene's expression there (0 when the gene is absent). Zero-expression variants form the reference bin b0_none; the rest are split into up to four quantile bins of log2(expression + 1), b1_Q1 to b4_Q4, and tied quantiles merge. A stratum is fitted only with at least 100 variants of positive expression and 5 variants in every bin and PTM-status cell, b0_none included. For each bin, beta_<bin> is the PTM effect in that bin (the main effect plus the bin's interaction) and se_<bin> its standard error. p_<bin> is the p-value of the main is_ptm term for b0_none, and of the interaction term, the difference from b0_none, for every other bin. A stratum missing from the matrix gets a row with a note.

The output TSV has one row per stratum:

  • lmm: stratum, n_variants, n_ptm, n_nonptm, n_genes, n_mixed_genes, beta_ptm, se_ptm, p_ptm, converged, note.
  • lmm-binned: stratum, n_variants, n_genes, bin_levels, converged, note, then beta_<bin>, se_<bin> and p_<bin> for each bin fitted.

The p-values are not adjusted for the number of strata. For the rank-based stratified analysis with plots and a report, see PTM constraint.

Option Default Description --test required lmm or lmm-binned --input required Variant table (CSV or TSV) --stratum-col required Column with each variant's stratum -o, --output required TSV to write --gene-col gene Gene column --af-col af_filled AF column --is-ptm-col is_ptm PTM-status column --expression-pkl none lmm-binned: pickled gene × stratum DataFrame --expression-tsv none lmm-binned: gene × stratum TSV

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
import hail as hl

from hvantk.algorithms.ptm import (
    PTMBuildConfig,
    annotate_variants_with_ptm,
    export_ptm_strata,
    generate_report,
    ptm_landscape,
    ptm_population,
)
from hvantk.skills.clinvar.shared.constants import (
    CLINVAR_BENIGN_LABELS,
    CLINVAR_PATHOGENIC_LABELS,
)
from hvantk.tools.ptm.pipeline import ptm_build_pipeline

# What `hvantk ptm build` runs. hvantk.algorithms.ptm.ptm_build_pipeline_core is the
# mapping step alone: it needs config.ptm_tsv and writes no Hail Table.
build = ptm_build_pipeline(
    PTMBuildConfig(output_dir="data/ptm/", output_ht="data/ptm/ptm_sites.ht")
)
print(build.source_counts, f"{build.n_mapped}/{build.n_total} sites mapped")

ptm = hl.read_table(build.output_ht)
clinvar = hl.read_table("data/clinvar.ht")

annotated = annotate_variants_with_ptm(clinvar, ptm, flanking_codons=5)
annotated = annotated.checkpoint("data/clinvar_ptm.ht")
strata = export_ptm_strata(annotated, "strata/")  # {"ptm": path, "non_ptm": path}

# landscape and population classify their input table themselves.
landscape = ptm_landscape(
    clinvar,
    ptm,
    "results/landscape/",
    pathogenic_labels=CLINVAR_PATHOGENIC_LABELS,  # both label sets are required
    benign_labels=CLINVAR_BENIGN_LABELS,
)
population = ptm_population(
    hl.read_table("data/gnomad_sites.ht"), ptm, "results/population/", af_field="AF"
)
print(landscape.summary())
print(population.summary())

generate_report(
    "results/ptm_report.html",
    landscape_result=landscape,
    population_result=population,
)

For variant tables in pandas, annotate_variants_by_symbol(variants_df, ptm_df) adds is_ptm_site and is_ptm_proximal by matching gene symbol and chromosome against a mapped TSV from build read into pandas (SYMBOL, chrom and pos columns by default). Its rules differ from annotate: a site variant lies anywhere from codon_start to codon_end, a proximal variant lies within proximal_bp (default 21) bases of that interval, and is_ptm_proximal is also true for site variants.

  • PTM example: a run from the sites table to the report

  • Data sources: the UniProt, PeptideAtlas and CPTAC downloads, and hvantk reprocess uniprot-ptm:sites

docs.title: QTL cascade
docs.text:
hvantk qtlcascade asks whether a variant that changes a gene's mRNA level (an eQTL) also changes the level of its protein (a pQTL), in the same direction, and whether the two signals share one causal variant. It joins eQTL and pQTL summary statistics by variant and gene, classifies each variant-gene pair, colocalises the two signals gene by gene with approximate Bayes factors (ABF), and summarises the evidence per gene, optionally with gnomAD constraint and a disease-gene list. A separate command, gwas-coloc, colocalises one GWAS locus with cis-eQTLs to rank candidate effector genes and checks the top gene with SuSiE fine-mapping.

For a run on one tissue from raw files to report, see the walkthrough.

Figure 1. The eQTL × pQTL pipeline run by hvantk qtlcascade run. gwas-coloc is a separate command.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does Needs run Full pipeline: cascade join, colocalisation (optional), gene summary, plots, HTML report; one or several tissues Hail cascade Join and classify only; writes the cascade table Hail coloc ABF colocalisation for a list of genes; writes a TSV Hail report Rebuilds the HTML report from existing TSVs and PNGs No Hail gwas-coloc Colocalises a FinnGen GWAS locus with eQTL Catalogue cis-eQTLs, then confirms with SuSiE Network access, no Hail

There is no gene-summary command: run writes the summary, or call build_cascade_gene_summary from Python.

docs.title: eQTL and pQTL tables
docs.text:
The cascade reads two Hail Tables keyed by (locus, alleles, gene_id) with the fields beta, se and p_value, plus tissue when you filter by tissue. Two plugins build them with hvantk reprocess (Building datasets; where to get the files: Data sources):

Dataset Raw files Plugin arguments that matter here gtex-eqtl:eqtls GTEx v11 parquet (source=gtex_v11, the default) or v8 TSV (source=gtex_v8) tissue=<name>; p_threshold, default 5e-8, 0 keeps every pair pqtl:metrics Fang et al. (2025) cis-pQTL all-pairs files, <Tissue>.allpairs_nobsGE72.txt.gz tissue=<name>; hgnc_ht=<hgnc.ht> (required); p_threshold, default none, so every pair is kept

Both datasets are bring-your-own: put the files in --raw-dir and reprocess skips the download stage. The walkthrough shows the build commands.

For the join to work:

  • Gene IDs: both sides need unversioned Ensembl IDs. The eQTL builder strips the version. The pQTL builder maps the Fang gene symbols to Ensembl IDs through an hgnc:lookup table given as --plugin-arg hgnc_ht=...; a symbol it cannot map keeps the symbol as gene_id and never joins (the build log counts them).
  • Alleles: both builders read alleles as [ref, alt] from GTEx-style variant IDs (chr1_1000050_C_T_b38), and both effect sizes are per ALT allele, so an exact (locus, alleles) match keeps effect directions comparable. Nothing flips alleles or strands: a variant coded the other way round in one table does not join.
  • Genome build: both tables must be GRCh38. The eqtlgen source of gtex-eqtl:eqtls is GRCh37 and has no beta or se, so it cannot be used here.
  • Tissue names: the tissue filter is an exact string match on both tables, and the builders take the tissue from the raw file name before the first dot. GTEx names sub-tissues (Heart_Left_Ventricle, Colon_Transverse, ...) while Fang uses Colon, Heart, Liver, Lung and Thyroid; only Liver, Lung and Thyroid match as they are. For the others, build one table per tissue and run without a tissue filter, or give the GTEx file (or a symlink to it) the Fang name.

docs.title: All-pairs tables for colocalisation
docs.text: Colocalisation needs every tested variant-gene pair in the window, not only the significant ones. Build the eQTL table with --plugin-arg p_threshold=0 from GTEx all-pairs files (GTEx distributes them separately from the significant pairs) and the pQTL table without p_threshold (the Fang files already hold every pair). Because cascade applies --eqtl-p and --pqtl-p itself, the same two tables can also be the cascade inputs. A significant-pairs table does not fail, but coloc then sees only the variants that passed the threshold, which hides evidence for distinct causal variants (H3) and overstates H4.

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text:
• --constraint-ht: a table keyed by gene_id (Ensembl) with an oe_lof_upper (LOEUF) field, such as the default gnomad-metrics:metrics build (gnomAD v2.1.1, by gene). The v4.0 build is keyed by transcript and has no oe_lof_upper, so it does not work here.
  • --disease-genes-ht: any table keyed by one gene_id field of Ensembl IDs; a gene gets is_disease_gene = true when its ID is a key of that table. The ClinGen and GenCC tables that hvantk builds have compound keys that start with hgnc_id and mondo_id, and stop the run with a key type mismatch. Re-key one through the HGNC table first (ClinGen shown):
import hail as hl

clingen = hl.read_table("data/clingen.ht")  # keyed by (hgnc_id, mondo_id); hgnc_id like "1100"
hgnc = hl.read_table("data/hgnc.ht")  # keyed by hgnc_id like "HGNC:1100"

genes = clingen.key_by()
genes = genes.select(gene_id=hgnc["HGNC:" + genes.hgnc_id].ensembl_gene_id)
genes = genes.filter(hl.is_defined(genes.gene_id)).key_by("gene_id").distinct()
genes.write("data/clingen_genes.ht")

docs.title: GWAS statistics
docs.text: gwas-coloc does not read a local GWAS table: it streams FinnGen R10 summary statistics for one endpoint (below). The gwas-catalog:associations dataset lists published lead associations without standard errors, so it cannot feed coloc; use it to pick a lead variant.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
With an all-pairs eQTL table and a pQTL table for liver, built as in the walkthrough:

hvantk qtlcascade run \
  --eqtl-ht data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht \
  --pqtl-ht data/pqtl_liver.ht \
  --eqtl-allpairs data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht \
  --pqtl-allpairs data/pqtl_liver.ht \
  --constraint-ht data/gnomad_metrics.ht \
  --tissues Liver \
  -o results/qtl_liver

This keeps the pairs with p ≤ 5e-8 on each side, classifies them, colocalises every gene that has an eQTL and a pQTL at the same variant, and writes:

results/qtl_liver/
├── per_tissue/
│   └── Liver/                     # "all" when --tissues is not given
│       ├── cascade.ht/            # variant-gene pairs with their class
│       ├── gene_summary.ht/       # one row per gene
│       ├── gene_summary.tsv       # the same table as TSV
│       └── coloc_results.tsv      # H0-H4 per gene, when coloc ran
├── plots/
│   ├── Liver_cascade_classes.png
│   ├── Liver_coloc_posteriors.png
│   └── cross_tissue_heatmap.png   # with two or more tissues
└── qtlcascade_report.html

Tissue names keep their case in paths; characters other than letters, digits, _ and - become _.

docs.title: Cascade join (cascade)
docs.text:
1. If --tissue is given, keep only the rows of that tissue in each table (a table without a tissue field is not filtered).
  2. Keep eQTL rows with p_value <= --eqtl-p and pQTL rows with p_value <= --pqtl-p. A threshold of 0 keeps every row.
  3. Outer-join the two tables on (locus, alleles, gene_id).

  4. Classify each pair:

    cascade_class Rule eqtl_mediated eQTL and pQTL, eqtl_beta * pqtl_beta > 0 (same direction) discordant eQTL and pQTL, eqtl_beta * pqtl_beta <= 0 eqtl_only eQTL, and no pQTL row for this variant and gene after filtering pqtl_only pQTL, and no eQTL row for this variant and gene after filtering

  5. For eqtl_mediated pairs, compute attenuation_ratio = 1 - |pqtl_beta| / |eqtl_beta| (missing for the other classes): 0 when both effects have the same size, towards 1 when the protein effect is smaller, negative when it is larger.

Joining on gene_id as well as the variant stops an eQTL for one gene and a pQTL for another gene at the same variant from being paired. It does not show that the eQTL and the pQTL share a causal variant; coloc tests that. Without a tissue filter, input tables that hold several tissues pair rows across tissues (a warning is logged).

Option Default Description --eqtl-ht required eQTL Hail Table --pqtl-ht required pQTL Hail Table -o, --output required Output cascade table (.ht) --tissue none Keep only this tissue in both tables --eqtl-p 5e-8 eQTL p-value threshold (0 keeps every row) --pqtl-p 5e-8 pQTL p-value threshold (0 keeps every row) --overwrite off Replace an existing output table 
hvantk qtlcascade cascade \
  --eqtl-ht data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht \
  --pqtl-ht data/pqtl_liver.ht \
  --tissue Liver \
  -o results/cascade_liver.ht

The cascade table is keyed by (locus, alleles, gene_id):

Field Type Description eqtl_beta, eqtl_se, eqtl_pvalue float64 eQTL statistics (missing for pqtl_only) pqtl_beta, pqtl_se, pqtl_pvalue float64 pQTL statistics (missing for eqtl_only) cascade_class str Class, as above attenuation_ratio float64 eqtl_mediated pairs only tissue str The --tissue value; missing without it

docs.title: Colocalisation (coloc)
docs.text:
For each requested gene, coloc tests whether the eQTL and the pQTL share one causal variant:

  1. Read both all-pairs tables, keep the requested genes (and --tissue), and inner-join them on (locus, alleles, gene_id): only variants present in both tables are used.
  2. Take the lead eQTL variant, the shared variant with the smallest eQTL p-value, and keep the shared variants within --window-kb of it (default ±500 kb).
  3. Skip the gene, leaving it out of the output, if fewer than 2 variants remain.
  4. Compute a log ABF per variant and trait from beta and se (Wakefield 2009), then the posterior of each hypothesis (Giambartolomei et al. 2014, the algebra of the R coloc package's coloc.abf). Sums run over the variants in the window; the code works in log space.
per variant:  z = beta / se,   r = W / (W + se^2),   log ABF = 0.5 * (log(1 - r) + r * z^2)

H0  no association                     L0 = 1
H1  eQTL only                          L1 = p1  * sum(ABF_eqtl)
H2  pQTL only                          L2 = p2  * sum(ABF_pqtl)
H3  both, distinct causal variants     L3 = p1 * p2 * (sum(ABF_eqtl) * sum(ABF_pqtl) - sum(ABF_eqtl * ABF_pqtl))
H4  both, one shared causal variant    L4 = p12 * sum(ABF_eqtl * ABF_pqtl)

PP.Hk = Lk / (L0 + L1 + L2 + L3 + L4)
Parameter Default Meaning p1 1e-4 Prior that a variant is causal for the eQTL only p2 1e-4 Prior that a variant is causal for the pQTL only p12 1e-5 Prior that a variant is causal for both W 0.04 Prior variance of the true effect (prior SD 0.2), the same for both traits Window ±500 kb Around the lead eQTL variant Colocalised H4 > 0.8 Label used by the gene summary, the run printout, the report and the plots

The CLI sets only the window and the tissue. Change the priors and W through CascadeConfig (coloc_p1, coloc_p2, coloc_p12, coloc_W) or run_coloc_per_gene. The 0.8 cut-off is fixed and only labels results: every tested gene is written.

Compared with the R coloc package, this implementation:

  • uses beta and se only: there is no p-value and MAF route, no sample size, no sdY estimate and no case fraction. R coloc's default prior for a quantitative trait with unit SD is W = 0.0225 (SD 0.15), which gwas-coloc uses for its eQTL side; the cascade uses 0.04 for both traits.
  • assumes at most one causal variant per trait in the window. With several independent signals, a shared one can be missed or reported as H3; only gwas-coloc adds SuSiE fine-mapping.
  • needs no allele alignment for the posteriors, which depend on z² only; variants coded differently in the two tables are not joined and drop out.

H4 ignores the direction of effect, so a discordant gene can colocalise. Coloc collects every shared variant of every requested gene to the driver before applying the window, so memory follows the size of the all-pairs tables, not --window-kb.

run tests every gene with at least one eqtl_mediated or discordant pair. For the CLI, list the genes in a text file, one gene_id per line.

Option Default Description --eqtl-allpairs required All-pairs eQTL table --pqtl-allpairs required All-pairs pQTL table --cascade-genes required Text file, one gene_id per line --tissue none Keep only this tissue; also the output tissue value (unknown without it) --window-kb 500 Half-width of the window around the lead eQTL variant, in kb -o, --output required Output TSV

The TSV has one row per tested gene: gene_id, tissue, H0 to H4, and n_variants (shared variants in the window). It is written even when no gene could be tested (header only).

docs.title: Gene summary
docs.text:
run aggregates the cascade table per gene into gene_summary.ht and gene_summary.tsv:

Column Description gene_id Ensembl gene ID (key) n_eqtl_variants, n_pqtl_variants Variants with an eQTL, and with a pQTL, for the gene n_concordant, n_discordant eqtl_mediated and discordant pairs best_eqtl_pvalue, best_pqtl_pvalue Smallest p-value on each side tissues Tissue labels of the gene's pairs has_complete_cascade n_concordant > 0 oe_lof_upper LOEUF, with --constraint-ht is_disease_gene With --disease-genes-ht coloc_max_h4 Highest H4 among the gene's coloc rows, when coloc ran coloc_n_tissues Number of those rows with H4 > 0.8

run passes one tissue's coloc results at a time, so there coloc_max_h4 is that tissue's H4 and coloc_n_tissues is 0 or 1; pass results for several tissues to build_cascade_gene_summary to count across tissues. Genes that coloc did not test have missing coloc columns.

docs.title: Full pipeline (run)
docs.text:
run executes the stages in order: build the cascade, colocalise (only when both all-pairs tables are given), build the gene summary, then write the plots and the report.

Option Default Description --eqtl-ht, --pqtl-ht required Cascade inputs --eqtl-allpairs, --pqtl-allpairs none All-pairs tables: give both to run coloc, or neither --constraint-ht none LOEUF overlay --disease-genes-ht none Disease-gene overlay --tissues none Comma-separated tissues, one pass each -o, --output-dir required Output directory --eqtl-p, --pqtl-p 5e-8 Thresholds, as in cascade --window-kb 500 Coloc window, as in coloc --no-plots off Skip the PNGs --no-report off Skip the HTML report --overwrite off Replace existing Hail tables --dry-run off Print the plan and exit
  • Without --tissues, run makes one pass with no tissue filter, writes under per_tissue/all/, and prints the number of genes in the summary and the class counts.
  • With --tissues A,B, it runs the tissues one at a time in alphabetical order and prints <tissue>: <n> genes, <m> colocalised for each, where m counts H4 > 0.8. A tissue that fails is skipped (the command fails only if all do). It draws cross_tissue_heatmap.png (class counts per tissue) when at least two tissues finish, and writes one combined report.
  • --dry-run prints the tissues, the inputs, whether coloc will run and the stages, without reading any table or writing anything to -o.
  • Plots need matplotlib (pip install 'hvantk[viz]'); without it, run logs a warning for each plot and carries on.
  • --overwrite replaces the Hail tables. A rerun in which no gene has both an eQTL and a pQTL still writes an empty (header-only) coloc_results.tsv, replacing any file from an earlier run at that path.

docs.title: Report (report)
docs.text:
report rebuilds the self-contained HTML report from files that run wrote: an overview, the top 50 genes by n_concordant, a coloc summary (genes tested, number and share with H4 > 0.8, median H4), every PNG in --plots-dir, and a fixed methods paragraph. It reads no Hail tables, so its overview has no class counts; the report that run writes has them. The footer carries a timestamp, so compare the TSVs, not report files, when checking a rerun.

Option Default Description --gene-summary none gene_summary.tsv --coloc-results none coloc_results.tsv --plots-dir none Directory whose *.png files are embedded -o, --output required Output HTML file --title QTL Cascade Analysis Report Page title 
hvantk qtlcascade report \
  --gene-summary results/qtl_liver/per_tissue/Liver/gene_summary.tsv \
  --coloc-results results/qtl_liver/per_tissue/Liver/coloc_results.tsv \
  --plots-dir results/qtl_liver/plots \
  -o results/liver_report.html

docs.title: GWAS colocalisation (gwas-coloc)
docs.text: gwas-coloc asks which cis gene at a GWAS locus is the likely effector. It colocalises the GWAS signal with the cis-eQTL of every gene in a window, ranks the genes by PP4, and confirms the top gene (or --gene) with SuSiE fine-mapping. It is independent of the eQTL × pQTL cascade and does not use Hail.

docs.title: What it downloads
docs.text:
Every run needs network access:

  • FinnGen R10 summary statistics for --endpoint over the window, by remote tabix from the public FinnGen bucket on storage.googleapis.com.
  • eQTL Catalogue all-variant statistics for --eqtl (a dataset ID such as QTD000251, in study --eqtl-study, default QTS000015, GTEx), by remote tabix from ftp.ebi.ac.uk. --eqtl also accepts a URL, or a local bgzipped, tabix-indexed file in the same column layout.
  • For fine-mapping, the 1000 Genomes high-coverage GRCh38 phased panel from ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk. The sample list and the chromosome's tabix index are downloaded once into the LD cache (--ld-cache-dir, else $HVANTK_LD_CACHE, else ~/.cache/hvantk/1kg); the genotypes of the window are streamed on every run. --ld-vcf replaces the panel with a local VCF (all its samples are used); the GWAS and eQTL statistics are still streamed.

pysam saves a copy of each remote tabix index (.tbi) in the current directory, so run gwas-coloc from a scratch directory. Everything it needs (pysam, NumPy, requests) is in the base install.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Window: --lead ± --window-kb (default 500 kb) on --chrom (GRCh38, no chr prefix).
  2. Match GWAS and eQTL variants by position and allele pair, in either order. No effect flip is needed, because the ABF uses z².
  3. ABF screen: for each gene with at least 20 matched variants, compute PP3 and PP4 with the coloc formulas but one prior variance per trait: W1 = 0.04 for the GWAS (case-control log odds ratio, prior SD 0.2) and W2 = 0.0225 for the eQTL (prior SD 0.15 on a unit-variance trait), with p1 = p2 = 1e-4 and p12 = 1e-5. Genes are ranked by PP4.
  4. Target gene: --gene if given (the verdict then uses that gene's PP4, wherever it ranks), otherwise the top-ranked gene.
  5. Fine-mapping (on by default): keep the variants present in the GWAS, in the target gene's eQTL and in the LD panel as biallelic SNPs, orient them to the GWAS ALT allele, and compute LD as the correlation of ALT dosages among unrelated founders of --superpop (EUR, AFR, EAS, SAS or AMR). SuSiE-RSS (up to 10 effects, 95% credible sets, minimum |r| of 0.5 within a set) fine-maps each trait from z = beta / se and its sample size (--gwas-n, --eqtl-n). coloc.susie then takes the highest PP4 over all pairs of GWAS and eQTL credible sets (p1 = p2 = 1e-4, p12 = 5e-6), or 0 when either trait has no credible set. Both are NumPy ports of susieR and the coloc package; R is not needed.

  6. Verdict, with one cut-off of 0.5 for both the ABF PP4 and the coloc.susie PP4:

    Verdict When CONFIRMED ABF PP4 ≥ 0.5 and coloc.susie PP4 ≥ 0.5 REFUTED ABF PP4 ≥ 0.5 but coloc.susie PP4 < 0.5: a trait has no credible set (a single-variant-ABF artifact), or the credible sets point to distinct causal variants SUGGESTIVE ABF PP4 ≥ 0.5, and fine-mapping was not run (--no-fine-map) or the LD reference could not be built INCONCLUSIVE Fine-mapping ran but gave no PP4 (fewer than 2 usable variants, or a SuSiE error) NO COLOC No gene tested, --gene not among the tested genes, or its ABF PP4 < 0.5

The printed verdict adds the reason in parentheses. The cut-off is 0.5, not the 0.8 used for the cascade, because coloc.susie is more conservative than single-variant ABF; change it with GwasColocConfig(pp4_threshold=...) from Python. A network failure fetching the LD reference leaves no LD reference: an ABF hit is then reported as SUGGESTIVE and the command does not fail. --superpop is restricted to the five 1000 Genomes super-populations, so a typo there fails at once instead of silently falling back this way. LD comes from a reference panel, not from the GWAS or eQTL samples; for weak eQTLs the credible sets can then be unreliable, the documented limitation of SuSiE-RSS.

docs.title: Options and outputs
docs.text:
Option Default Description --endpoint required FinnGen R10 endpoint code, such as I9_AF --chrom required Chromosome, GRCh38, without chr --lead required Lead variant position (GRCh38) --eqtl required eQTL Catalogue dataset ID, URL or local tabix file --eqtl-study QTS000015 eQTL Catalogue study ID --window-kb 500 Half-width of the window around the lead, in kb --gene top ABF gene Ensembl gene ID to confirm --fine-map / --no-fine-map --fine-map Run the SuSiE confirmation --gwas-n, --eqtl-n none Sample sizes; required unless --no-fine-map --superpop EUR 1000 Genomes super-population for LD: EUR, AFR, EAS, SAS or AMR --ld-cache-dir $HVANTK_LD_CACHE, else ~/.cache/hvantk/1kg Cache for the panel's sample list and indexes --ld-vcf none Local VCF to use as the LD reference -o, --output-dir required Output directory

Without --gwas-n and --eqtl-n, the default --fine-map stops before any download with fine-mapping requires gwas_N and eqtl_N (or pass --no-fine-map).

hvantk qtlcascade gwas-coloc \
  --endpoint I9_AF --chrom 10 --lead 73600000 \
  --eqtl QTD000251 \
  --gwas-n 261395 --eqtl-n 372 \
  -o results/af_10q22

It writes two files to --output-dir:

  • coloc_<endpoint>_<chrom>_<lead>.tsv: one row per tested gene, sorted by PP4, with gene_id, gene (the ID again unless symbols are passed from Python), n_snp, eqtl_min_p, PP3 and PP4.
  • report_<endpoint>_<chrom>_<lead>.json: region and genome build, sources and sample sizes, coloc_params, results (genes tested, top gene and its PP4, gene of interest and its PP4), fine_map (credible sets per trait, coloc_susie_PP4, LD panel, note; null with --no-fine-map), verdict, run date and provenance notes.

The walkthrough runs a confirmed and a refuted locus.

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text:
• Classes depend on the thresholds and on what each study measured. eqtl_only means that no pQTL for that variant and gene passed --pqtl-p: the protein effect may be small, the variant untested, or the protein not measured in the pQTL study.
  • eqtl_mediated records a same-direction effect of one variant on both layers. The class names follow Fang et al. (2025); none of them is a mediation test.
  • High H4 means that the eQTL and the pQTL share a causal variant in the window. High H3 means distinct causal variants, so a cascade seen at a shared variant is an LD artifact. High H1 or H2 means that only one trait has a signal in the window.
  • eqtl_beta and pqtl_beta come from different studies, each on its own scale; compare attenuation ratios between genes rather than reading one value on its own.
  • For gwas-coloc, trust CONFIRMED and REFUTED over the ABF ranking: a strong GWAS signal next to a weak eQTL can give a high single-variant PP4 that fine-mapping does not support.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: The code lives in hvantk/algorithms/qtlcascade/; the CLI is hvantk/tools/qtl/qtlcascade_cli.py.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade import CascadeConfig, CascadePipeline

config = CascadeConfig(
    eqtl_ht="data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht",
    pqtl_ht="data/pqtl_liver.ht",
    eqtl_allpairs_ht="data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht",
    pqtl_allpairs_ht="data/pqtl_liver.ht",
    constraint_ht="data/gnomad_metrics.ht",
    output_dir="results/qtl_liver",
)
pipeline = CascadePipeline(config)  # validates the config; creates no directories yet
result = pipeline.run(tissue="Liver")
print(result.class_counts, result.n_cascade_genes)
if result.coloc_df is not None:
    print((result.coloc_df["H4"] > 0.8).sum(), "genes with H4 > 0.8")

CascadeConfig fields map to the run options, plus the coloc priors that the CLI does not expose:

Field Default CLI option eqtl_ht, pqtl_ht, output_dir required --eqtl-ht, --pqtl-ht, -o eqtl_allpairs_ht, pqtl_allpairs_ht "" --eqtl-allpairs, --pqtl-allpairs constraint_ht, disease_genes_ht "" --constraint-ht, --disease-genes-ht tissues [] --tissues eqtl_p_threshold, pqtl_p_threshold 5e-8 --eqtl-p, --pqtl-p coloc_window_kb 500 --window-kb coloc_p1, coloc_p2, coloc_p12, coloc_W 1e-4, 1e-4, 1e-5, 0.04 none generate_plots, generate_report True --no-plots, --no-report overwrite False --overwrite

CascadePipeline(config) raises ValueError for an invalid configuration (config.validate() lists the problems) but creates no directories; run() and run_collection() create output_dir, per_tissue/ and (unless generate_plots is False) plots/ when they actually execute, so show_plan() writes nothing. run(tissue=None) returns a CascadeResult with tissue, cascade_ht_path, gene_summary_ht_path, class_counts, n_cascade_genes (genes in the summary) and coloc_df. run_collection() runs every tissue in config.tissues and returns {tissue: CascadeResult}; show_plan() returns the --dry-run text.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade import (
    build_cascade,
    build_cascade_gene_summary,
    run_coloc_per_gene,
)
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade.pipeline import coloc_gene_ids
from hvantk.core.utils.hail_context import init_hail

init_hail()
cascade = build_cascade(
    eqtl_ht_path="data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht",
    pqtl_ht_path="data/pqtl_liver.ht",
    output_path="results/cascade.ht",
    tissue="Liver",
)
coloc_df = run_coloc_per_gene(
    eqtl_allpairs_ht_path="data/eqtl_liver_allpairs.ht",
    pqtl_allpairs_ht_path="data/pqtl_liver.ht",
    cascade_genes=coloc_gene_ids(cascade),  # genes with an eqtl_mediated or discordant pair
    tissue="Liver",
    W=0.04,
)
genes = build_cascade_gene_summary(
    cascade_ht_path="results/cascade.ht",
    output_path="results/gene_summary.ht",
    constraint_ht_path="data/gnomad_metrics.ht",
    coloc_df=coloc_df,
)

build_cascade and build_cascade_gene_summary return the checkpointed Hail Tables. run_coloc_per_gene returns a pandas DataFrame with the coloc TSV columns and also takes window_kb, p1, p2 and p12.

The ABF itself runs on NumPy arrays, without Hail:

import numpy as np
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade import coloc_abf

res = coloc_abf(
    eqtl_beta=np.array([0.5, 0.3, -0.1]),
    eqtl_se=np.array([0.1, 0.1, 0.05]),
    pqtl_beta=np.array([0.4, 0.2, -0.05]),
    pqtl_se=np.array([0.1, 0.1, 0.05]),
)
print(round(res["H4"], 2))  # 0.93

coloc_abf returns a dict with H0 to H4, n_variants and lead_snp_h4_idx (the variant with the largest joint ABF); compute_log_abf(beta, se, W) returns the per-variant log ABFs.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
run draws the class bar chart, the H4 histogram and the cross-tissue heatmap (plot_cascade_classes, plot_coloc_posteriors, plot_cross_tissue_heatmap). Two more plots take a DataFrame of variant-gene pairs:

import hail as hl
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade import plot_attenuation, plot_loeuf_by_cascade_class

pairs = hl.read_table("results/qtl_liver/per_tissue/Liver/cascade.ht")
genes = hl.read_table("results/qtl_liver/per_tissue/Liver/gene_summary.ht")
# oe_lof_upper is in the gene summary only when --constraint-ht was given
pairs = pairs.annotate(oe_lof_upper=genes[pairs.gene_id].oe_lof_upper)
df = (
    pairs.key_by()
    .select("eqtl_beta", "pqtl_beta", "cascade_class", "oe_lof_upper")
    .to_pandas()
)

plot_attenuation(df, output_path="results/attenuation.png")  # eQTL beta against pQTL beta
plot_loeuf_by_cascade_class(df, output_path="results/loeuf_by_class.png")

Each plot function returns a matplotlib figure, saves it when output_path is given, and needs the viz extra.

docs.title: GWAS colocalisation from Python
docs.text:
from hvantk.algorithms.qtlcascade.gwas_pipeline import (
    GwasColocConfig,
    run_gwas_coloc_pipeline,
)

config = GwasColocConfig(
    endpoint="I9_AF",
    chrom="10",
    lead=73600000,
    eqtl_dataset="QTD000251",
    output_dir="results/af_10q22",
    gene_of_interest="ENSG00000177791",
    gwas_N=261395,
    eqtl_N=372,
    gene_symbols={"ENSG00000177791": "MYOZ1"},  # fills the `gene` column
)
report = run_gwas_coloc_pipeline(config)  # the JSON report, as a dict; raises ValueError
# for an invalid config (same problems config.validate() lists) before anything runs
print(report["verdict"], report["results"]["goi_PP4_abf"])

GwasColocConfig also takes min_snps (20), W1 (0.04), W2 (0.0225), p1, p2, p12 and pp4_threshold (0.5).
